On behalf of @atlas-axis , we are submitting the Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle proposal below. This proposal includes the following edit: Codify Deflationary Tokenomics - Sets forth the core deflationary tokenomics of the SKY token. Codify Deflationary Tokenomics Add new documents as subdocuments of A.4.1.2 - SKY (Portal) / A.4.1 - Core Tokens - SKY (Github) . The documents should be located directly after A.4.1.2.1 - MKR To SKY Upgrade (Portal) / A.4.1 - Core Tokens - SKY - MKR To SKY Upgrade (Github) to read as follows: A.4.1 - Core Tokens - SKY - Deflationary Tokenomics (Core) - The documents herein set forth the core deflationary tokenomics of the SKY token. A.4.1 - Core Tokens - SKY - Initial Token Supply (Core) - The initial token supply of SKY tokens is derived from the total number of legacy MKR tokens as of the launch of Sky, multiplied by the conversion ratio of 24,000. SKY is the exclusive governance token of the Sky Protocol and takes over all governance and economic rights previously held by MKR. See A.4.1 - Core Tokens - SKY - MKR To SKY Upgrade Approval . A.4.1 - Core Tokens - SKY - No New Token Emissions (Core) - No new SKY tokens may be emitted except for (1) emissions required to recapitalize the protocol if it is at risk of insolvency (see A.3.7 ) and (2) temporary emissions that are being deprecated and fully offset by corresponding burns, resulting in no net increase to the intended long-term token supply (see A.4.1 - Core Tokens - SKY - Deprecated Emissions Mechanisms). A.4.1 - Core Tokens - SKY - Burning Of Existing Tokens (Core) - At the same time that no new SKY tokens are issued, SKY tokens are bought back and burned on a regular basis, using a portion of the Net Revenue of the Protocol as dictated by the Treasury Management Function. See A.2.5 - Treasury Management - Treasury Management - Allocation Steps - Step 4: Smart Burn And Standard Activity Staking Rewards - Smart Burn Buffer . As a result, the total supply of SKY tokens will continue to decrease over time. A.4.1 - Core Tokens - SKY - Deprecated Emissions Mechanisms (Core) - The subdocuments herein define legacy mechanisms involving the issuance of new SKY tokens. Each of these mechanisms is being deprecated. While these mechanisms do not increase the net supply of SKY tokens, they must be replaced with solutions that do not involve any emissions of SKY tokens, as defined in the documents herein. A.4.1 - Core Tokens - SKY - SKY Token Rewards Emissions (Core) - USDS users are able to earn SKY Rewards. See A.4.3 - A2 - Savings Rate And Token Reward Mechanism - Token Reward Mechanism . These rewards are currently funded by emissions of new SKY tokens. These ongoing emissions will be eliminated and replaced with a solution that funds these rewards using SKY held by the Sky Protocol. At the same time that this new solution is implemented, SKY tokens equal to the total SKY emissions previously used to fund SKY Rewards, including the Early Bird Reward (see A.5.5 - Accessibility Campaigns - Early Bird Reward - Token Distribution ), will be burned from SKY held by the Sky Protocol. The combination of these actions will achieve a state where the number of total SKY tokens is exactly the same as if SKY Rewards had never been funded with protocol emissions. A.4.1 - Core Tokens - SKY - MKR To SKY Conversion Emissions (Core) - The legacy MKR to SKY conversion contract (Legacy Conversion Contract) burns MKR and mints new SKY. The new MKR to SKY conversion contract (New Conversion Contract) instead burns MKR and issues SKY from the existing supply of preminted SKY. The Legacy Conversion Contract will be disabled as soon as practicable. To offset SKY minted by the Legacy Conversion Contract after the deployment of the New Conversion Contract, an equivalent amount of preminted SKY will be burned. This action will ensure the total SKY token supply remains as if these specific emissions from the Legacy Conversion Contract had not occurred.

On behalf of @atlas-axis , we are submitting the following proposal to prepare for the launch of the SPK token. This proposal contains the following edits: Build Out Allocation System Primitive - Builds out the Allocation System Primitive, including the process for Star Agents to comply with the risk framework. Add Spark - Launch Agent 1 Ecosystem Accord - Adds an Ecosystem Accord between Spark and Launch Agent 1. Add Sky - Spark / Launch Agent 1 Ecosystem Accord - Adds an Ecosystem Accord between Sky, Spark, and Launch Agent 1. Add Logic Regarding Key Interest Rates - Adds logic regarding how the Base Rate is set and how it relates to the Agent Credit Line Borrow Rate. Update Risk Framework - Updates the risk framework to include a new model for lending markets and models for Smart Contract Risk and Administrative Risk. Rename First Loss Capital To Junior Risk Capital - Renames First Loss Capital to Junior Risk Capital to better align with other terminology in the Atlas. Update Logic Regarding Distribution Of Agent Tokens - Clarifies the distribution of Agent Tokens received by Sky under an Ecosystem Accord. Update Spark Liquidity Layer Documentation - Updates the documentation of the Spark Liquidity Layer to reflect that it is an implementation of the Allocation System Primitive. Update Spark Artifact Based On Ecosystem Accords - Updates Spark Artifact to reflect the Ecosystem Accords entered into by Spark. Update Launch Agent 1 Artifact Based On Ecosystem Accords - Updates the Launch Agent 1 Artifact to reflect the Ecosystem Accords entered into by Launch Agent 1. Given the size of the proposal, we are following the same approach that we used for the Agent Launch. First, we have published the proposal to a public Notion page: [Public] Atlas Edit Weekly Proposal For SPK Launch . Second, we have generated an HTML version of the Proposal; this allows us to guarantee that the Proposal submitted herein is immutable - it cannot be altered. We have attached the HTML file to the Notion page linked above. Simply click on the file, and your browser will download it. Please note: due to a Notion bug, internal references in the Proposal are not displayed correctly in the HTML file. To see the internal references and get the best experience, we would recommend that community members review the Notion page. Using the process below, community members can independently verify the contents of the Proposal submitted herein: Download the HTML file from the Notion page Open it in an editor such as VS Code Copy the contents into the hash generator at Keccak-256 - Online Tools Verify that the hash is equal to bedf45dceb0748041815e6a534eba006a83d00aded64c96b0d2ee7ac297f199d

commits.changeSummary: On behalf of @atlas-axis , we are submitting the Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle proposal below. This proposal includes the following edits: Add Timeline For Disabling Legacy Conversion Contract - Specifies when the Legacy Conversion Contract will be disabled. Refine SKY Rewards Rate Normalization Process - Provides the Governance Facilitators with greater flexibility in normalizing the effective yield for SKY Token Rewards. Update Spark Artifact And Ecosystem Accord To Prepare For SPK Launch - Updates Spark’s Agent Artifact and one of its Ecosystem Accords to prepare for the SPK launch. Add Timeline For Disabling Legacy Conversion Contract Replace A.4.1.2.2.4.2 - MKR To SKY Conversion Emissions (Portal) / A.4.1 - Core Tokens - SKY - MKR To SKY Conversion Emissions (Github) to read as follows: A.4.1 - Core Tokens - SKY - MKR To SKY Conversion Emissions (Core) - The legacy MKR to SKY conversion contract (Legacy Conversion Contract) burns MKR and mints new SKY. The new MKR to SKY conversion contract (New Conversion Contract) instead burns MKR and issues SKY from the existing supply of preminted SKY. The Legacy Conversion Contract will be disabled as specified in 4.1 - Core Tokens - SKY - Disabling Legacy Conversion Contract. To offset SKY minted by the Legacy Conversion Contract after the deployment of the New Conversion Contract, an equivalent amount of preminted SKY will be burned. This action will ensure the total SKY token supply remains as if these specific emissions from the Legacy Conversion Contract had not occurred. A.4.1 - Core Tokens - SKY - Disabling Legacy Conversion Contract (Core) - The disabling of the Legacy Conversion Contract will be executed in the June 26, 2025 Executive Vote. This action is authorized to proceed directly to an Executive Vote without a prior Governance Poll. Refine SKY Rewards Rate Normalization Process Replace A.4.3.2.1 - SKY Token Rewards (Portal) / A.4.3 - Savings Rate And Token Reward Mechanism - Token Reward Mechanism - SKY Token Rewards (Github) to read as follows: A.4.3 - Savings Rate And Token Reward Mechanism - Token Reward Mechanism - SKY Token Rewards (Core) - With each Executive Vote, the distribution of SKY token rewards to USDS holders is normalized to ensure the effective yield provided by these rewards equals the Sky Savings Rate (SSR) for the upcoming period. The effective yield is defined as: (Total Market Value of Distributed SKY Tokens / Total Eligible USDS Balance). To achieve this normalization, the quantity of SKY token rewards to be distributed is determined through the following calculation, performed for each normalization period: Determine Target Reward Value: Calculate the total US dollar value required to meet the SSR for the period: (Total Eligible USDS Balance * SSR). Determine SKY Token Quantity: Divide the Target Reward Value (from step 1) by the Current Market Price of SKY (determined at the time of the Executive Vote). The Governance Facilitators, on the recommendation of the Stability Scope Advisors, may maintain the quantity of SKY token rewards to be distributed for a normalization period at its current level if they conclude that: the difference between the effective yield provided by SKY Tokens Rewards and the SSR is not material; the difference between the effective yield provided by SKY Token Rewards and the SSR is unlikely to persist due to other factors; or adjusting the quantity of SKY Token Rewards is otherwise inadvisable. The recommendation of the Stability Scope Advisors must be posted to the Sky Forum and approved by the Stability Facilitators. Update Spark Artifact And Ecosystem Accord To Prepare For SPK Launch Delete A.2.9.1.2.2.2.1.2.2 - Liquidity For Market Makers Stipulation (Portal) / A.2.10 - Liquidity For Market Makers Stipulation (Github) Replace A.2.9.1.2.2.5.4 - Initial Allocation Mechanism (Portal) / A.2.10 - Initial Allocation Mechanism (Github) to read as follows: Initial Allocation Mechanism ( Core ) - Shortly after the Agent Token launch, an Atlas Edit Proposal submitted to Sky Governance will allow the respective founding teams of Spark and Launch Agent 1 to propose an initial cash grant to their respective Star Foundation. Sky Governance must consent to this initial cash grant via approving the Sky Atlas modification. Add new subdocuments of A.AG1.2.1.P1.3.1.1.4 - Custom Instance Parameters (Portal) / Spark - Custom Instance Parameters (Github) to read as follows: Spark Foundation (Core) - The Spark Foundation is the Star Foundation associated with Spark. Its mandate is to support the development, growth, and adoption of Spark. Phoenix Labs (Core) - Phoenix Labs is a development company that provides services to the Spark Foundation. Phoenix Labs is a “Nested Contributor”, i.e., a core contributor to both Spark and Sky. Add new subdocuments of A.AG1.2.1.P4.2.1.1.7 - Custom Instance Parameters (Portal) / Spark - Custom Instance Parameters (Github) to read as follows: Staking (Core) - SPK token holders can stake their tokens. The rewards for staking will be specified in a future iteration of the Spark Artifact. Replace the subdocuments of A.AG1.2.1.P4.2.1.2 - Operational Process Definition (Portal) / Spark - Operational Process Definition (Github) to read as follows: Minting Of Tokens To SPK Company Ltd (Core) - The Genesis Supply was minted to an account owned by SPK Company Ltd. The address of the account on the Ethereum Mainnet is 0x6FE588FDCC6A34207485cc6e47673F59cCEDF92B . Transfer Of Tokens To Sky (Core) - SPK Company Ltd transferred 6.5 billion SPK tokens from the SPK Company Ltd account to the Sky Pause Proxy. The SPK Company Ltd account is specified in Minting Of Tokens To SPK Company Ltd. Transfer Of Tokens To Spark SubProxy Account (Core) - SPK Company Ltd transferred 918,760,451 SPK tokens from the SPK Company Ltd account to the Spark SubProxy Account. The SPK Company Ltd account is specified in Minting Of Tokens To SPK Company Ltd. The Spark SubProxy Account is specified in SubProxy Account . Transfer Of Tokens To Spark Foundation (Core) - SPK Company Ltd will transfer 1 billion SPK tokens from the SPK Company Ltd account to the Spark Foundation. The SPK Company Ltd account is specified in Minting Of Tokens To SPK Company Ltd. The address of the Spark Foundation on the Ethereum Mainnet will be specified in a future iteration of the Spark Artifact. Tokens Retained By SPK Company Ltd ( Core) - 1,581,239,549 SPK tokens will be retained by SPK Company Ltd. The use of these tokens will be specified in a future iteration of the Spark Artifact. Replace the subdocuments of A.AG1.2.2.P6.2.1.2.1 - Routine Protocol (Portal) / Spark - Routine Protocol (Github) to read as follows: Root Edit Proposal Submission (Core) - The Root Edit process begins with a SPK token holder submitting a proposal through the Powerhouse system containing a draft Artifact Edit Proposal. A SPK token holder must hold at least 1% of the total token supply to submit a proposal. The proposal must also be posted on the Sky Forum under the “Spark” tag. Root Edit Proposal Submission Requirements Exception For Nested Contributors (Core) - Nested Contributors are always authorized to submit Artifact Edit Proposals and do not have to fulfill the token-holding requirements defined in Root Edit Proposal Submission. However, all other procedural requirements within the Root Edit process continue to apply. To see the Agent’s Nested Contributors, see Phoenix Labs. Root Edit Proposal Submission Requirements Exception For Spark Foundation (Core) - While it is a core service provider to Spark, the Spark Foundation is authorized to submit Artifact Edit Proposals and does not have to fulfill the token-holding requirements defined in Root Edit Proposal Submission. However, all other procedural requirements within the Root Edit process continue to apply. Short-Term Transitionary Measures (Core) - Until the Powerhouse system supports submitting Artifact Edit Proposals, SPK token holders may submit Artifact Edit Proposals by posting them to the Sky Forum under the “Spark” category. The title of the post must include the text “Spark Artifact Edit Proposal”. The post must include cryptographic proof that the author controls an account holding the required percentage of the total SPK token supply specified in Root Edit Proposal Submission. Root Edit Expert Advisor Review (Core) - A future iteration of the Spark Artifact will specify guidelines for obtaining specialized review of proposals requiring advanced technical or financial analysis. Root Edit Proposal Review By Operational Facilitator (Core) - Within seven (7) days of the proposal being submitted, the Operational Facilitator must review the Root Edit Proposal for alignment. If the proposal is aligned, the Operational Facilitator must respond to the Forum post to announce their finding. In this Forum post, the Operational Facilitator must also confirm that the proposal is feasible for Operational GovOps to operationalize. If the proposal is misaligned, the Operational Facilitator must respond to the Forum post to announce their finding and provide the reasoning for it. Root Edit Token Holder Vote (Core) - Where their review of the proposal results in a finding of alignment with the Sky Core Atlas and Spark Artifact, the Operational Facilitator next triggers a Snapshot poll to allow token holders to vote on the proposal. The poll is open for three (3) days. A poll must have at least 10% of the circulating token supply participating and must have 50% of votes in favor to be approved. Circulating Supply Definition (Core) - For purposes of Root Edit Token Holder Vote, the circulating supply of SPK tokens is equal to the total supply of SPK tokens minus the sum of: Tokens retained by SKY and not yet distributed as token rewards (see A.2.10 - Sky Retained Tokens And Reward Pools ); and Tokens retained in vesting agreements for Spark contributors and not yet distributed; and Tokens in the Spark SubProxy Account (see SubProxy Account ). Root Edit Artifact Update (Core) - At the conclusion of the poll, if the proposal is approved, the Operational Facilitator submits the edit to Powerhouse to formally update the Agent Artifact. Regardless of the outcome, the Operational Facilitator updates the Powerhouse System to include the result of the vote, including any pertinent documents. Short Term Transitionary Measures (Core) - Until the Powerhouse system supports updating Agent Artifacts, the Operational Facilitator works with the Governance Facilitators to update the Atlas GitHub repository located at Pull requests · sky-ecosystem/next-gen-atlas · GitHub to reflect proposals approved by Star Governance. Artifact Edit Restrictions (Core) - The Spark Artifact cannot be edited in any way that violates the Sky Core Atlas or its specifications of the Sky Primitives, or in any way that is otherwise misaligned. The Operational Facilitator must enforce this rule through their review of Artifact Edit Proposals. Time-Limited Root Edit Restrictions On Removal Of Nested Contributors (Core) - For a period of three years after June 4, 2025, any Artifact Edit that would have the effect of removing a Nested Contributor must be approved by a vote of SKY holders in addition to a vote of SPK holders to be effective. Add a new subdocument of A.AG1.2.2.P6.2.1.2 - Operational Process Definition (Portal) / Spark - Operational Process Definition (Github) This document should be located directly after A.AG1.2.2.P6.2.1.2.3 - Emergency Protocol (Portal) / Spark - Emergency Protocol (Github) to read as follows: Short Term Transitionary Measures (Core) - In the short term, the parameters of the Spark Liquidity Layer, SparkLend, and Spark Savings are controlled by Sky Core, but will be transitioned to Spark in a future iteration of the Spark Artifact. See SparkLend Risk Parameters Modification .

This document should be located directly after A.AG3.3.1 - Governance Information Unrelated To Root Edit Primitive (Portal) / Launch Agent 2 - Governance Information Unrelated To Root Edit Primitive (GitHub) and its subdocuments, to read as follows: Use Of Idle Funds (Core) - In the short term prior to Launch Agent 2’s implementation of the Allocation System Primitive, Launch Agent 2 may invest idle funds in low risk decentralized finance opportunities, including providing liquidity to established lending protocols on Solana. These deployments will be subject to the approval of Operational GovOps. Correct Issues In The SPK Launch Proposal Replace A.2.3.9.1.1.2.2.1.3.2.1 - Core GovOps TRC Report Validation Process (Portal) / A.2.4 - Core GovOps TRC Report Validation Process (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.4 - Core GovOps TRC Report Validation Process (Core) -Core GovOps receives TRC Reports from Stars on a regular basis and must perform the following validation process. Core GovOps verifies against the Atlas any Ecosystem Accord referenced in the TRC Report for sourced Star-External Junior Risk Capital (SEJRC) or rented Originated Senior Risk Capital (OSRC). This includes confirming the existence, current validity, and terms of such Accords as formally recorded within the Atlas. Core GovOps validates the Star Agent’s reported IJRC by reconciling the reported IJRC amount and its constituent asset composition against the actual on-chain state of the Star Agent’s designated SubProxy account. This involves direct on-chain verification of asset balances. Core GovOps verifies that all assets reported as IJRC and held within the SubProxy account meet the definition of “eligible assets” for IJRC as defined by the Atlas. See A.3.3 - Internal Junior Risk Capital (IJRC) . For reported Tokenized External Junior Risk Capital (TEJRC) and Originated Senior Risk Capital directly originated by the Star, Core GovOps validates the reported amounts and statuses by cross-referencing data from the relevant smart contract systems. This may involve querying TEJRC pool contracts, OSRC auction records, and other on-chain infrastructure to confirm the existence, ownership, and eligibility of these capital components. Core GovOps reviews all attestations and disclosures made by the Star Agent in the TRC Report. This review focuses on understanding the Star Agent’s TRC compliance with Aggregate RRC throughout the entire reporting period. This assessment is critical for identifying intra-period shortfalls that might not be visible to on-chain monitoring systems or reflected in the end-of-period snapshot alone. The assessment process may include requiring the Star Agent to provide supplementary documentation, verifiable evidence, or independent third-party confirmations for material off-chain claims or attestations concerning intra-period events; and/or cross-referencing disclosed off-chain information with relevant on-chain indicators or transactions that might corroborate or contradict the attestations. On behalf of @atlas-axis , we are submitting the Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle proposal below. This proposal includes the following edits: Establish Framework For Implementation Of Monthly Settlement Cycle - Introduces a framework for a staged implementation of the Monthly Settlement Cycle. Update Slippage Estimation In The Risk Framework - Updates the methodology for estimating slippage in the Risk Framework. Provide Flexibility For Launch Agent 2 Capital Funding - Provides Launch Agent 2 with flexibility to fund development with capital previously allocated to providing liquidity. This initial implementation of the Monthly Settlement Cycle does not include the Senior Risk Capital System, which is still being developed, and funds continue to be allocated through Executive Votes rather than the allocation steps of the Treasury Management Function. See A.2.5 - Treasury Management - Treasury Management - Short Term Transitionary Measures . A.2.6 - Stage 1 (Core) - The documents herein define Stage 1 of the implementation of the Monthly Settlement Cycle. A.2.6 - Stage 1 Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation (Core) - In Stage 1 of the implementation of the Monthly Settlement Cycle, the net amount due from each Star to Sky will be calculated using a Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation. The Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation will be specified in a future iteration of the Atlas. A.2.6 - Stage 1 Timing (Core) - Stage 1 is currently expected to be implemented in the August 21, 2025 Executive Vote for the period from July 1, 2025 to July 31, 2025. A.2.6 - Stage 1 Actions (Core) - The actions specified herein must be completed to achieve Stage 1 implementation of the Monthly Settlement Cycle. A.2.6 - Reduction Of Star Allocator Vault Stability Fees (Core) - The Stability Fees for each Star Allocator Vault must be reduced to zero so that value is transferred from Stars to Sky Core exclusively through Executive Votes. The Core Executor Agent, in consultation with the Stability Facilitators and the Stability Scope Advisors, is directed to use the Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module to reduce the Stability Fee for each Star Allocator Vault to zero. See A.3.9 - Measures For Endgame Transition - Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module - Allocator Vault Parameters . A.2.6 - Documentation Of Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation (Core) - The Core Executor Agent must document the Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation herein. A.2.6 - Automation Of Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation (Core) - The Stability Scope Advisors must develop tooling to allow the net amount due from each Star to Sky each month under the Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation to be computed automatically. A.2.6 - Stage 2 (Core) - The documents herein define Stage 2 of the implementation of the Monthly Settlement Cycle. A.2.6 - Stage 2 Virtual Base Rate (Core) - In Stage 2 of the implementation of the Monthly Settlement Cycle, the net amount due from each Star to Sky is calculated as specified in the Atlas without the use of the Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation. However, interest under the Base Rate does not accrue in real time onchain and is instead calculated offchain and paid through Executive Votes as part of the Monthly Settlement Cycle. This is known as the Virtual Base Rate as these calculations occur offchain. A.2.6 - Stage 2 Timing (Core) - The timing for Stage 2 implementation of the Monthly Settlement Cycle will be specified in a future iteration of the Atlas. A.2.6 - Stage 2 Actions (Core) - The actions specified herein must be completed to achieve Stage 2 implementation of the Monthly Settlement Cycle. A.2.6 - Automation Of Monthly Settlement Cycle Calculation Including Virtual Base Rate (Core) - The Stability Scope Advisors must develop automated tooling for calculating the net amount due from each Star to Sky each month, incorporating the Virtual Base Rate. A.2.6 - Stage 3 (Core) - The documents herein define Stage 3 of the implementation of the Monthly Settlement Cycle. A.2.6 - Stage 3 Onchain Base Rate (Core) - In Stage 3 of the implementation of the Monthly Settlement Cycle, the net amount due from each Star to Sky is calculated as specified in the Atlas without the use of the Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation. In Stage 3, interest from the Base Rate accrues onchain to the Allocator Vault of each Star. Thus, in Stage 3 Executive Votes are only required to pay down accrued interest on Allocator Vaults, as necessary, and settle other amounts due to and from Stars. A.2.6 - Stage 3 Timing (Core) - The timing for Stage 3 implementation of the Monthly Settlement Cycle will be specified in a future iteration of the Atlas. A.2.6 - Stage 3 Actions (Core) - The actions specified herein must be completed to achieve Stage 3 implementation of the Monthly Settlement Cycle. A.2.6 - Automation Of Monthly Settlement Cycle Based On Base Rate (Core) - The Stability Scope Advisors must update the tooling specified in A.2.6 - Automation Of Monthly Settlement Cycle Calculation Including Virtual Base Rate to reflect the onchain accrual of the Base Rate. Document Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation Replace A.2.5.1.2.1.1 - Stage 1 Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation (Portal) / A.2.6 - Sky Core Monthly Settlement Cycle - Monthly Settlement Cycle Overview - Implementation - Stage 1 - Stage 1 Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation (GitHub) and its subdocuments to read as follows: A.2.6 - Stage 1 Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation (Core) - In Stage 1 of the implementation of the Monthly Settlement Cycle, the net amount due from each Star to Sky will be calculated using a Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation as specified in the documents herein. A.2.6 - Amount Due From Sky To Stars With Respect To Demand Side Primitives And Agent Rate (Core) - The amount due from Sky to each Star with respect to Demand Side Primitives and the Agent Rate is calculated as specified in the documents herein. A.2.6 - Amount Due From Sky To Stars With Respect To Accessibility Reward (Core) - The amount due from Sky to a Star in a month with respect to the Accessibility Reward is the amount earned by the Star with respect to all USDS and sUSDS balances marked with the Star’s reward codes. See A.2.4 - Accessibility Reward Primitive . This includes any Bonus Accessibility Reward. See A.2.10 - 2025 Bonus . A.2.6 - Amount Due From Sky To Stars With Respect To Agent Rate (Core) - The amount due from Sky to a Star in a month with respect to the Agent Rate is calculated as specified in A.3.2 - Core Stability Parameters - Parameters - Agent Rate . A.2.6 - Amount Due From Sky To Stars With Respect To Accessibility Reward And Agent Rate (Core) - The amount due from Sky to a Star in a month with respect to the Accessibility Reward and the Agent Rate is the sum of the amounts specified in A.2.6 - Amount Due From Sky To Stars With Respect To Accessibility Reward and A.2.6 - Amount Due From Sky To Stars With Respect To Agent Rate. A.2.6 - Amount Due From Stars To Sky With Respect To Supply Side Primitives (Core) - The amount due from each Star to Sky with respect to Supply Side Primitives is calculated as specified in the documents herein. A.2.6 - Step 1: Calculate Total Allocation System Revenue (Core) - First, Total Allocation System Revenue is calculated for each Star for the month. Total Allocation System Revenue for a Star in a month is the sum of Instance Revenue for each Active Instance of the Allocation System Primitive that the Star has deployed. A.2.6 - Instance Revenue (Core) - Instance Revenue for an Allocation System Instance for a month is all earnings from that Instance. A.2.6 - Step 2: Calculate Total Allocation System Profit (Core) - Second, Total Allocation System Profit is calculated for each Star for the month. Total Allocation System Profit for a Star in a month is the sum of Instance Profit for each Active Instance of the Allocation System Primitive that the Star has deployed. A.2.6 - Instance Profit (Core) - Instance Profit for an Allocation System Instance is equal to the greater of (1) Instance Revenue (see A.2.6 - Instance Revenue) minus Instance Expenses (see A.2.6 - Instance Expense) and (2) zero. A.2.6 - Instance Expense (Core) - Instance Expense for an Allocation System Instance for a month is the interest expense on the funds from Sky’s Collateral Portfolio invested in the Instance. It is calculated on a per block basis based on the amount invested from Sky’s Collateral Portfolio and the Base Rate. A.2.6 - Step 3: Calculate Adjusted Allocation System Profit (Core) - Third, Adjusted Allocation System Profit is calculated for each Star for the month. Adjusted Allocation System Profit for a Star in a month is Total Allocation System Profit minus the Distortion Penalty (see A.2.6 - Distortion Penalty) and the Low Yield Actively Stabilizing Collateral Penalty (see A.2.6 - Low Yield Actively Stabilizing Collateral Penalty). A.2.6 - Distortion Penalty (Core) - The Distortion Penalty is a discretionary penalty designed to mitigate the potential misalignment caused by the asymmetric nature of the Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation, where Stars earn profits on Allocation System Instances that earn more than the Base Rate but do not suffer losses when Instances earn less than the Base Rate. The Core Executor Agent, in consultation with the Stability Facilitators and the Stability Scope Advisors, may assess a penalty of up to 100% of Total Allocation System Profit (see A.2.6 - Step 2: Calculate Total Allocation System Profit) if it determines that a Star’s decisions were distorted by this incentive structure. A.2.6 - Low Yield Actively Stabilizing Collateral Penalty (Core) - The Low Yield Actively Stabilizing Collateral Penalty is a formulaic penalty designed to prevent Stars from holding excessive amounts of low yield Actively Stabilizing Collateral. The penalty, as a percentage of the Total Allocation System Profit, is the lesser of (1) ten times the Excess Low Yield Actively Stabilizing Collateral Percentage and (2) 100%. A.2.6 - Excess Low Yield Actively Stabilizing Collateral Percentage (Core) - The Excess Low Yield Actively Stabilizing Collateral Percentage for a Star is equal to the excess of (1) its Low Yield Actively Stabilizing Collateral (see A.2.6 - Low Yield Actively Stabilizing Collateral) as a percentage of its Collateral Portfolio above (2) its Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral (see A.3.4 - Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral ) as a percentage of its Collateral Portfolio. A.2.6 - Low Yield Actively Stabilizing Collateral (Core) - Low Yield Actively Stabilizing Collateral is Actively Stabilizing Collateral (see A.3.4 - Actively Stabilizing Collateral ) that earns less than the Base Rate. A.2.6 - Step 4: Calculate Amount Due To Sky With Respect To Supply Side Primitives (Core) - Fourth, the amount due to Sky with respect to Supply Side Primitives is calculated for each Star for the month. The amount due to Sky with respect to Supply Side Primitives is Total Allocation System Revenue (see A.2.6 - Step 1: Calculate Total Allocation System Revenue) minus Adjusted Allocation System Profit (see A.2.6 - Step 3: Calculate Adjusted Allocation System Profit). A.2.6 - Net Amount Due From Stars To Sky (Core) - The net amount due from each Star to Sky is the amount due from the Star to Sky with respect to Supply Side Primitives (see A.2.6 - Amount Due From Stars To Sky With Respect To Supply Side Primitives) plus any amount due from the Star to Sky with respect to the Token Launch Penalty (see A.2.10 - Token Launch Penalty ) minus the amount due from Sky to the Star with respect to Demand Side Primitives and the Agent Rate (see A.2.6 - Amount Due From Sky To Stars With Respect To Demand Side Primitives And Agent Rate). Net amounts due from a Star to Sky are transferred from the Star’s Treasury to the Surplus Buffer through a Star Spell included in an Executive Vote. Net amounts due from Sky to a Star are transferred from the Surplus Buffer to the Star’s Treasury through an Executive Vote. These documents should be located directly after A.1.9.2.2.11 - Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module Breaker Exception (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module Breaker Exception (GitHub) to read as follows: A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Linear Interpolation Module (Core) - The Linear Interpolation Module ( lerp ) is a smart contract tool that allows a governance parameter to be adjusted on a straight-line basis over time, without requiring additional Executive Votes. The Linear Interpolation Module refers to the smart contract logic that enables time-based parameter changes. To deploy individual lerp instances, each of which manages the adjustment of a specific parameter over time, the Linear Interpolation Module Factory contract is used. Once authorized through an Executive Vote, the lerp may enact parameter changes without being subject to the GSM Pause Delay. The subdocuments herein specify the features of the lerp and its authorized use. A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Linear Interpolation Module Features (Core) - The lerp must be activated in an Executive Vote but can thereafter change the value of the designated parameter without additional Executive Votes. Each lerp instance is defined in terms of a start value, representing the desired starting value, an end value, representing the desired ending value, and a duration over which the parameter will be adjusted between the starting value and the ending value. Any user can then permissionlessly call tick to set the governance parameter to the appropriate value based on the time elapsed. A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Linear Interpolation Module Parameters (Core) - Each lerp instance has the following parameters: target - The target contract in which a parameter is being changed what - The name of the parameter being changed startTime - The starting time of this lerp instance start - The starting value of that parameter end - The ending value of that parameter duration - How long this lerp instance will run for done - Indicates whether this given lerp instance is completed or not A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Linear Interpolation Module Factory (Core) - lerp instances are created using a factory contract LERP_FAB that contains standard logic for creating those instances and maintains a registry of all active lerp instances. The contract may also be used to cancel an existing lerp instance through the remove function. The factory contract provides a list method that lists the addresses of all active lerp instances, as well as a tall (short for “tick all”) method that calls tick on all active contracts. A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Linear Interpolation Module Usage Process Definition (Core) - The subdocuments herein define the governance process for using the Linear Interpolation Module. A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Linear Interpolation Module Authorization (Core) - The Facilitators responsible for the Scope that governs the parameter to be adjusted by the Linear Interpolation Module, in consultation with the Scope Advisor(s), may recommend deploying the Linear Interpolation Module for parameter adjustments. A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Linear Interpolation Module Consideration (Core) - The Facilitators must take into consideration the benefits and costs with using the Linear Interpolation Module. A longer duration has the benefit of adjusting the parameter more slowly, giving users more time to adjust. However, the drawback of a longer duration is that the parameter will not reach its desired end value for a longer period of time. When the cost of a parameter not being at its desired value is high, use of the Linear Interpolation Module is not appropriate and the parameter should be adjusted to its desired value following the required process. A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Governance Process For Linear Interpolation Module (Core) - The process to utilize the Linear Interpolation Module to adjust a parameter must follow the same governance process required to modify the designated parameter. If the parameter can be updated directly through an Executive Vote, then utilizing the Linear Interpolation Module to adjust it may also be included directly in an Executive Vote. If modifying the parameter requires a prior Governance Poll, then utilizing the Linear Interpolation Module for that parameter must also be preceded by a Governance Poll.

commits.changeSummary: On behalf of @atlas-axis , we are submitting the Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle proposal below. This proposal includes the following edits: Establish Spark Delegate System - Introduces a Delegate System for Spark. Improve Organization Of Risk Framework - Updates the organization of the Risk Framework to move all short term logic to the Implementation Section. Update Name Of Audit Firm - Updates the name of yAudit to Electisec to reflect their rebranding. Remove Documents For Deprecated Vaults - Removes documents for the deprecated Morpho Direct Deposit Module and Spark Dai Direct Deposit Modules. Establish Spark Delegate System Replace A.AG1.2.2.P6.2.1.2.1.4 - Root Edit Token Holder Vote (Portal) / Spark - Root Edit Token Holder Vote (GitHub) to read as follows: Root Edit Token Holder Vote (Core) - Where their review of the proposal results in a finding of alignment with the Sky Core Atlas and Spark Artifact, the Operational Facilitator next triggers a Snapshot poll to allow token holders to vote on the proposal. Token holders may vote directly or through Delegates. See Delegation Framework. The poll is open for three (3) days. A poll must have at least 10% of the circulating token supply participating and must have 50% of votes in favor to be approved. Add new subdocuments of A.AG1.3.1 - Governance Information Unrelated To Root Edit Primitive (Portal) / Spark - Governance Information Unrelated To Root Edit Primitive (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly before A.AG1.3.1.3 - Sky Ecosystem Emergency Response (Portal) / Spark - Sky Ecosystem Emergency Response (GitHub) and after A.AG1.3.1.2 - Discord (Portal) / Spark - Discord (GitHub) and its subdocuments to read as follows: Delegation Framework (Core) - The documents herein specify Spark’s governance delegation system, defining the rights and duties of Delegates and Delegators, as well as the processes for onboarding and offboarding Delegates. Delegate Definition (Core) - A “Delegate” is a recognized actor empowered to exercise governance voting power on behalf of one or more SPK holders (”Delegators”). Delegates act as trusted representatives and are expected to vote in the long-term best interest of the Spark ecosystem. How Delegation Works (Core) - SPK holders may assign (“delegate”) the full voting power of their wallet to an Active Delegate at any time (see Registry of Delegates). The key features of delegation are specified in the subdocuments herein. Interfaces (Core) - Delegation can be executed through (i) the Spark App or (ii) directly on Spark’s Snapshot page. Snapshot Voting-Power Lock (Core) - A snapshot records voting power at each proposal snapshot-block height. Voting power (including delegations) cannot be altered for the duration of a specific active proposal. Changes in voting power are reflected in future votes. Undelegation Re-delegation (Core) - Delegators may revoke or move their delegation whenever no proposal is live. All changes take effect at the next snapshot-block. Restrictions (Core) - SPK holders may only assign their voting power to Active Delegates. This also means Delegators cannot delegate to another wallet they themselves control, unless it is an Active Delegate wallet. Delegate Responsibilities (Core) - The responsibilities for Delegates are defined in the subdocuments herein. Monitor Governance Channels (Core) - The Delegate must track the Sky Forum (“Spark Prime” category), Discord, and any other official communication venues for new proposals and discussions. Review Proposals Thoroughly (Core) - The Delegate must evaluate technical, economic, and risk implications before voting. Vote on Every Proposal (Core) - The Delegate must cast a vote (For / Against) on 100% of governance proposals within the designated voting window (see Root Edit Token Holder Vote ). Abstain Only for Disclosed Conflicts (Core) - The “Abstain” option may be used solely in cases where the Delegate has a documented conflict of interest for the specific proposal. Disclosure Of Conflicts (Core) - Conflicts must be disclosed to both the Spark Foundation and the Operational Facilitator before the voting window (see Root Edit Token Holder Vote ) for the proposal begins. Recording Of Conflicts (Core) - All conflicts are recorded in Registry of Delegates under the Delegate’s entry. Abstaining For Non-Disclosed Conflicts (Core) - Abstaining for any reason other than a recorded conflict is treated as non-performance under Delegate Offboarding. Report Rationale (Core) - The Delegate must post a concise rationale for each vote on the proposal thread. Maintain Independence (Core) - The Delegate must disclose conflicts of interest and abstain where impartiality is compromised (see Disclosure Of Conflicts). Failure to meet these obligations is grounds for offboarding (see Delegate Offboarding). Delegate Onboarding (Core) - The Delegate onboarding process is specified in the subdocuments herein. Bootstrapping Phase (Core) - During the bootstrapping phase, before the Spark Risk Council (SRC) is formally established, two (2) initial Delegates will be appointed directly by the Operational Facilitator with the advice and consent of the Spark Foundation through a public announcement on the Sky Forum, following a due diligence review equivalent to the standards set out in Application Requirements. Upon the formal constitution of the SRC, all future Delegate appointments and oversight will be conducted by the SRC as specified below. Application Requirements (Core) - Prospective Delegates must submit (i) identity contact info, (ii) delegate wallet address, and (iii) a signed statement accepting the responsibilities in Delegate Responsibilities. These requirements are further specified in the subdocuments herein. Requirement To Verify Identity (Core) - Every prospective Delegate must complete an initial, confidential identity verification process with the Spark Foundation, subject to additional KYC verification as necessary in the future. Delegates may remain anonymous or pseudonymous to the public. Conflict-of-Interest Disclosure (Core) - At onboarding, prospective Delegates must provide any known conflicts of interest to the Spark Foundation and the Operational Facilitator. Disclosures are appended to their entry in Registry of Delegates and updated as new conflicts arise. Eligibility (Core) - Individuals or entities listed on any international sanctions list are ineligible to serve as Delegates. In addition, a prospective Delegate may be deemed ineligible if, in the Spark Foundation’s sole discretion, their participation would be unlawful or would pose undue risk to Spark. Ongoing Compliance (Core) - Delegates must promptly update the Spark Foundation on any material change in their legal status. Failure to do so results in automatic suspension until rectified. Grounds for Disqualification (Core) - Submission of fraudulent information, criminal indictment for financial crime, or repeated governance negligence (see Non-Performance Removal) triggers an SRC-initiated Delegate Removal vote. Application Does Not Guarantee Acceptance (Core) - The submission of a Delegate Application is not a guarantee of acceptance and is subject to the above requirements, availability of additional Delegate seats, and the SRC. Minimum Term (Core) - Delegates are guaranteed to serve at least six (6) months, unless they are in violation of their duties. Delegates can always voluntarily offboard according to the process outlined in Delegate Offboarding. Delegate Record (Core) - Accepted Delegates are appended to Registry of Delegates. Delegate Offboarding (Core) - The delegation offboarding process is specified in the subdocuments herein. Voluntary Offboarding (Core) - A Delegate can voluntarily offboard by submitting a resignation message in the Spark Star category of Sky Forum with a signed message from their Delegate wallet as proof. The offboarding takes effect immediately after all active proposals conclude. Non-Performance Removal (Core) - A Delegate is automatically offboarded if they: Fail to vote on ≥ 3 proposals in a row; or Maintain a voting percentage less than 85%. Emergency-Removal (Core) - The Spark Risk Council can immediately offboard a delegate if they: Breach disclosure / conflict-of-interest duties; Engage in malicious or negligent conduct; or Fail to provide acceptable KYC or updated KYC when requested. Updating of Status (Core) - Upon offboarding, the Delegate’s status in Registry of Delegates is updated to Inactive. SPK delegators must manually revoke their delegations and redelegate if they wish to continue participating in Spark governance. Incentives Compensation (Core) - Spark currently offers no protocol-level monetary incentives to Delegates. Delegation is viewed as a pro-bono stewardship role. The governance community may revisit compensation only through a future Root Edit proposal. Security Requirements Compromise Procedure (Core) - The security requirements and procedure for a compromised key are specified in the subdocuments herein. Operational Security (Core) - Delegates must: Sign votes from a hardware wallet or an equivalent secure device. Use unique signing keys that are never reused for personal transactions. Enable Multi-Factor Authentication on any platform accounts used for governance communication. Compromised Key Response (Core) - If a Delegate suspects key compromise, the following steps must be taken: The Delegate must notify the SRC as soon as the breach is discovered. SRC flags the Delegate in Registry of Delegates as “Suspended - Security Review” and notifies the governance community on the Sky Forum. All voting power to the suspended address is annulled. The Delegate may submit a new verified address; upon SRC approval, suspensions are lifted and delegations migrate at the next snapshot-block. Non-Compliance (Core) - Failure to execute the steps in Compromised Key Response within 48 hours constitutes grounds for emergency removal. Registry of Delegates (Core) - The subdocuments herein list each active Delegate’s name, wallet address, effective date, status and conflict disclosures. Entries are maintained via an Active Data document updated by the Operational Facilitator. Template Information For Each Delegate (Core) - The list of Delegates must follow this template for each recorded Delegate: Delegate Name: Delegate Wallet Address: Effective Date: Status: Active/Inactive/Suspended Conflict Disclosures: Updating List of Delegates (Active Data Controller) - The list of Delegates is defined as Active Data in List of Delegates. The Active Data is updated as follows: The Responsible Party is the Operational Facilitator. The Update Process must follow the protocol for ‘Direct Edit’. List of Delegates (Active Data) - The information for each Delegate is listed below: Subject to Change (Core) - Spark reserves the right to vary or amend these terms at its discretion, subject to established Spark Artifact governance procedures related to Artifact edits. Prepare For Implementation Of stUSDS Add a new subdocument of A.1.9.2.2.10 - Bounded External Access Modules (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Bounded External Access Modules (GitHub) . This document should be located directly after A.1.9.2.2.10.2 - Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module Exception (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Bounded External Access Modules - Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module Exception (GitHub) to read as follows: A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - stUSDS Bounded External Access Module Exception (Core) - The stUSDS Bounded External Access Module (stUSDS BEAM) manages the parameters of the stUSDS system. Whitelisted operators can use the stUSDS BEAM to modify rates without waiting for the GSM Pause Delay. The stUSDS BEAM modifies stUSDS parameters within specified ranges. See A.4.4 - stUSDS Bounded External Access Module. This functionality allows the Sky Protocol to update stUSDS parameters more quickly than waiting for the Governance and Spell Process execution and the GSM Pause Delay. The risk opened up by this functionality is malicious action by whitelisted operators setting stUSDS parameters to undesirable values. This risk can be mitigated through the stUSDS BEAM parameters and the STUSDS_MOM. Add a new subdocument of A.1.9.2.2 - Exceptions (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Exceptions (GitHub) . This document should be located directly before A.1.9.2.2.12 - Linear Interpolation Module (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Linear Interpolation Module (GitHub) and after A.1.9.2.2.11 - Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module Breaker Exception (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module Breaker Exception (GitHub) to read as follows: A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - stUSDS Bounded External Access Module Breaker Exception (Core) - The STUSDS_MOM contract allows Sky Governance to bypass the GSM Pause Delay and disable the stUSDS Bounded External Access Module or set the cap or line stUSDS parameters to zero. This functionality allows Sky Governance to react more quickly in an emergency, e.g., if an operator of the stUSDS BEAM is hacked or is a malicious actor. Once the STUSDS_MOM is activated to disable the stUSDS BEAM, the stUSDS BEAM will not be able to change any stUSDS parameters in the system. If the STUSDS_MOM has been triggered, it will still be possible to modify stUSDS parameters through the usual Executive Vote process, subject to the GSM Pause Delay. Replace A.4.4.1.2.2 - stUSDS Rate (Portal) / A.4.4 - SKY Staking Mechanism - SKY Staking - SKY-Backed Borrowing - stUSDS Rate (GitHub) and its subdocuments to read as follows: A.4.4 - stUSDS Rate (Core) - The variable yield earned by stUSDS holders is calculated using the formula: stUSDS Rate = Sky Savings Rate + (SKY Borrow Rate - SKY Borrow Minimum Rate) * Utilization - Rfactor * f(Utilization) A.4.4 - Parameters Definition (Core) - The parameters of the stUSDS Rate formula are further defined in the documents herein. A.4.4 Sky Savings Rate Definition (Core) - Sky Savings Rate is the Sky Savings Rate defined in A.3.2 - Core Stability Parameters - Parameters - Sky Savings Rate . A.4.4 - SKY Borrow Rate Definition (Core) - SKY Borrow Rate is the SKY Borrow Rate defined in A.4.4 - SKY Borrow Rate . SKY Borrow Minimum Rate Definition (Core) - SKY Borrow Minimum Rate is the SKY Borrow Minimum Rate defined in A.4.4 - SKY Borrow Minimum Rate . A.4.4 - Utilization Definition (Core) - Utilization is the percent of funds in the stUSDS contract that are used to fund borrowing against staked SKY. A.4.4 - Utilization Calculation (Core) - The Utilization is calculated as a time-weighted utilization over a one (1) day interval. A.4.4 - Time-Weighted Utilization (Core) - The documents herein define the process to calculate time-weighted utilization. A.4.4 - Determine Start And End Times (Core) - First, the start time T_{0} and end time T_{n} of the interval, over which time-weighted utilization are to be calculated, are selected. A.4.4 - Collect Borrow And Supply Events (Core) - Data is then collected on all supply and borrow events, sorted by time, where: t_{i} is the timestamp of event i ; B_{i} is the total amount borrowed at time t_{i} ; S_{i} is the total amount supplied at time t_{i} ; and U_{i} is the utilization at time t_{i} , \frac{B_{i}}{S_{i}} . A.4.4 - Insert Synthetic Events (Core) - If t_{0} is greater than T_{0} then a synthetic event is inserted at T_{0} with values B_{0} and S_{0} . Similarly, if t_{n} is less than T_{n} then a synthetic event is inserted at T_{n} with values B_{n} and S_{n} . A.4.4 - Calculate Time-Weighted Utilization (Core) - Finally, the time-weighted utilization is calculated using the following formula: \text{Util}_{\mathrm{avg}} = \frac{\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} U_i \cdot (t_{i+1} - t_i)}{T_n - T_0} A.4.4 - Reference Implementation (Core) - A reference implementation of the time-weighted utilization formula is included herein. The reference implementation uses sample data and a 30 day interval for illustrative purposes. # Your list of real events: (timestamp, total_borrowed, total_supply) events = [ (datetime(2025, 7, 25, 10), 100_000, 200_000), (datetime(2025, 7, 25, 16), 120_000, 210_000), (datetime(2025, 7, 26, 8), 130_000, 220_000), (datetime(2025, 7, 27, 12), 110_000, 215_000), (datetime(2025, 7, 28, 9), 140_000, 225_000), ] # Ensure events are sorted events.sort() # Get time window now = datetime.utcnow() start_time = now - timedelta(days=30) # Add synthetic first event (30d ago) using earliest known borrow/supply first_real_ts, first_borrow, first_supply = events[0] if first_real_ts start_time: events.insert(0, (start_time, first_borrow, first_supply)) # Add synthetic final event (now) using most recent known borrow/supply last_real_ts, last_borrow, last_supply = events[-1] if last_real_ts now: events.append((now, last_borrow, last_supply)) # Step 1: Compute utilization per event utilizations = [] for ts, borrow, supply in events: utilization = borrow / supply if supply != 0 else 0 utilizations.append((ts, utilization)) # Step 2: Compute time-weighted utilization average weighted_sum = 0 total_time = 0 for i in range(len(utilizations) - 1): ts1, util1 = utilizations[i] ts2, _ = utilizations[i + 1] time_diff = (ts2 - ts1).total_seconds() weighted_sum += util1 * time_diff total_time += time_diff avg_utilization = weighted_sum / total_time if total_time 0 else 0 print(f"30-day time-weighted average utilization: {avg_utilization:.2%}") A.4.4 - Rfactor Definition (Core) - Rfactor is calculated using the formula: Rfactor = \frac{2u_m - 1}{2u_m \left( u_{opt}(\alpha + 1) - 1 + \frac{\beta u_{opt}}{slope1} \right)} The parameters of this formula are specified in the documents herein. A.4.4 - Maximum Profit Utilization Definition (Core) - u_{m} is the maximum profit utilization. A.4.4 - Maximum Profit Utilization Current Value (Core) - The current value of u_{m} is 70%. A.4.4 - Target Utilization Definition (Core) - u_{opt} is the target utilization specified in A.4.4 Rate Setting Mechanism. A.4.4 - Alpha Definition (Core) - \alpha is calculated using the formula: alpha = ((SKY Borrow Maximum Rate - SKY Borrow Minimum Rate) / Slope 1) - 1 The parameters of this formula are specified in the documents herein. A.4.4 - SKY Borrow Maximum Rate Definition (Core) - SKY Borrow Maximum Rate is the maximum value of the SKY Borrow Rate at 100% Utilization. A.4.4 - SKY Borrow Maximum Rate Current Value (Core) - The current value of the SKY Borrow Maximum Rate is 30%. A.4.4 - SKY Borrow Minimum Rate Definition (Core) - SKY Borrow Minimum Rate is the SKY Borrow Minimum Rate specified in A.4.4 - SKY Borrow Minimum Rate . A.4.4 - Slope 1 Definition (Core) - Slope 1 is the Slope 1 parameter specified in A.4.4 - Slope 1. A.4.4 - Beta Definition (Core) - \beta is a tuning parameter that determines how much profit is made at maximum utilization. A.4.4 - Beta Current Value (Core) - The current value of \beta is 100%. A.4.4 - Slope 1 Definition (Core) - slope1 is the Slope 1 parameter specified in A.4.4 - Slope 1. A.4.4 - Utilization Function Definition (Core) - f(Utilization) is calculated using the formula: f(Utilization) = Utilization * ((SKY Borrow Maximum Rate - SKY Borrow Minimum Rate + Beta) * Utilization + SKY Borrow Minimum Rate - SKY Borrow Rate) The parameters of this formula are specified in the documents herein. A.4.4 - Utilization Definition (Core) - Utilization is the utilization as specified in A.4.4 - Utilization Definition. A.4.4 - SKY Borrow Maximum Rate Definition (Core) - SKY Borrow Maximum Rate is the SKY Borrow Maximum Rate specified in A.4.4 - SKY Borrow Maximum Rate Definition. A.4.4 - SKY Borrow Minimum Rate Definition (Core) - SKY Borrow Minimum Rate is the SKY Borrow Minimum Rate specified in A.4.4 - SKY Borrow Minimum Rate Definition. A.4.4 - Beta Definition (Core) - Beta is the beta specified in A.4.4 - Beta Definition. A.4.4 - SKY Borrow Rate Definition (Core) - SKY Borrow Rate is the SKY Borrow Rate specified in A.4.4 - SKY Borrow Rate. A.4.4 - Parameters Modification (Core) - The parameters specified in A.4.4 - Parameters Definition that are set by governance may be modified by the Core Executor Agents, in consultation with the Stability Scope Advisors. This process will be conducted through the Operational Weekly Governance Cycle or, if necessary, through out-of-schedule Executive Votes. This document should be located directly before A.2.3.9.1.1 - Allocation System Process Definition (Portal) / A.2.4 - Allocation System Process Definition (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.4 - Base Elements (Core) - The documents herein define base elements of the Allocation System Primitive. A.2.4 - Liquidity Layer Parameter Definitions (Core) - The documents herein define common parameters of implementations of the Allocation System based on the Spark Liquidity Layer, including the Grove Liquidity Layer A.2.4 - Rate Limiter (Core) - Rate Limiter refers to the overall mechanism or system that limits the volume of token movements over time, implemented via the RateLimits contracts. The Rate Limiter manages multiple rate limits and enforces constraints on controller operations to prevent rapid asset drainage and mitigate risks from compromised relayers or other attacks. This ensures that the maximum amount of tokens processed within a specific time period stays within safe bounds. The RateLimits contracts and their addresses for each chain can be found in the Allocation System Primitive for a Prime, under ALM Contracts. A.2.4 - Rate Limits (Core) - Rate limits set the maximum allowable amount of tokens that can be processed for specific operations within a given time period. Each rate limit contains the rate limit data: maxAmount , slope , lastAmount and lastUpdated . The current rate limit is calculated using the formula: currentRateLimit = min(slope * (block.timestamp - lastUpdated) + lastAmount, maxAmount) . The rate limit data maxAmount and slope are configurable parameters that are set and modified by Governance. The rate limit data lastAmount and lastUpdated are internal state data dynamically tracked by the Rate Limiter to perform its calculations. Rate limits set caps on the rate of allocation to a given Instance, they do not act as a limit on the total amount that may be allocated to that Instance. A.2.4 - MaxAmount (Core) - maxAmount sets a hard cap on the level of allocation to an Instance at any given time. It sets the absolute rate limit regardless of how much time has passed since the last allocation. For example, if maxAmount is set to 1,000,000 tokens, the rate limit will increase over time at the rate determined by the slope until it reaches 1,000,000 tokens, at this point the rate limit will stop increasing, but it will resume increasing once an allocation to the Instance has been made. A.2.4 - Slope (Core) - slope is the linear refill rate of a rate limiter’s allowance over time. It defines how quickly the capacity to perform additional inflow or outflow accrues after prior consumption. For example, if the slope is set to 1,000,000 tokens per day (converted to per second for on-chain execution), the rate limit will recover at that rate until it reaches the maxAmount. A.2.4 - LastUpdated (Core) - lastUpdated is the timestamp when the rate limit was last updated, serving as the reference point for calculating time-elapsed refills in the formula. A.2,4 - LastAmount (Core) - lastAmount is the remaining allowance available at the last update, used to compute the current rate limit by adding accrued capacity. A.2.4 - Inflow Rate Limits (Core) - Inflow rate limits constrain the rate at which allocated liquidity can increase into a scope. “Inflow” means movements that raise exposure or capital allocated to an Instance or market, such as depositing, minting, or rebalancing into a position. A.2.4 - Outflow Rate Limits (Core) - Outflow Rate Limits constrain the rate at which allocated liquidity can be withdrawn or exposure reduced from a scope. “Outflow” means movements that lower exposure or capital allocated to an Instance or market, such as withdrawals, redemptions, or unwind operations. Outflow limits are often configured more permissively to prioritize safety and fast exits. When outflow limits are “unlimited,” the rate limits contract simply does not apply a cap in that direction. A.2.4 - Rate Limit IDs (Core) - A Rate Limit ID is a bytes32 key that uniquely identifies a rate limit. Rate Limit IDs allow the system to maintain independent allowance state for each relevant transaction. A.2.4 - MaxSlippage (Core) - maxSlippage is a configurable parameter that sets the maximum allowed price impact or deviation from expected output when executing trades or liquidity operations in a pool. maxslippage is expressed as a decimal and must be a non-zero value. This protects against excessive price impact during volatile market conditions. The SRC safeguards the integrity and security of the Spark Ecosystem by conducting pre-vote risk reviews and, where necessary, preventing proposals from proceeding to a vote in order to protect Spark. Purpose And Mandate (Core) - The SRC identifies, assesses, and mitigates technical, economic, and governance-process risks posed by proposals subject to Spark Governance. The SRC’s mandate is to inform the community of potential risks inherent in proposals and, where necessary, prevent proposals from proceeding that are malicious or likely to expose Spark to substantial, unreasonable risk. Scope Of Review (Core) - The SRC reviews proposals for (i) security vulnerabilities and operational attack surface, (ii) market and treasury risks, (iii) economic risk, and (iv) misalignment with the Sky Core Atlas or the Spark Artifact. The SRC’s authority is limited to reviewing proposals within this scope. SRC Risk Review Process (Core) - The subdocuments herein clarify the process of the SRC independent risk review in terms of new Root Edit proposals. See Root Edit Proposal Submission. SRC Risk Review (Core) - Within seven (7) days (based on the start of the weekly cycle) of a new Atlas Root Edit proposal, the SRC must conduct an independent risk review and post (i) a conclusion (“Passed SRC Review,” or “Failed SRC Review”) and (ii) a stand-alone risk analysis to the relevant forum thread. Details for each of these deliverables are set out in the subdocuments herein. SRC Risk Review Conclusion (Core) - The SRC conclusion must reflect the majority opinion of SRC members. However, individual SRC members are free to post dissenting or concurring opinions at their discretion. See Concurring Or Dissenting Opinions. SRC Risk Analysis (Core) - The SRC risk analysis must summarize key findings, assumptions, mitigations, and any monitoring plan. SRC Risk Review Extension (Core) - The SRC can formally request, at the Operational Facilitator’s discretion, an extension of the deadline of seven (7) days by posting a public justification for an extension in the Sky Forum. Failure To Review (Core) - If no SRC conclusion or request for extension is posted within seven (7) days of submission, the Operational Facilitator will move the proposal to the Snapshot voting phase, provided the proposal is aligned with the Sky Core Atlas and the Spark Artifact. “Failed SRC Review” Authority and Procedure (Core) - The subdocuments herein set out the threshold, process and implications of a “Failed SRC Review” determination by the SRC. Standard (Core) - A determination of “Failed SRC Review” may be exercised when a proposal is determined to be: malicious or exploitative; procedurally non-compliant with the Sky Core Atlas or Spark Artifact; likely to expose Spark to substantial, unreasonable risk; or in need of revisions in order for the SRC to evaluate the proposal. Threshold (Core) - A determination of “Failed SRC Review” must reflect the majority opinion of SRC members. Failed SRC Review Notice (Core) - A “Failed SRC Review” notice must be posted on the Sky Forum in the relevant thread prior to the Snapshot voting window opening (or, if already posted, prior to closure). Operational Facilitator Designation (Core) - The Operational Facilitator marks the proposal “Failed SRC Review.” Effect (Core) - The proposal does not proceed to Snapshot (or is withdrawn). Composition, Tenure, And Due Diligence (Core) - The subdocuments herein set out key details about the SRC, including their composition and appointment. Expertise (Core) - SRC members shall be domain experts across security, risk/economics, and operations. Seat Count (Core) - The SRC will have a seat count of three (3). Bootstrapping Phase (Core) - During the bootstrapping phase, initial members are appointed directly by the Operational Facilitator in consultation with the Spark Foundation through a public announcement on the Sky Forum. The Operational Facilitator shall either reappoint current SRC members to their seats or appoint new members in consultation with and with the consent of the Spark Foundation on an as-needed basis to allow the Operational Facilitator and the Spark Foundation flexibility during the initial governance procedures. Coordinator (Core) - The Nested Contributor Phoenix Labs has a seat on the SRC as a non-voting coordinating member. The role of the coordinator is to facilitate the work of the SRC being done in a timely manner. Due Diligence (Core) - Members may be required to complete a confidential due diligence process, if the Spark Foundation deems it necessary. Compensation (Core) - SRC members will receive compensation for performing their role on terms approved by the Spark Foundation. Council Meetings (Core) - The subdocuments herein set out details about SRC meetings, including cadence and external participation. Cadence (Core) - The SRC shall hold a monthly internal governance meeting. Participants (Core) - In addition to SRC members, representatives of the Spark Foundation, Nested Contributor Phoenix Labs, and the Operational Facilitator are each permitted to attend in a coordinating and facilitating capacity. Mid-Term Appointments And Member Changes (Core) - The subdocuments herein set out the process for mid-term appointments and other out-of-schedule replacement rules. Vacancies Mid-Term (Out-Of-Schedule Replacement Appointment) (Core) - If a seat becomes vacant (resignation, removal, ineligibility, or failure to complete due diligence), the Operational Facilitator shall make an out-of-schedule replacement appointment. This process is defined in the subdocuments herein. Notice (Core) - Within seven (7) days of the vacancy, the Operational Facilitator publishes a vacancy notice and forum thread on the Sky Forum describing the circumstances of the vacancy. Appointment (Core) - The Operational Facilitator shall appoint a replacement member of the SRC to fill the vacant seat in consultation with the Spark Foundation and publish a new post in the relevant forum thread in order to announce the appointment. Term (Core) - The appointee is seated upon due diligence completion to the Spark Foundation’s satisfaction and update to the SRC Membership Registry and serves the remainder of the current term. Seating And Continuity (Core) - Incumbent SRC members remain in office until successors are seated to ensure continuity of SRC operations. Newly appointed members are seated upon completion of due diligence to the Spark Foundation’s satisfaction and publication to the SRC Membership Registry. Process Requirements (Core) - The subdocuments herein set out key deliverables for the SRC as well as rules around conflicts of interest. Concurring Or Dissenting Opinions (Core) - In addition to the determinative independent risk review posted by the SRC for each proposal, individual SRC members may post concurring or dissenting opinions in the Sky Forum at their discretion. Conflicts Of Interest (Core) - SRC members must disclose conflicts of interest to Spark Foundation and recuse themselves where impartiality is compromised. Non-Performance (Core) - Repeated failure to meet review timelines; failure to document decisions; blocking valid proposals due to malicious intent or evident poor due diligence; or any other failure to uphold the duties of the SRC set forth in the Spark Artifact may trigger removal and replacement of SRC members at the discretion of the Spark Foundation. A.2.10 - Dispute Resolution By Core Council (Core) - Disputes regarding Ecosystem Accords are resolved by the Core Council as specified in the documents herein. A.2.10 - Roles (Core) - The documents herein define the respective roles of Core GovOps and the Core Facilitator in resolving disputes. A.2.10 - Role Of Core GovOps (Core) - Core GovOps manages the overall dispute resolution process, including establishing communication channels for dispute resolution, communicating with the parties, and gathering and analyzing information relating to the dispute. A.2.10 - Role Of Core Facilitator (Core) - The Core Facilitator decides how the dispute is ultimately resolved. The Core Facilitator is isolated from the parties to maintain impartiality. The Core Facilitator exclusively reviews the information prepared by Core GovOps and delivers a decision to Core GovOps, which communicates it to the parties. A.2.10 - Process Definition (Core) - The documents herein define the process for resolving disputes. A.2.10 - Dispute Intake (Core) - The documents herein define the process for dispute intake for dispute resolution. A.2.10 - Formal Request For Dispute Resolution (Core) - The dispute resolution process begins with an actor in the Sky Ecosystem requesting formal dispute resolution from Core GovOps. A.2.10 - Preliminary Determination Of Reasonableness By Core GovOps (Core) - After receiving the request for dispute resolution, Core GovOps makes a brief preliminary determination regarding whether the request is reasonable (i.e. not vexatious or frivolous), within three (3) working days. A.2.10 - Handling Of Unreasonable Requests (Core) - If Core GovOps determines that the request for dispute resolution is not reasonable, it will inform the actor who submitted the request accordingly, providing their reasons. In this case, there is no further action. A.2.10 - Handling Of Reasonable Requests (Core) - If Core GovOps makes a determination that the request is reasonable, then Core GovOps formally begins the dispute resolution process by notifying all relevant parties that the process is about to begin. The notifications to each party will outline the process to be followed, including relevant steps and timeframes that the party should be aware of. A.2.10 - Presentation Of Arguments (Core) - The documents herein define the process for the presentation of arguments for dispute resolution. A.2.10 - Statement Of Problem (Core) - The party that initiated the dispute resolution process has five (5) working days from the formal initiation of the process to submit a Statement of Problem, laying out the facts they consider relevant to the dispute and the issues related to the Atlas as they see them. A.2.10 - Statement Of Response (Core) - Core GovOps provides the Statement of Problem to the other party/parties. They have five (5) working days to submit a Statement of Response, which sets out their perspective on the relevant facts and issues in the dispute. A.2.10 - Statement Of Rebuttal (Core) - Core GovOps provides the Statement of Response to the party that initiated the dispute resolution process. They have three (3) working days to submit a Statement of Rebuttal. A.2.10 - Decision (Core) - The documents herein define the decision process for dispute resolution. A.2.10 - Analysis By Core GovOps (Core) - Core GovOps prepares a confidential analysis of the dispute for the Core Facilitator. This analysis must include a summary of all relevant facts as far as it is possible to ascertain, clear identification of any areas of factual ambiguity or disagreement between the parties, a structured presentation of the arguments in favor of each party, and a recommendation if Core GovOps believes one conclusion is clearly supported by the facts.
