7b43d159:c33ada595dd2223ed3e30df670dccc8.content: The net amount due to or from a Prime Agent in an Initial Calculation is a Disputed Amount if it is not an Agreed Amount.

7b43d159:2c7ad775a8eb18e1ad2b98997a98a83.title: Independent Calculation By Core Council Risk Advisor On Behalf Of Core Council
7b43d159:2c7ad775a8eb18e1ad2b98997a98a83.content: Within seven (7) calendar days of the end of each month, the Core Council Risk Advisor replies to the Monthly Settlement Cycle Post with their own independent calculation of the net amounts due to or from each Prime Agent (the “Independent Calculation”). The Independent Calculation must contain reasonable supporting detail. The required contents of the Independent Calculation will be further specified in a future iteration of the Atlas.

154b4d27:72a95e807799eba68425ad92b1d32dd.title: stUSDS Accessibility Reward
154b4d27:72a95e807799eba68425ad92b1d32dd.content: The stUSDS Distribution Reward is an incentive mechanism, similar to the USDS Accessibility Reward, designed to encourage Prime Agents and Integrators to promote stUSDS adoption. See A.2.4 - Distribution Reward Primitive. It is calculated as a percentage of the stUSDS balance associated with a Reward Code. The reward is initially set at 0.05% for the Integrator portion and 0.05% for the Prime Agent Management Fee, totaling 0.1%.

154b4d27:84e522270df6e40acd667aede26db62.title: Modification Of stUSDS Auction Parameters
154b4d27:84e522270df6e40acd667aede26db62.content: A clear justification and analysis must be provided to validate any proposed changes to the `Calc`, `Tau`, `Buf`, `Cusp`, `Tail`, `Chip`, `Tip`, `Chop`, or `Hole` parameters. Before these changes are added to an Executive Vote, the Core Executor Agents must obtain approval through a Governance Poll. However, in an emergency, the Core Executor Agents have the authority to bypass the Governance Poll and add the proposed parameters directly to an Executive Vote. These parameters must be regularly monitored and updated if needed.

154b4d27:1648b5fb921bfcce65921a455239457.title: stUSDS Bounded External Access Module
154b4d27:1648b5fb921bfcce65921a455239457.content: The stUSDS Bounded External Access Module (stUSDS BEAM) enables designated, Governance-whitelisted operators to adjust the stUSDS Rate (`str`), the SKY Borrow Rate (`dut`y), the maximum amount that users can deposit into the stUSDS contract (`cap`), and the maximum Debt Ceiling (`line`). Adjustments are governed by the stUSDS BEAM smart contract logic and specific parameters set by Sky Governance. stUSDS BEAM holds four parameters that can be set for each stUSDS parameter: (i) `min`, (ii) `max`, (iii) `step`, and (iv) `tau`.

154b4d27:18c367789fdf07c8bc683b2f3ff756e.title: Modification Of stUSDS Risk Parameters
154b4d27:18c367789fdf07c8bc683b2f3ff756e.content: Except as specified in A.4.4 - Modification Of stUSDS Auction Parameters, the Core Executor Agents, in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor, have the ability to modify any of the parameters defined in A.4.4 - stUSDS Risk Parameters. The modification of said parameters is pursuant to the Operational Weekly Cycle and can be effected directly via an Executive Vote, without requiring a Governance Poll.

154b4d27:44cbbe90761353c4b9bcc5222c6c88d.title: Definitions
154b4d27:44cbbe90761353c4b9bcc5222c6c88d.content: The documents herein define the parameters of the stUSDS BEAM.

-   Liquidation Ratio: 125%
-   `Calc`: StairstepExponentialDecrease

-   `Tolerance`: 0.5
-   `Cut`: 0.99
-   `Step`: 60 seconds
-   `Buf`: 120%
-   `Cusp`: 40%
-   `Tail`: 6,000 seconds
-   `Chip`: 0.1%
-   `Stopped`: 3
-   `Tip`: 300 USDS
-   `Chop`: 13%
-   `Hole`: 250,000
-   `Dust`: 30,000

154b4d27:4d5046db31ef1c2278faf57db96dc3d.title: Min Definition
154b4d27:4d5046db31ef1c2278faf57db96dc3d.content: The `min` parameter defines the minimum value for the `str` and `duty` parameters that can be set using the stUSDS BEAM. Each of the `str` and `duty` parameters has a specific `min`.

154b4d27:821c7c5a1b5a06bd9183eea90558c82.title: Implementation
154b4d27:821c7c5a1b5a06bd9183eea90558c82.content: The documents herein define the initial implementation of the Monthly Settlement Cycle. This initial implementation of the Monthly Settlement Cycle does not include the Senior Risk Capital System, which is still being developed, and funds continue to be allocated through the modified Treasury Management Function. See A.2.5 - Treasury Management - Treasury Management - Short Term Transitionary Measures.

154b4d27:e7850873b8492572d1eaab74883a04a.title: Operational Processes
154b4d27:e7850873b8492572d1eaab74883a04a.content:
The Monthly Settlement Cycle (MSC) synchronizes several key operational processes across the ecosystem, including:

1.  Sky Protocol's net revenue from the previous month is calculated and allocated through the steps of the Treasury Management Function. See A.2.5.
2.  The monthly Senior Risk Capital (SRC) origination process is settled: the clearing price is established, costs are deducted from winning Prime Agents' accounts, and their accounts are credited with Originated SRC (OSRC) for the upcoming month. See 3.3 - Settlement Of Origination.
3.  Queued conversions between USDS and srUSDS within the SRC system are processed. See A.3.3 - Deposit And Redemption Queues.
4.  Pioneer Incentive Pools are funded with an amount equivalent to the Sky Savings Rate multiplied by the balance of Unrewarded USDS. See A.2.4 - Pioneer Chain Primitive.
5.  The Smart Burn Buffer's burning operation occurs synchronously with each Monthly Settlement Cycle. At each cycle, the system calculates the appropriate Burn Rate based on current market conditions and executes the burn operation, if applicable, according to the formula specified in the Atlas. See A.2.5 - Treasury Management - Treasury Management - Allocation Steps - Step 4: Smart Burn And Standard Activity Staking Rewards - Smart Burn Buffer - Usage Of Smart Burn Buffer.
6.  Critical Core GovOps functions related to the operationalization of Sky Primitives are executed, including payment/reimbursement processing, compliance monitoring, and the calculation and application of retroactive penalties.

154b4d27:2ad260d7ac07348bacd446a878d5e8d.title: True Up In Subsequent Monthly Settlement Cycle
154b4d27:2ad260d7ac07348bacd446a878d5e8d.content:
If the amounts of any payments included in the Sky Core Executive Vote (see A.2.6 - Settlement Through Sky Core Executive Vote) are subsequently determined to be incorrect, adjustments are included in the next Monthly Settlement Cycle to ensure that each party pays the amount it owes or receives the amount to which it is entitled.

Core GovOps Atlas Axis must prepare a statement specifying the errors, the correct amounts, and the adjustments needed (the “Correction Calculation”). The Correction Calculation must be posted to the Sky Forum under the “Sky Core” category with the \`monthly-settlement-cycle\` tag. The required contents of the Correction Calculation will be further specified in a future iteration of the Atlas.

154b4d27:4a45c7e72187523aac38134982c0be3.title: Ethereum LayerZero Freezer Multisig Usage Standards
154b4d27:4a45c7e72187523aac38134982c0be3.content:
The Ethereum LayerZero Freezer Multisig can only be used in urgent or emergency situations (e.g., potential code exploits). Such situations are characterized by the fact that 1) they have the potential to harm the Sky Ecosystem or its users; and 2) the preparation time required for an Executive Vote would leave the ecosystem vulnerable to harm (e.g., an exploit).

The multisig should be used to prevent technical vulnerabilities; prevent unwanted functionality of the smart contracts or corresponding parts of the system (e.g., price oracles); or prevent unwanted usage of the smart contracts or corresponding parts of the system which deviates from intended behavior.

The Core Council must ensure that use of the multisig is generally aligned and specifically accords with these requirements.

7b43d159:76eac278dcc0aecb59f77fefb05c76f.title: Disputes By Prime Agents
7b43d159:76eac278dcc0aecb59f77fefb05c76f.content:
A Prime Agent may dispute the calculation of the net amount due to or from it (a "Dispute Notice"). The Dispute Notice must be posted as a reply to the Monthly Settlement Cycle Post within five (5) calendar days of the posting of the Initial Calculation or Independent Calculation being disputed. The Dispute Notice must specify the errors in the Initial Calculation or Independent Calculation and the Prime's own calculation of the net amount due to or from it. The required contents of the Dispute Notice will be further specified in a future iteration of the Atlas.

Core GovOps may at its discretion resolve the differences between the calculations using the process specified in A.2.6 - Final Calculation By Core GovOps. Alternatively, Core GovOps may elect to determine the correct amount and true up any differences in the next Monthly Settlement Cycle as specified in A.2.6 - True Up In Subsequent Monthly Settlement Cycle. In either case Core GovOps must post its decision as a reply to the Dispute Notice.

7b43d159:3e8347837ec04f323a4fe60bedc0d7d.title: Final Amount
7b43d159:3e8347837ec04f323a4fe60bedc0d7d.content: The net amount due to or from a Prime Agent in a Final Calculation is a Final Amount.

7b43d159:a547f74fad8916babee55137612f8eb.title: Settlement Through Sky Core Executive Vote
7b43d159:a547f74fad8916babee55137612f8eb.content: When Core GovOps has posted the Final Calculation then the Core Facilitator must include payments of these amounts in the next Sky Core Executive Vote as specified herein.

a3b60814:d1c097cceec5a8c72dbfee8c0c62cc6.title: Process Flow
a3b60814:d1c097cceec5a8c72dbfee8c0c62cc6.content: The process flow is defined herein.• The Prime Agent identifies an opportunity to drive USDS adoption through an Accessibility Reward to either 1) reward an existing Integrator for driving USDS adoption or 2) incentivize a new actor to onboard as an Integrator to drive USDS adoption.• Existing Integrators ◦ The Prime Agent and the third party, if applicable, develop a plan to track USDS utilization attributable to the actor using either on-chain or off-chain data.• Prospective Integrators ◦ Near Term process: • The Prospective Integrator must first apply to the Integrator program and be approved by Viridian Advisors per A.2.4 - Near Term Process. Post approval, Viridian Advisors issues a Reward Code to the Integrator. • The Prime Agent and the third party develop a plan to track USDS utilization attributable to the actor using either on-chain or off-chain data. ◦ Long Term process: • The Prospective Integrator must first apply to the Integrator program and be approved by Operational GovOps pursuant to A.2.4 - Long Term Process. Post approval, Operational GovOps issues a Reward Code to the Integrator. • The Prime Agent develops a plan to track USDS utilization attributable to it using either on-chain or off-chain data. Where applicable, the plan should include how the Prime Agent will support the prospective Integrator in including the Reward Code in their on-chain infrastructure.• The Prime Agent may also be (or choose to be) an Integrator itself and deploy a Reward Code on its frontend to earn the Accessibility Reward. ◦ Near Term process: • If the Prime Agent is not already an approved Integrator, it must apply to the Program and be approved by Viridian Advisors. Post approval, Viridian Advisors issues a Reward Code to the Prime Agent. • The Prime Agent develops a plan to track USDS utilization attributable to it using either on-chain or off-chain data. ◦ Long Term process: • The Prime Agent must first apply to the Integrator program and be approved by Operational GovOps pursuant to A.2.4 - Long Term Process. Post approval, Operational GovOps issues a Reward Code to the Prime Agent. • The Prime Agent develops a plan to track USDS utilization attributable to it using either on-chain or off-chain data.

a3b60814:66264874179baebbae01e0096cf72b7.title: Dependencies

66dcdb78:64701fa25eb21273d9ce1fac3b09428.title: Process Flow
66dcdb78:64701fa25eb21273d9ce1fac3b09428.content: The process flow is defined herein.• The Prime Agent identifies an opportunity to drive USDS adoption through an Distribution Reward to either 1) reward an existing Integrator for driving USDS adoption or 2) incentivize a new actor to onboard as an Integrator to drive USDS adoption.• Existing Integrators ◦ The Prime Agent and the third party, if applicable, develop a plan to track USDS utilization attributable to the actor using either on-chain or off-chain data.• Prospective Integrators ◦ Near Term process: • The Prospective Integrator must first apply to the Integrator program and be approved by Viridian Advisors per A.2.4 - Near Term Process. Post approval, Viridian Advisors issues a Reward Code to the Integrator. • The Prime Agent and the third party develop a plan to track USDS utilization attributable to the actor using either on-chain or off-chain data. ◦ Long Term process: • The Prospective Integrator must first apply to the Integrator program and be approved by Operational GovOps pursuant to A.2.4 - Long Term Process. Post approval, Operational GovOps issues a Reward Code to the Integrator. • The Prime Agent develops a plan to track USDS utilization attributable to it using either on-chain or off-chain data. Where applicable, the plan should include how the Prime Agent will support the prospective Integrator in including the Reward Code in their on-chain infrastructure.• The Prime Agent may also be (or choose to be) an Integrator itself and deploy a Reward Code on its frontend to earn the Accessibility Reward. ◦ Near Term process: • If the Prime Agent is not already an approved Integrator, it must apply to the Program and be approved by Viridian Advisors. Post approval, Viridian Advisors issues a Reward Code to the Prime Agent. • The Prime Agent develops a plan to track USDS utilization attributable to it using either on-chain or off-chain data. ◦ Long Term process: • The Prime Agent must first apply to the Integrator program and be approved by Operational GovOps pursuant to A.2.4 - Long Term Process. Post approval, Operational GovOps issues a Reward Code to the Prime Agent. • The Prime Agent develops a plan to track USDS utilization attributable to it using either on-chain or off-chain data.

a3b60814:1648b5fb921bfcce65921a455239457.title: stUSDS Bounded External Access Module
a3b60814:1648b5fb921bfcce65921a455239457.content: The stUSDS Bounded External Access Module (stUSDS BEAM) enables designated, Governance-whitelisted operators to adjust the stUSDS Rate (`str`), the SKY Borrow Rate (`dut`y), the maximum amount that users can deposit into the stUSDS contract (`cap`), and the maximum Debt Ceiling (`line`). Adjustments are governed by the stUSDS BEAM smart contract logic and specific parameters set by Sky Governance. stUSDS BEAM holds four parameters that can be set for each stUSDS parameter: (i) `min`, (ii) `max`, (iii) `step`, and (iv) `tau`.

a3b60814:4d5046db31ef1c2278faf57db96dc3d.title: Min Definition
a3b60814:4d5046db31ef1c2278faf57db96dc3d.content: The `min` parameter defines the minimum value for the `str` and `duty` parameters that can be set using the stUSDS BEAM. Each of the `str` and `duty` parameters has a specific `min`.

a3b60814:b9ca14c7a632453ddb0661dcc5e975f.title: stUSDS Accessibility Reward
a3b60814:b9ca14c7a632453ddb0661dcc5e975f.content: The stUSDS Accessibility Reward is an incentive mechanism, similar to the USDS Accessibility Reward, designed to encourage Prime Agents and Integrators to promote stUSDS adoption. See A.2.4 - Accessibility Reward Primitive. It is calculated as a percentage of the stUSDS balance associated with a Reward Code. The reward is initially set at 0.05% for the Integrator portion and 0.05% for the Prime Agent Management Fee, totaling 0.1%.

a3b60814:0c7778ff61dd9eff867c40e242b0d07.title: Max Definition
a3b60814:0c7778ff61dd9eff867c40e242b0d07.content: The `max` parameter defines the maximum value for the `str` and `duty` parameters that can be set using the stUSDS BEAM. Each of the `str` and `duty` parameters has a specific `max`.

a3b60814:84e522270df6e40acd667aede26db62.title: Modification Of stUSDS Auction Parameters
a3b60814:84e522270df6e40acd667aede26db62.content: A clear justification and analysis must be provided to validate any proposed changes to the `Calc`, `Tau`, `Buf`, `Cusp`, `Tail`, `Chip`, `Tip`, `Chop`, or `Hole` parameters. Before these changes are added to an Executive Vote, the Core Executor Agents must obtain approval through a Governance Poll. However, in an emergency, the Core Executor Agents have the authority to bypass the Governance Poll and add the proposed parameters directly to an Executive Vote. These parameters must be regularly monitored and updated if needed.

a3b60814:e7a2f8a85640708bce4486bfe72ab7c.title: Step Definition
a3b60814:e7a2f8a85640708bce4486bfe72ab7c.content: The `step` parameter limits how much the `str` and `duty` parameters can be increased or decreased in a single transaction, bound by the `tau` parameter. Each of the `str` and `duty` parameters has a specific `step`.

a3b60814:26920901b9db6df0dc2e0910efc2142.title: Parameters
a3b60814:26920901b9db6df0dc2e0910efc2142.content:
The current Target Risk Tolerance Ratio is 90%.

This parameter will be maintained in parallel with the value specified in the Spark Artifact Allocation System Primitive section at Spark's Operation Of Spark Liquidity Layer And Agreement Regarding Risk Tolerance Ratio; any change to one section of the Spark Artifact will require a corresponding change in the other section.

a3b60814:3ae341cf818218a184abdc327c6edfc.title: Operational Process
a3b60814:3ae341cf818218a184abdc327c6edfc.content:
Spark governance and contributors must take immediate action to reduce the Risk Tolerance Ratio when it exceeds the Target Risk Tolerance Ratio level. These actions may fall into two categories, risk capital actions or allocation system actions.

Risk capital actions are actions Spark takes to increase Total Risk Capital, including increasing Internal Junior Risk Capital, sourcing External Junior Risk Capital from other Prime Agents or tokenized sources, or sourcing External Senior Risk Capital from Sky or tokenized sources.

Allocation system actions involve adjusting the capital allocations within the Spark instance of the Allocation System to reduce Required Risk Capital, such as unwinding or disposing of assets requiring higher levels of risk capital as a percent of exposure.

The operational processes implemented at Spark will meet or exceed the requirements specified in the Sky Atlas at A.2.4 - Primes' Total Risk Capital (TRC) Management.

a3b60814:45c9f163ca4f81c79960570747bb0c9.title: Spark Savings Configuration
a3b60814:45c9f163ca4f81c79960570747bb0c9.content: The documents herein specify Spark's strategy and operational processes for managing parameters and liquidity for the Spark Savings protocol.

a3b60814:5061e70aefe0e1d7ed2416e5876deb4.title: Definition
a3b60814:5061e70aefe0e1d7ed2416e5876deb4.content: The Risk Tolerance Ratio is defined as the ratio of Spark's Required Risk Capital (RRC) to Total Risk Capital (TRC), as these terms are defined in the Sky Atlas Stability Scope (A.3.3 - Risk Tolerance Ratio). Spark will seek to maintain a Risk Tolerance Ratio not greater than the Target Risk Tolerance Ratio specified in Parameters.

a3b60814:304de431b7be4cb74fa349d6979e1d6.title: Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module
a3b60814:304de431b7be4cb74fa349d6979e1d6.content: The Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module (SP-BEAM) enables designated, Governance-whitelisted operators to adjust the Stability Fees of supported vault types, the Dai Savings Rate (DSR), and the Sky Savings Rate (SSR). Adjustments are governed by the SP-BEAM smart contract logic and specific parameters set by Sky Governance. SP-BEAM holds four parameters that can be set for each vault type or savings rate: (i) `min`, (ii) `max`, (iii) `step`, and (iv) `tau`.

a3b60814:644804224769890e3581ebc2be0fe40.title: Min Definition
a3b60814:644804224769890e3581ebc2be0fe40.content: The `min` parameter defines the minimum value for rates in basis points that can be set using the Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module. Each rate parameter added to the SP-BEAM has a specific `min`.
ancestors: Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module

a3b60814:5efd561fd0c74af976c6224b0013b91.title: Updates
a3b60814:5efd561fd0c74af976c6224b0013b91.content: If not otherwise specified, Core GovOps, in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor, has the ability to modify any of the parameters defined in A.3.9 - Measures For Endgame Transition - Native Vault Engine - Risk Parameter Definitions for any of the Vault Types in A.3.9 - Measures For Endgame Transition - Native Vault Engine - Vault Types. As a general rule, the modification of said parameters is pursuant to the Operational Weekly Cycle and can be effected directly via an Executive Vote, without requiring a Governance Poll. Exceptions to this general rule must be clearly stated in the relevant Atlas document.

a3b60814:e420bf4320f1bcc038f605a2b01fad9.title: Max Definition
a3b60814:e420bf4320f1bcc038f605a2b01fad9.content: The `max` parameter defines the maximum value for rates in basis points that can be set using the Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module. Each rate parameter added to the SP-BEAM has a specific `max`.
ancestors: Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module

a3b60814:045a4b3620144299ff1e9a647082d79.title: Oracles
a3b60814:045a4b3620144299ff1e9a647082d79.content:
The Native Vault Engine collateral types of ETH, STETH, WBTC will specifically use the Chronicle v3 oracle solution, until at least January 1st 2026. The Native Vault Engine collateral types must be migrated to the new version of the Chronicle v3 oracle when it is feasible to do so.

Other oracle solutions, including diversified oracles, will only be considered until January 1st, 2026, and only if there are unresolvable security concerns with the Chronicle v3 oracles.

a3b60814:0c152188c0dc8650b410857c2a6e244.title: Max Technical Upper Limit
a3b60814:0c152188c0dc8650b410857c2a6e244.content: Although the `max` parameter can be set higher, the SP-BEAM cannot be used to set a rate higher than 50% (5,000 basis points) due to technical limitations. Attempts to use the SP-BEAM in this manner will revert. To avoid confusion, `max` should not be set to a value higher than 50% (5,000 basis points).
ancestors: Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module

a3b60814:b32305df602bf0788f6a157c75ace9b.title: Conditions For The Pre-launch Token Rewards
a3b60814:b32305df602bf0788f6a157c75ace9b.content: Spark has a pre-launch token rewards program based on the usage of its lending platform. Users of the platform will receive an airdrop of SPK tokens, depending on how much and how long they have used the platform during the pre-launch token reward period. These rewards are only for users on Ethereum Mainnet. There are two seasons of the Spark pre-launch token rewards: Season 1 and Season 2. Season 1 of pre-launch token rewards was active from August 20 2023 and lasted for nine months, ending on May 20 2024. 130,434,783 SPK tokens were allocated in this period. In Season 2 14,478,261 SPK will be rewarded per month to SparkLend users who qualify for the airdrop. Season 2 is an additional pre-farming period, which runs until the Spark Agent launches as part of Sky Endgame launch season. The monthly SPK rewards are allocated as follows:◦ 80 % is allocated to users borrowing DAI and/or USDS◦ 20 % is allocated to users supplying ETHThe proposed full anti-cheat SPK Airdrop for SparkLend is calculated using the following formula:Airdrop = 80% \* (DAI Borrows + USDS Borrows - sDAI Supplies \* sDAI Liquidation Threshold - sUSDS Supplies \* sUSDS Liquidation Threshold) + 20% \* (ETH Supplies - ETH Borrows / ETH Liquidation Threshold)All supplies and borrows are denominated in USD based on the on-chain oracle price at that block to determine the conversion.

a3b60814:fae420fa16bcf7e93b469a0044a610f.title: Special Pre-launch Token Reward Programs
a3b60814:fae420fa16bcf7e93b469a0044a610f.content: Spark can activate a new SPK token pre-launch token reward airdrop program to capture other growth opportunities. The program can last until the moment SPK launches, or a shorter duration. When activated, the exact details of the special pre-launch token reward airdrop program must be specified in Special Pre-launch Token Reward Program Details. The SPK tokens for the future Spark Airdrop are allocated between all borrowers based on a formula announced by Spark and specified in the above cited document. The rate of SPK tokens being earned is 7,239,130 SPK per month, distributed on a per block basis proportional to the formula specified in the above cited document.

a3b60814:edb33474d30012737b1be0cadbf0d20.content:
The SPK Company Ltd account will transfer all of the SPK tokens held by it, other than the tokens specified in Transfer Of Tokens For Token Launch, to the Spark Foundation. The SPK Company Ltd account is specified in Minting Of Tokens To SPK Company Ltd.

The address of the Spark Foundation on the Ethereum Mainnet is `0x92e4629a4510AF5819d7D1601464C233599fF5ec`.

a3b60814:1bf2bb1fee90dff81bdf3f7e4421643.content: The Instances of the Spark Liquidity Layer with `Active` Status are stored herein. The `RRC Framework Full Implementation` status defines whether the Instance Financial RRC is calculated based on a fully implemented risk model (see A.3.3 - Fully Implemented Risk Models) or a pending risk model (see A.3.3 - Pending Risk Models). If the Instance Financial RRC is calculated based on a fully implemented risk model the status is `Covered`. 66dcdb78:c52cea2bb60e453403ffa59049a8fff.title: Call CancelMapleRedemption Function
66dcdb78:c52cea2bb60e453403ffa59049a8fff.content:
Only an operator with the relayer role can cancel a previously requested redemption of shares from Maple. To do so, they must call the `cancelMapleRedemption` function on the Controller contract on mainnet, providing the Maple token address and the number of shares to cancel. All Maple cancellations of redemption operations are performed on behalf of the ALM Proxy. Calling this function will carry out the following actions:

-   The contract will confirm the relayer status of the operator. If the caller does not have the relayer role, the transaction will revert.
-   The contract will check that a rate limit exists for the asset. If no rate limit exists the transaction will revert.
-   The contract will submit a cancellation request to the vault, removing the specified number of shares from the pending redemption.

The function call is as follows:

```

              function cancelMapleRedemption(address mapleToken, uint256 shares) external

```

66dcdb78:4c9b1747edd89ad4bd39d2e91c5dffb.title: Call RequestMapleRedemption Function
66dcdb78:4c9b1747edd89ad4bd39d2e91c5dffb.content:
Only an operator with the relayer role can request the redemption of shares from Maple. To do so, they must call the `requestMapleRedemption` function on the Controller contract on mainnet, providing the Maple token address and the number of shares to request. All Maple redemption operations are performed on behalf of the ALM Proxy and the destination address is always set to the proxy by the contract. Calling this function will carry out the following actions:

-   The contract will confirm the relayer status of the operator. If the caller does not have the relayer role, the transaction will revert.
-   The contract will ensure the redemption amount is within the allowed rate limit for the specified vault and decrease the rate limit for the redemption amount.
-   The contract will submit a redemption request to the vault. Assets will not be received immediately; they must be claimed in a separate step after the vault processes the redemption.

The function call is as follows:

```

              function requestMapleRedemption(address mapleToken, uint256 shares) external

```

a3b60814:474ed85d62ae82664cf6eb271533f3e.title: Compliance With Local Laws And Regulations As A Condition Precedent To Integrators Receiving Accessibility Rewards
a3b60814:474ed85d62ae82664cf6eb271533f3e.content:
This document and its subdocuments define the jurisdictional compliance rules applicable to Integrators that operate user-facing frontends that integrate with, and thus offer access to, the Sky Protocol and receive Accessibility Rewards. Integrators are solely responsible for complying with all relevant legal and regulatory requirements related to their participation in the Integrator Program. Integrators represent and warrant that their participation and activities under the Integrator Program are and will remain in full compliance with all applicable laws and regulations.

In connection with integrating with, and thereby providing access to, the Sky Protocol, Integrators must operate their frontends and infrastructure in compliance with all relevant legal and regulatory requirements in the jurisdictions applicable to their services. This requires compliance with all relevant legal and regulatory requirements in relation to frontend operations, marketing, and promotions in the jurisdictions where the Integrator provides access to the Sky Protocol through the integration.

An Integrator's right to participate in the Integrator Program is contingent upon its ongoing compliance with all applicable laws and regulations.

a3b60814:690ad2a7deedff4e2f94dd3399fc876.title: Alignment
a3b60814:690ad2a7deedff4e2f94dd3399fc876.content: The Integrator must be aligned with Sky's overall strategy regarding promoting adoption of USDS. In the near term, this determination of a prospective or current Integrator's alignment with Sky's overall strategy is made by Operational GovOps in consultation with Ecosystem Actor Viridian Advisors. In the future Operational GovOps may make this determination themselves or consult with another actor to do so. Sky Core may choose whether to maintain an Integrator's Reward Code in its sole and absolute discretion.

a3b60814:6b671b977ff8c287ae5fa5166515ff9.title: Consequence For Integrator Non-Compliance With Local Laws And Regulations
a3b60814:6b671b977ff8c287ae5fa5166515ff9.content: Sky Ecosystem Governance, in its absolute and unilateral discretion, retains the right to withhold, revoke, or demand immediate repayment of any and all Accessibility Rewards from any Integrator that is determined, suspected, or alleged to be in violation of the Atlas or any legal, regulatory, or other obligations associated with its integration with, and provision of access to, the Sky Protocol.

a3b60814:739b3fa6fbb05bcb8a44f8f51dbe3ec.title: Integrator Requirements
a3b60814:739b3fa6fbb05bcb8a44f8f51dbe3ec.content: The documents herein define the requirements for Integrators.

a3b60814:fb7b75036e3c05fe5c71b0a906fc76a.title: Removal From Integrator Program
a3b60814:fb7b75036e3c05fe5c71b0a906fc76a.content: If Sky Governance removes an Integrator from the Integrator Program, Operational GovOps must remove the Integrator from the list of Current Integrators in A.2.4 - List Of Current Integrators and deactivate the Instances of the Accessibility Reward and Integration Boost Primitive associated with them.

a3b60814:162689087e9f2142d905952147f8138.content: Integrators are actors that offer access to the Sky Protocol via their frontends or infrastructure. a3b60814:5dc8c526fe585e63b3d758c7f104f81.title: Accessibility Reward Strategy
a3b60814:5dc8c526fe585e63b3d758c7f104f81.content: Launch Agent 3's strategy with respect to the Accessibility Reward Primitive is to encourage the broad adoption of USDS by bridging into new communities and DeFi platforms, thereby earning and distributing Accessibility Rewards for USDS balances facilitated through its frontend. Prospective partners should demonstrate strong alignment with Launch Agent 3's mission, and offer clear pathways to engage new user bases and support the sustainable growth of USDS across diverse ecosystems. The guiding criteria are as follows:- **Shared Mission Alignment:** Partners must demonstrate a commitment to promoting user-friendly stablecoin usage and responsible financial empowerment.- **Clear Synergy:** The collaboration should enhance USDS accessibility, by offering either a unique distribution channel or a robust incentive model. - **Community Benefit**: Proposed partnerships should deliver tangible rewards or advantages that resonate with Sky's user base. - **Scalability & Compliance:** Potential integrations should have the capacity to handle increased demand and adhere to the risk management guidelines described in the Atlas.

a3b60814:4918cc27ececc714d4e9fcbb7e9663d.title: Sky Primitives Strategy
a3b60814:4918cc27ececc714d4e9fcbb7e9663d.content: The documents herein define Launch Agent 3's strategic intent with respect to certain Sky Primitives.

a3b60814:e1eb943d16f7afa0fcdc57051907902.title: Integration Boost Strategy
a3b60814:e1eb943d16f7afa0fcdc57051907902.content: Launch Agent 3's strategy with respect to the Integration Boost Primitive is to deliver a "Sky Savings Rate" (or similar program) to USDS users across selected DeFi platforms. This approach aims to extend the reach of USDS by tapping into fresh communities and expanding its overall market presence. New collaborations should exhibit compatibility with Launch Agent 3's accessibility ethos, showcase steady on-chain activity, and present clear opportunities to onboard broader user segments into the Launch Agent 3 ecosystem. The guiding criteria are as follows:- **Long-Term Viability:** Target platforms must exhibit strong on-chain activity and a track record of stability.- **Aligned Incentives:** Collaborations should offer meaningful yield enhancements that support the broader Sky mission.- **Growth Potential:** Partners must show clear prospects for sustainable scaling, ensuring that users can benefit from ongoing improvements.

a3b60814:ccb72598cad4806fc4b0f486f4a557f.title: Agent-Specific Emergency Response
a3b60814:ccb72598cad4806fc4b0f486f4a557f.content: The documents herein specify Launch Agent 3's emergency response protocol in situations solely impacting Launch Agent 3 versus the broader Sky Ecosystem. This protocol will be specified in a future iteration of the Launch Agent 3 Artifact.

a3b60814:9998838e1f7bf80f53ec38276e41e38.title: Core Governance Reward Strategy
a3b60814:9998838e1f7bf80f53ec38276e41e38.content: Launch Agent 3's strategy with respect to the Core Governance Reward Primitive is to provide continuous, secure, and user-friendly governance frontend hosting for SKY holders, ensuring critical decision-making processes remain accessible and reliable over time. The guiding criteria are as follows:- **Security & Reliability:** The Prime Agent will uphold robust security measures and maintain high availability to prevent disruptions or unauthorized access.- **Governance Framework Alignment:** Any updates to the frontend should integrate smoothly with Launch Agent 3's existing governance mechanisms, preserving uninterrupted voting and proposal workflows.

a3b60814:9122ad15b4d6220a7cb09674a22328f.title: Sky Ecosystem Emergency Response
a3b60814:9122ad15b4d6220a7cb09674a22328f.content: The documents herein specify Launch Agent 3's emergency response protocol in situations that impact the entire Sky Ecosystem. This protocol will be specified in a future iteration of the Launch Agent 3 Artifact.

a3b60814:9c3631536b1c4c3a20113df7da887bc.title: Launch Agent 4
a3b60814:9c3631536b1c4c3a20113df7da887bc.content: The documents herein specify all of the logic for Launch Agent 4, including Launch Agent 4's strategy and how it uses the Sky Primitives to operationalize this strategy.

a3b60814:ec3578fbca2c6fa8c127578c69b08e8.title: Introduction
a3b60814:ec3578fbca2c6fa8c127578c69b08e8.content: Launch Agent 4 is an "incubator" Agent operationalizing a turnkey solution for the Sky Ecosystem's development and deployment of Prime and Halo Agents. This will give Agent founders a streamlined pathway to establish, build, operationalize, fundraise, and launch new Agents. The overall goal of the Launch Agent 4 Agent is to produce Agents for the Sky Ecosystem at scale, supporting cohorts of new Agent founders through leveraging rich content, workstreams and turnkey services for legal, risk, tech, and operational requirements.

a3b60814:eab32b6137d5f58fff51a9eed8aee3a.title: Governance Accessibility Rewards Paid To Prime Agents
a3b60814:eab32b6137d5f58fff51a9eed8aee3a.content: 0.5% of Step 1 Capital is allocated to Prime Agents that manage the rewards for Governance Integrators, incentivizing the active participation of Prime Agents. See A.2.5 - Treasury Management - Treasury Management - Allocation Steps - Step 1: Security and Stability Maintenance - Governance Accessibility Rewards Paid To Integrators.

a3b60814:f95d85532de23b1c9c2a29a71599e7d.title: Governance Accessibility Rewards Paid To Integrators
a3b60814:f95d85532de23b1c9c2a29a71599e7d.content: 0.5% of Step 1 Capital is allocated to frontends and other Integrators that facilitate accessible governance, following security and information standards specified in the Atlas. These standards will be specified in a future iteration of the Atlas. See A.2.4 - Core Governance Reward Primitive.

a3b60814:9f3eef5c1781c063ad161e7e4db7fd3.title: Step 2: High Activity Staking Rewards
a3b60814:9f3eef5c1781c063ad161e7e4db7fd3.content: 5% of the Step 2 Capital is allocated to High Activity Staking Rewards (”HASR”) as specified in the documents herein. The remaining 95% of Step 2 Capital becomes Step 3 Capital.

a3b60814:dcc71e080c0f5a97b84b59ab85176c9.title: Voluntary Reduction By Aligned Delegates
a3b60814:dcc71e080c0f5a97b84b59ab85176c9.content: Aligned Delegates may agree to voluntarily reduce their compensation in order to incentivize SKY holders to delegate to them. To the extent that Aligned Delegates reduce their compensation, Step 2 Capital is increased by a corresponding amount. The mechanism by which Aligned Delegates may agree to reduce their compensation will be specified in a future iteration of the Atlas.

a3b60814:20bf8eeb257dfc45f2e3da9373f3070.title: Purpose
a3b60814:20bf8eeb257dfc45f2e3da9373f3070.content: High Activity Staking Rewards provide a boosted staking reward to SKY stakers that delegate their SKY through compliant Governance Accessibility frontends and provide feedback to their delegates every three (3) months. This ensures that there is a minimum amount of SKY that is always actively following current events and governance to detect potential misalignment or buildup of hidden risks.

a3b60814:189c5bcbb7ac8afbe12e1f40865c137.title: Aligned Delegates
a3b60814:189c5bcbb7ac8afbe12e1f40865c137.content: Up to 1% of Step 1 Capital is allocated to Aligned Delegates.

a3b60814:f00f2441e3d63b99815b2cb90b7c2e5.title: Funding Of High Activity Staking Rewards Buffer
a3b60814:f00f2441e3d63b99815b2cb90b7c2e5.content: 5% of the Step 2 Capital is allocated to funding the High Activity Staking Rewards Buffer (HASRB) linearly over the course of the month. Funds from the High Activity Staking Rewards Buffer are then paid out to Governance Accessibility Integrators as specified in A.2.5 - Treasury Management - Treasury Management - Allocation Steps - Step 2: High Activity Staking Rewards - Payout From High Activity Staking Rewards Buffer. Governance Accessibility Integrators are in turn responsible for distributing those funds to High Activity Stakers as specified in A.2.5 - Treasury Management - Treasury Management - Allocation Steps - Step 2: High Activity Staking Rewards - High Activity Staker Qualification.

a3b60814:d2558fc23ac4c47182628f609d1153f.title: Sourcing Of Internal Senior Risk Capital
a3b60814:d2558fc23ac4c47182628f609d1153f.content: ISRC is sourced from the various surplus buffers, which are themselves funded via the Treasury Management Function. See A.2.5 - Treasury Management - Treasury Management - Allocation Steps.

a3b60814:a8889b4517480087bac6511450d9dad.title: Senior Risk Capital System Implementation
a3b60814:a8889b4517480087bac6511450d9dad.content: The documents herein define operational requirements and protocols for the implementation of the Senior Risk Capital system in the Risk Framework.

a3b60814:d19b35ce957b47bdb586359f9341123.title: External Senior Risk Capital And srUSDS System
a3b60814:d19b35ce957b47bdb586359f9341123.content: The documents herein define rules and infrastructure pertaining to the sourcing of External Senior Risk Capital (ESRC). ESRC is capital provided by external investors to be invested as Senior Risk Capital of Prime Agents.

a3b60814:0407f9abc9ce30ea38568683768a68a.title: Tokenized External JRC System Implementation
a3b60814:0407f9abc9ce30ea38568683768a68a.content: This document will be further developed in a future iteration of the Atlas.

a3b60814:a6e408a09137c19c6cc7be5e32d2144.title: srUSDS Contract
a3b60814:a6e408a09137c19c6cc7be5e32d2144.content: srUSDS is the tokenized form of External Senior Risk Capital. Users can deposit USDS into the srUSDS contract to provide External Senior Risk Capital to the SRC system, making it available for origination by Prime Agents. See A.3.3 - Senior Risk Capital (SRC) Origination Process. srUSDS holders can potentially earn higher yields in exchange for the risk that the External Senior Risk Capital will suffer losses.

a3b60814:f8c3ca8df24b2ce6938d81c5de17e56.title: Prime External JRC Rental System Implementation
a3b60814:f8c3ca8df24b2ce6938d81c5de17e56.content: The implementation of the PEJRC rental system is defined as a Sky Primitive, specifically, the Junior Risk Capital Rental Primitive. See A.2.4 - Junior Risk Capital Rental Primitive.

a3b60814:56aa24cf6045d7494e38b56777663b3.title: Deposit And Redemption Queues
a3b60814:56aa24cf6045d7494e38b56777663b3.content:
The srUSDS contract utilizes distinct queues for managing conversions. Users can add USDS to the deposit queue for conversion into srUSDS; or add srUSDS to the redemption queue for conversion back into USDS at any point during the month.

Assets placed in either queue can be withdrawn by the user at any time before the Monthly Settlement Cycle begins.

At the Monthly Settlement Cycle, all assets remaining in the queues are processed: queued USDS is converted into srUSDS, and queued srUSDS is converted into USDS based on the prevailing Conversion Rate. See A.3.3 - Conversion Rate.

a3b60814:3d617bbf1d0f57b32ed950a33ba1d68.title: Treasury Management Function-Derived Voting Rewards
a3b60814:3d617bbf1d0f57b32ed950a33ba1d68.content: USDS rewards are distributed via two distinct mechanisms based on the staker's activity level: the High Activity Staking Reward (HASR) and the Standard Activity Staking Reward (SASR). SASR is the base reward when funding from the Treasury Management Function is available; HASR is an additional boost reserved for High-Activity wallets. See A.2.5 - Treasury Management - Treasury Management - Allocation Steps - Step 2: High Activity Staking Rewards - Payout From High Activity Staking Rewards Buffer.

a3b60814:9dcff0e858ec349f038642b30be3f32.title: Sources of Voting Rewards
a3b60814:9dcff0e858ec349f038642b30be3f32.content: SKY stakers are eligible to receive voting rewards sourced from the Sky Treasury Management Function (TMF) or the Agent Token Distribution mechanism defined in A.4.5.

a3b60814:ce90d8d08aad98fcaa351c3ff1cb658.title: Activity Levels
a3b60814:ce90d8d08aad98fcaa351c3ff1cb658.content: At the Monthly Settlement Cycle, all SKY-staking wallets are tagged as High Activity or Standard Activity, pursuant to the criteria defined in A.2.5 - Treasury Management - Treasury Management - Allocation Steps - Step 2: High Activity Staking Rewards - High Activity Staker Qualification and A.2.5 - Treasury Management - Treasury Management - Allocation Steps - Step 4: Smart Burn And Standard Activity Staking Rewards - Standard Activity Staking Rewards - Standard Activity Staker Qualification. Only High Activity wallets share HASR; both High and Standard Activity wallets share SASR.

a3b60814:bfb838bcab76bf54c14bf8554fb6555.title: SKY Staking Voting Rewards
a3b60814:bfb838bcab76bf54c14bf8554fb6555.content: The documents herein define the SKY Staking Voting Rewards. SKY stakers may choose between receiving USDS or Agent Token rewards.

a3b60814:14629e34d62c931a9f40a4d9305ad3b.title: High Activity Staking Rewards
a3b60814:14629e34d62c931a9f40a4d9305ad3b.content: The High Activity Staking Rewards (HASR) is a boosted reward provided to High Activity wallets. The HASR amount is distributed each monthly cycle pro-rata to the SKY stake of all High Activity wallets. High Activity wallets receive SASR (when funding is available) plus their separate HASR boost.

a3b60814:d317ed8ba7c3e5f67c4f521b192aec8.title: SKY Staking
a3b60814:d317ed8ba7c3e5f67c4f521b192aec8.content: SKY holders can stake their tokens via the SKY Staking Mechanism available on Ethereum Mainnet and SkyLink Deployments. SKY stakers earn voting rewards sourced from the Sky Treasury Management Function. In lieu of USDS rewards and SKY rewards, SKY stakers can choose to earn Agent Token Rewards, including SPK and the tokens of other Prime Agents incubated by Sky. SKY stakers can also borrow USDS against their staked collateral using the SKY-backed borrowing mechanism defined herein.

a3b60814:dfed3689377817397d2daee88790534.title: Standard Activity Staking Rewards
a3b60814:dfed3689377817397d2daee88790534.content: The Standard Activity Staking Rewards (SASR) is the base reward shared by all wallets with Standard Activity status or higher. When funding is available, the SASR amount is distributed each monthly cycle pro‑rata to the SKY stake of every Standard or High Activity wallet.

a3b60814:f9cb1bf72c34baa363b85da2d713a18.title: Burning of Existing Tokens
a3b60814:f9cb1bf72c34baa363b85da2d713a18.content: At the same time that no new SKY tokens are issued, SKY tokens are bought back and burned on a regular basis, using a portion of the Net Revenue of the Protocol as dictated by the Treasury Management Function. See A.2.5 - Treasury Management - Treasury Management - Allocation Steps - Step 4: Smart Burn And Standard Activity Staking Rewards - Smart Burn Buffer. As a result, the total supply of SKY tokens will continue to decrease over time.

a3b60814:6a29cdfab859f079bfee76cab4b38ae.title: No New Token Emissions
a3b60814:6a29cdfab859f079bfee76cab4b38ae.content: No new SKY tokens may be emitted except for (1) emissions required to recapitalize the protocol if it is at risk of insolvency (see A.3.7) and (2) temporary emissions that are being deprecated and fully offset by corresponding burns, resulting in no net increase to the intended long-term token supply (see A.4.1 - Core Tokens - SKY - Deprecated Emissions Mechanisms).

a3b60814:f55b2e2516ad444e9cf0e0fef9c1e27.title: Deprecated Emissions Mechanisms
a3b60814:f55b2e2516ad444e9cf0e0fef9c1e27.content: The subdocuments herein define legacy mechanisms involving the issuance of new SKY tokens. Each of these mechanisms is being deprecated. While these mechanisms do not increase the net supply of SKY tokens, they must be replaced with solutions that do not involve any emissions of SKY tokens, as defined in the documents herein.

a3b60814:8e096f853f67e1b3e85305db451caff.title: Initial Token Supply
a3b60814:8e096f853f67e1b3e85305db451caff.content: The initial token supply of SKY tokens is derived from the total number of legacy MKR tokens as of the launch of Sky, multiplied by the conversion ratio of 24,000. SKY is the exclusive governance token of the Sky Protocol and takes over all governance and economic rights previously held by MKR. See A.4.1 - Core Tokens - SKY - MKR To SKY Upgrade Approval.

a3b60814:3f99688ecf247c4be2db3e074a2c578.title: SKY Token Rewards Emissions
a3b60814:3f99688ecf247c4be2db3e074a2c578.content:
USDS users are able to earn SKY Rewards. See A.4.3 - A2 - Savings Rate And Token Reward Mechanism - Token Reward Mechanism. These rewards are currently funded by emissions of new SKY tokens.

These ongoing emissions will be eliminated and replaced with a solution that funds these rewards using SKY held by the Sky Protocol.

At the same time that this new solution is implemented, SKY tokens equal to the total SKY emissions previously used to fund SKY Rewards, including the Early Bird Reward (see A.5.5 - Accessibility Campaigns - Early Bird Reward - Token Distribution), will be burned from SKY held by the Sky Protocol.

The combination of these actions will achieve a state where the number of total SKY tokens is exactly the same as if SKY Rewards had never been funded with protocol emissions.

a3b60814:f6c774566b7008c34e23d5e79fcbd13.title: Deflationary Tokenomics
a3b60814:f6c774566b7008c34e23d5e79fcbd13.content: The documents herein set forth the core deflationary tokenomics of the SKY token.

a3b60814:f977747484c6161df45a61c4092d915.title: MKR To SKY Conversion Emissions
a3b60814:f977747484c6161df45a61c4092d915.content:
The legacy MKR to SKY conversion contract (Legacy Conversion Contract) burns MKR and mints new SKY. The new MKR to SKY conversion contract (New Conversion Contract) instead burns MKR and issues SKY from the existing supply of preminted SKY.

The Legacy Conversion Contract will be disabled as specified in 4.1 - Core Tokens - SKY - Disabling Legacy Conversion Contract. To offset SKY minted by the Legacy Conversion Contract after the deployment of the New Conversion Contract, an equivalent amount of preminted SKY will be burned. This action will ensure the total SKY token supply remains as if these specific emissions from the Legacy Conversion Contract had not occurred.

a3b60814:8f38c99b2ff7bc65290b75e9e11e72f.title: Net Revenue
a3b60814:8f38c99b2ff7bc65290b75e9e11e72f.content: Net Revenue is equal to Income minus Expenses. Income is defined in A.2.5 - Treasury Management - Treasury Management - Allocation Steps - Step 0: Net Revenue - Income. Expenses are defined in A.2.5 - Treasury Management - Treasury Management - Allocation Steps - Step 0: Net Revenue - Expenses. Income and Expenses are defined such that Net Revenue must always be positive.

a3b60814:4a20fea9b55350f384632241d2bba57.title: Step 0: Net Revenue
a3b60814:4a20fea9b55350f384632241d2bba57.content: The sole function of Step 0 is to establish the Net Revenue of the Sky Protocol. It performs no allocations to downstream functions or buffers, unlike subsequent steps for which this Net Revenue serves as the input.

a3b60814:4885672d7a302965a2e0a827a81548d.title: Income
a3b60814:4885672d7a302965a2e0a827a81548d.content: The documents herein define each of the components of the Income of the Sky Protocol. These components are added together to arrive at total Income.

a3b60814:5c9a20ac0192932ef5805678349af21.title: Allocation Steps
a3b60814:5c9a20ac0192932ef5805678349af21.content: The documents herein define the allocation steps of the Sky Treasury Management Function. The process is divided into steps beginning with Net Revenue. These steps form a “waterfall” with each previous step needing to be fully funded before any funds can be allocated to later steps.

a3b60814:947f32bb3768e5bef89834f7668dbe9.title: Stability Fees From Base Rate
a3b60814:947f32bb3768e5bef89834f7668dbe9.content: Stability Fees are the fees that Sky Core charges Prime Agents to borrow from Sky. See A.3.2 - Core Stability Parameters - Parameters - Base Rate. Sky Core's legacy ALM infrastructure is currently being transferred to Prime Agents; during this transition period and until this transfer is fully complete, income generated from the Sky Core Collateral Portfolio contributes to net revenue. See A.3.4 - Application To Sky Core.

a3b60814:8eb274e094519504cf6ca26c4f14496.title: Integration With Monthly Settlement Cycle
a3b60814:8eb274e094519504cf6ca26c4f14496.content: The Sky Treasury Management Function is synchronized with the Monthly Settlement Cycle. See A.2.6. At the conclusion of each MSC, the Net Revenue of the Sky Protocol for the preceding month is calculated and allocated according to the waterfall process defined in A.2.5 - Treasury Management - Treasury Management - Allocation Steps.

a3b60814:0dbad7e3ef24d378cfa5c7e6190255a.title: Internal Senior Risk Capital Income
a3b60814:0dbad7e3ef24d378cfa5c7e6190255a.content: Internal Senior Risk Capital income is the revenue attributed to Sky from the total payments made by Primes for Originated Senior Risk Capital (OSRC). ISRC itself comprises surplus capital allocated from designated buffers funded by the Sky Treasury Management Function. While Primes pay a single clearing price for their OSRC based on the monthly Origination Process, the total revenue received by Sky is subsequently allocated proportionally, with the portion corresponding to ISRC's share of the Total Senior Risk Capital (TSRC) pool designated as ISRC Income. See A.2.5 - Treasury Management - Treasury Management - Sourcing Of Internal Senior Risk Capital From Surplus Buffers.

a3b60814:98aba395ec57913052bf359d5746082.title: Step 1: Security and Stability Maintenance
a3b60814:98aba395ec57913052bf359d5746082.content: All of the Net Revenue from Step 0 (A.2.5 - Treasury Management - Treasury Management - Allocation Steps - Step 0: Net Revenue) becomes Step 1 Capital. 10% of Step 1 Capital is allocated for security and stability maintenance as specified in the documents herein. The remaining 90% of Step 1 Capital becomes Step 2 Capital and is allocated as specified in A.2.5 - Treasury Management - Treasury Management - Allocation Steps - Step 2: High Activity Staking Rewards.

a3b60814:43ed002638270af336f2e8585530b2d.title: Pioneer Rewards
a3b60814:43ed002638270af336f2e8585530b2d.content: Pioneer Rewards are paid to Pioneer Primes as specified in A.2.4 - Pioneer Incentive Pool.

a3b60814:7812badcb556e289ab2c0592a6a82f5.title: Core Executor Budget
a3b60814:7812badcb556e289ab2c0592a6a82f5.content: Up to 5% of Step 1 Capital is allocated to the Core Executor Budget. This budget funds active Core Executor Agents responsible for the continuous improvement of the Atlas, including the risk management framework and other critical components.

a3b60814:4db913837f05b847f104e609aef7fa0.title: Reimbursement Rewards
a3b60814:4db913837f05b847f104e609aef7fa0.content: Reimbursement Rewards are paid to Prime Agents to reimburse them for the costs of building common infrastructure used by the entire Sky Ecosystem, such as Token SkyLink deployments.

a3b60814:9744da70403ce3f070cf486541d096d.title: Voluntary Reduction By Core Executor Agents
a3b60814:9744da70403ce3f070cf486541d096d.content: The Core Executor Agents may agree to voluntarily reduce their budget below 5% when applying for a Core Executor Slot in order to increase their chances of being elected to a Core Executor Slot. To the extent that Core Executor Agents reduce their budget, Step 2 Capital is increased by a corresponding amount. The mechanism by which Core Executor Agents are elected will be specified in a future iteration of the Atlas.

a3b60814:9bdf8ff6ac98ec1718c8e45776ca26d.title: Accessibility Rewards
a3b60814:9bdf8ff6ac98ec1718c8e45776ca26d.content: The Accessibility Reward is paid to Prime Agents and third-party partners that drive adoption of USDS. See A.2.4 - Accessibility Reward Primitive.

a3b60814:269bb84289abad601c609668bbb8f07.title: Core Executor Reward
a3b60814:269bb84289abad601c609668bbb8f07.content: Up to 3% of Step 1 Capital is allocated to Core Executor Agents whose terms have ended in the last four (4) years. This incentivizes Core Executor Agents to increase the long term profitability of the Sky Ecosystem during their Core Executor Slot terms, as the Core Executor Reward is a percentage of future Net Revenue.

a3b60814:baca4f85ec292adc80d6de38e1d8384.title: Agent Token Distribution Voting Rewards
a3b60814:baca4f85ec292adc80d6de38e1d8384.content: SKY stakers are eligible to receive Agent Token rewards as specified in A.4.5. At the Monthly Settlement Cycle, Agent Tokens are distributed pro‑rata, by staked SKY, among wallets that have opted to receive a specific Agent Token for the cycle. To qualify for Agent Token payout a wallet must satisfy the Standard Activity criteria specified in A.2.5 - Treasury Management - Treasury Management - Allocation Steps - Step 4: Smart Burn And Standard Activity Staking Rewards - Standard Activity Staking Rewards - Payout From Standard Activity Staking Rewards Buffer.

66dcdb78:91e15fb4a95a5a45345f0c07b6624e2.title: Governance Distribution Rewards Paid To Prime Agents
66dcdb78:91e15fb4a95a5a45345f0c07b6624e2.content: 0.5% of Step 1 Capital is allocated to Prime Agents that manage the rewards for Governance Integrators, incentivizing the active participation of Prime Agents. See A.2.5 - Treasury Management - Treasury Management - Allocation Steps - Step 1: Security and Stability Maintenance - Governance Distribution Rewards Paid To Integrators.

66dcdb78:f95d85532de23b1c9c2a29a71599e7d.title: Governance Distribution Rewards Paid To Integrators
66dcdb78:f95d85532de23b1c9c2a29a71599e7d.content: 0.5% of Step 1 Capital is allocated to frontends and other Integrators that facilitate accessible governance, following security and information standards specified in the Atlas. These standards will be specified in a future iteration of the Atlas. See A.2.4 - Core Governance Reward Primitive.

66dcdb78:9f3eef5c1781c063ad161e7e4db7fd3.title: Step 2: High Activity Staking Rewards
66dcdb78:9f3eef5c1781c063ad161e7e4db7fd3.content: 5% of the Step 2 Capital is allocated to High Activity Staking Rewards (”HASR”) as specified in the documents herein. The remaining 95% of Step 2 Capital becomes Step 3 Capital.

66dcdb78:dcc71e080c0f5a97b84b59ab85176c9.title: Voluntary Reduction By Aligned Delegates
66dcdb78:dcc71e080c0f5a97b84b59ab85176c9.content: Aligned Delegates may agree to voluntarily reduce their compensation in order to incentivize SKY holders to delegate to them. To the extent that Aligned Delegates reduce their compensation, Step 2 Capital is increased by a corresponding amount. The mechanism by which Aligned Delegates may agree to reduce their compensation will be specified in a future iteration of the Atlas.

66dcdb78:20bf8eeb257dfc45f2e3da9373f3070.title: Purpose
66dcdb78:20bf8eeb257dfc45f2e3da9373f3070.content: High Activity Staking Rewards provide a boosted staking reward to SKY stakers that delegate their SKY through compliant Governance Accessibility frontends and provide feedback to their delegates every three (3) months. This ensures that there is a minimum amount of SKY that is always actively following current events and governance to detect potential misalignment or buildup of hidden risks.

66dcdb78:189c5bcbb7ac8afbe12e1f40865c137.title: Aligned Delegates
66dcdb78:189c5bcbb7ac8afbe12e1f40865c137.content: Up to 1% of Step 1 Capital is allocated to Aligned Delegates.

66dcdb78:f00f2441e3d63b99815b2cb90b7c2e5.title: Funding Of High Activity Staking Rewards Buffer
66dcdb78:f00f2441e3d63b99815b2cb90b7c2e5.content: 5% of the Step 2 Capital is allocated to funding the High Activity Staking Rewards Buffer (HASRB) linearly over the course of the month. Funds from the High Activity Staking Rewards Buffer are then paid out to Governance Accessibility Integrators as specified in A.2.5 - Treasury Management - Treasury Management - Allocation Steps - Step 2: High Activity Staking Rewards - Payout From High Activity Staking Rewards Buffer. Governance Accessibility Integrators are in turn responsible for distributing those funds to High Activity Stakers as specified in A.2.5 - Treasury Management - Treasury Management - Allocation Steps - Step 2: High Activity Staking Rewards - High Activity Staker Qualification.

a3b60814:91b304336e9ae794a3a50256bf9577a.title: stUSDS Accessibility Reward Definition
a3b60814:91b304336e9ae794a3a50256bf9577a.content: stUSDS Accessibility Reward is defined in A.4.4 - SKY Staking Mechanism - SKY Staking - SKY-Backed Borrowing - stUSDS Accessibility Reward.

a3b60814:928eac95e041c9c7bb2d16497232d57.title: Sky Savings Rate Definition
a3b60814:928eac95e041c9c7bb2d16497232d57.content: Sky Savings Rate is defined in A.3.2 - Core Stability Parameters - Parameters - Sky Savings Rate.

a3b60814:ec3101bcd9f99273c2361a449bc50c2.title: stUSDS Risk Parameters
a3b60814:ec3101bcd9f99273c2361a449bc50c2.content:
The liquidation parameters for SKY-backed loans funded via stUSDS are:

-   Liquidation Ratio: 125%
-   `Calc`: StairstepExponentialDecrease
-   `Tau`: 0 days
-   `Tolerance`: 0.5
-   `Cut`: 0.99
-   `Step`: 60 seconds
-   `Buf`: 120%
-   `Cusp`: 40%
-   `Tail`: 6,000 seconds
-   `Chip`: 0.1%
-   `Stopped`: 3
-   `Tip`: 300 USDS
-   `Chop`: 13%
-   `Hole`: 250,000
-   `Dust`: 30,000

a3b60814:1d62327c1e63b18efdbf78fbe7d1957.title: Parameters Definition
a3b60814:1d62327c1e63b18efdbf78fbe7d1957.content: The parameters of the SKY Borrow Minimum Rate formula are further defined in the documents herein.

a3b60814:18c367789fdf07c8bc683b2f3ff756e.title: Modification Of stUSDS Risk Parameters
a3b60814:18c367789fdf07c8bc683b2f3ff756e.content: Except as specified in A.4.4 - Modification Of stUSDS Auction Parameters, the Core Executor Agents, in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor, have the ability to modify any of the parameters defined in A.4.4 - stUSDS Risk Parameters. The modification of said parameters is pursuant to the Operational Weekly Cycle and can be effected directly via an Executive Vote, without requiring a Governance Poll.

a3b60814:e7135f4b5eecaad0f28fb889506089e.title: SKY Borrow Minimum Rate
a3b60814:e7135f4b5eecaad0f28fb889506089e.content:
The SKY Borrow Minimum Rate is calculated according to the following formula:

```

            SKY Borrow Minimum Rate = Sky Savings Rate + stUSDS Accessibility Reward
```

The formula ensures the SKY Borrow Minimum Rate covers the baseline cost of capital (Sky Savings Rate) plus the incentive cost (stUSDS Accessibility Reward), preventing value-draining arbitrage where users could borrow below the Sky Savings Rate.

a3b60814:54100bad725bcd872f08eee20040a66.title: stUSDS Function
a3b60814:54100bad725bcd872f08eee20040a66.content: stUSDS is a yield-bearing token representing USDS deposited into the stUSDS contract. Its primary function is to provide segregated risk capital for the SKY-backed borrowing mechanism. Users convert USDS to stUSDS to provide this capital and earn the stUSDS Rate. See A.4.4 - SKY Staking Mechanism - SKY Staking - SKY-Backed Borrowing - stUSDS Rate. stUSDS can be converted back to USDS subject to available unutilized liquidity in the stUSDS converter contract.

a3b60814:938e1035312d7d7113ce41c26fa9c41.title: SKY-Backed Borrowing
a3b60814:938e1035312d7d7113ce41c26fa9c41.content: SKY stakers can borrow USDS against their staked SKY collateral. This borrowing will be facilitated exclusively by the stUSDS system which will provide protocol-independent, or segregated, risk capital. The stUSDS system is currently in development; its elements are outlined in the subdocuments below. During the transition period to the stUSDS system, the protocol-dependent SKY-backed borrowing system remains operational and is governed by A.4.4 - SKY Staking Mechanism - SKY Staking - Short Term Transitionary Measures.

a3b60814:2a61ae9c09218a6b88f97a5f32c1745.title: stUSDS Rate
a3b60814:2a61ae9c09218a6b88f97a5f32c1745.content:
The variable yield earned by stUSDS holders is calculated using the formula:

```

            stUSDS Rate = Sky Savings Rate + (SKY Borrow Rate - SKY Borrow Minimum Rate) * Utilization - Rfactor * f(Utilization)
```

a3b60814:f0e762e7dd6dab7224bc44406e492e2.title: Parameters Definition
a3b60814:f0e762e7dd6dab7224bc44406e492e2.content: The parameters of the stUSDS Rate formula are further defined in the documents herein.

a3b60814:490fb53057fcf8276a47a761199de44.title: Sky Savings Rate Definition
a3b60814:490fb53057fcf8276a47a761199de44.content: `Sky Savings Rate` is the Sky Savings Rate defined in A.3.2 - Core Stability Parameters - Parameters - Sky Savings Rate.

66dcdb78:b987cec0f960e8b51207d58a221e04d.title: stUSDS Distribution Reward Definition
66dcdb78:b987cec0f960e8b51207d58a221e04d.content: stUSDS Distribution Reward is defined in A.4.4 - SKY Staking Mechanism - SKY Staking - SKY-Backed Borrowing - stUSDS Accessibility Reward.

66dcdb78:928eac95e041c9c7bb2d16497232d57.title: Sky Savings Rate Definition
66dcdb78:928eac95e041c9c7bb2d16497232d57.content: Sky Savings Rate is defined in A.3.2 - Core Stability Parameters - Parameters - Sky Savings Rate.

66dcdb78:1d62327c1e63b18efdbf78fbe7d1957.content: The parameters of the SKY Borrow Minimum Rate formula are further defined in the documents herein.

66dcdb78:18c367789fdf07c8bc683b2f3ff756e.title: Modification Of stUSDS Risk Parameters
66dcdb78:18c367789fdf07c8bc683b2f3ff756e.content: Except as specified in A.4.4 - Modification Of stUSDS Auction Parameters, the Core Executor Agents, in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor, have the ability to modify any of the parameters defined in A.4.4 - stUSDS Risk Parameters. The modification of said parameters is pursuant to the Operational Weekly Cycle and can be effected directly via an Executive Vote, without requiring a Governance Poll.

66dcdb78:e7135f4b5eecaad0f28fb889506089e.title: SKY Borrow Minimum Rate
66dcdb78:e7135f4b5eecaad0f28fb889506089e.content:
The SKY Borrow Minimum Rate is calculated according to the following formula:

```

            SKY Borrow Minimum Rate = Sky Savings Rate + stUSDS Accessibility Reward
```

The formula ensures the SKY Borrow Minimum Rate covers the baseline cost of capital (Sky Savings Rate) plus the incentive cost (stUSDS Accessibility Reward), preventing value-draining arbitrage where users could borrow below the Sky Savings Rate.

66dcdb78:84e522270df6e40acd667aede26db62.title: Modification Of stUSDS Auction Parameters
66dcdb78:84e522270df6e40acd667aede26db62.content: A clear justification and analysis must be provided to validate any proposed changes to the `Calc`, `Tau`, `Buf`, `Cusp`, `Tail`, `Chip`, `Tip`, `Chop`, or `Hole` parameters. Before these changes are added to an Executive Vote, the Core Executor Agents must obtain approval through a Governance Poll. However, in an emergency, the Core Executor Agents have the authority to bypass the Governance Poll and add the proposed parameters directly to an Executive Vote. These parameters must be regularly monitored and updated if needed.

a3b60814:cf21073ea2832423b8448b92a7badf1.title: Risk Tolerance Ratio
a3b60814:cf21073ea2832423b8448b92a7badf1.content: The Risk Tolerance Ratio for a Prime Agent is the ratio of its Aggregate Required Risk Capital to its Total Risk Capital.

a3b60814:9bb5fc3128bdf31b20894b489e3b789.title: Financial Penalties For Breach Of Capital Requirements
a3b60814:9bb5fc3128bdf31b20894b489e3b789.content: The documents herein define the financial penalties for breaches of Risk Capital requirements.

a3b60814:81a0e26513da8f92e8d67aacf53956c.title: Severity Of Breaches
a3b60814:81a0e26513da8f92e8d67aacf53956c.content: The financial penalties for breaches of Risk Capital requirements depend on whether the breaches are Low Severity or High Severity. The documents herein define Low Severity and High Severity Breaches. The financial penalties associated with High Severity Breaches and Low Severity Breaches are defined in A.3.3 - Financial Penalties For Low Severity Breaches and A.3.3 - Financial Penalties For High Severity Breaches, respectively.

a3b60814:c72d6bb9385b4ab34f697404edee9e5.title: Penalty Mechanisms For Prime Agents
a3b60814:c72d6bb9385b4ab34f697404edee9e5.content: The documents herein specify the penalty mechanisms for Prime Agents for breaches of the Risk Capital requirements.

a3b60814:088019becbd39f4b904586aef4cea2e.title: Low Severity Breach Definition
a3b60814:088019becbd39f4b904586aef4cea2e.content: A Low Severity Breach is one in which the Risk Tolerance Ratio is greater than or equal to 100% but less than 103%.

a3b60814:c1100caa7f15d57f70294c3a4bb2a9d.title: Penalty Mechanisms
a3b60814:c1100caa7f15d57f70294c3a4bb2a9d.content: The documents herein specify the penalty mechanisms that exist to incentivize Prime Agents and Operational Agents to ensure that sufficient capital is always held against investments by Prime Agents and to protect Sky from risks due to insufficient capital.

a3b60814:a479145d5ffeaf626310050afd5b08b.title: High Severity Breach Definition
a3b60814:a479145d5ffeaf626310050afd5b08b.content: A High Severity Breach is one in which the Risk Tolerance Ratio is greater than 103%.

66dcdb78:56a6c8fdc33ac504307a18186759276.title: Encumbrance Ratio
66dcdb78:56a6c8fdc33ac504307a18186759276.content: The Encumbrance Ratio for a Prime Agent is the ratio of its Aggregate Required Risk Capital to its Total Risk Capital.

66dcdb78:9bb5fc3128bdf31b20894b489e3b789.title: Financial Penalties For Breach Of Capital Requirements
66dcdb78:9bb5fc3128bdf31b20894b489e3b789.content: The documents herein define the financial penalties for breaches of Risk Capital requirements.

66dcdb78:81a0e26513da8f92e8d67aacf53956c.title: Severity Of Breaches
66dcdb78:81a0e26513da8f92e8d67aacf53956c.content: The financial penalties for breaches of Risk Capital requirements depend on whether the breaches are Low Severity or High Severity. The documents herein define Low Severity and High Severity Breaches. The financial penalties associated with High Severity Breaches and Low Severity Breaches are defined in A.3.3 - Financial Penalties For Low Severity Breaches and A.3.3 - Financial Penalties For High Severity Breaches, respectively.

66dcdb78:c72d6bb9385b4ab34f697404edee9e5.title: Penalty Mechanisms For Prime Agents
66dcdb78:c72d6bb9385b4ab34f697404edee9e5.content: The documents herein specify the penalty mechanisms for Prime Agents for breaches of the Risk Capital requirements.

66dcdb78:d30423203d90b3d4a51b4657a572141.title: Low Severity Breach Definition
66dcdb78:d30423203d90b3d4a51b4657a572141.content: A Low Severity Breach is one in which the Encumbrance Ratio is greater than or equal to 100% but less than 103%.

66dcdb78:c1100caa7f15d57f70294c3a4bb2a9d.title: Penalty Mechanisms
66dcdb78:c1100caa7f15d57f70294c3a4bb2a9d.content: The documents herein specify the penalty mechanisms that exist to incentivize Prime Agents and Operational Agents to ensure that sufficient capital is always held against investments by Prime Agents and to protect Sky from risks due to insufficient capital.

66dcdb78:ac99515e40f28a261d661d38f431877.title: High Severity Breach Definition
66dcdb78:ac99515e40f28a261d661d38f431877.content: A High Severity Breach is one in which the Encumbrance Ratio is greater than 103%.

a3b60814:2ad260d7ac07348bacd446a878d5e8d.title: True Up In Subsequent Monthly Settlement Cycle
a3b60814:2ad260d7ac07348bacd446a878d5e8d.content:
If the amounts of any payments included in the Sky Core Executive Vote (see A.2.6 - Settlement Through Sky Core Executive Vote) are subsequently determined to be incorrect, adjustments are included in the next Monthly Settlement Cycle to ensure that each party pays the amount it owes or receives the amount to which it is entitled.

Core GovOps Atlas Axis must prepare a statement specifying the errors, the correct amounts, and the adjustments needed (the “Correction Calculation”). The Correction Calculation must be posted to the Sky Forum under the “Sky Core” category with the \`monthly-settlement-cycle\` tag. The required contents of the Correction Calculation will be further specified in a future iteration of the Atlas.

a3b60814:25c21e6f4baf1cd274801652d5a5e09.title: Communication Channels And Media Assets
a3b60814:25c21e6f4baf1cd274801652d5a5e09.content:

a3b60814:ae4147d498a07c97eafafbacab904b0.title: Following Actions
a3b60814:ae4147d498a07c97eafafbacab904b0.content: Parameter changes designed to offboard users, such as changes to the liquidation ratio or stability fee, can only be implemented once 14 calendar days have passed following a second public announcement.

a3b60814:d85163dcb390f9621e9ac35446799f8.title: Expedited Offboarding
a3b60814:d85163dcb390f9621e9ac35446799f8.content: The subdocuments herein define an expedited offboarding process in the event a collateral type needs to be removed quickly due to security or solvency concerns.

a3b60814:646116e4d3cc0a9ab430c19622f5090.title: Immediate Actions
a3b60814:646116e4d3cc0a9ab430c19622f5090.content:
Upon approval by Sky Governance to offboard a permissionless collateral type or vault type, the following actions are taken as soon as is practicable:

-   Set debt ceiling to zero (0) Dai or USDS.
-   Make an initial public announcement on all communication channels listed in A.3.9 - Measures For Endgame Transition - Offboarding Process - Communication Channels And Media Assets Listing.
-   Make a second public announcement on all communication channels in the above cited document no later than 14 calendar days after the initial public announcement.
-   Once the second public announcements have been made, set the liquidation penalty to 0%.

a3b60814:97bfe50ac7aada470ae1595c8b14ef9.title: Requirements
a3b60814:97bfe50ac7aada470ae1595c8b14ef9.content:
When a collateral type threatens the security or solvency of the Sky Protocol, an expedited offboarding is in order. Expedited offboardings override the timeline specified in A.3.9 - Measures For Endgame Transition - Offboarding Process - Technical Process and allow the immediate modification of all relevant parameters.

Expedited offboardings must proceed pursuant to the following requirements:

-   The Offboarding Proposal must state that the offboarding should be expedited due to an emergency or urgent concern, as defined in A.1.8 - Emergency Response System - Emergency Response - Definition Of Emergency Situations.
-   The Offboarding Proposal must explicitly reference this Atlas document.

a3b60814:72c50560bb027dcf041fb9ec5737302.title: Technical Process
a3b60814:72c50560bb027dcf041fb9ec5737302.content: The subdocuments herein specify actions to be taken by specific actors within Sky when offboarding a vault type.

a3b60814:c02d300c432c78e764f92c5d7f59710.title: Announcements
a3b60814:c02d300c432c78e764f92c5d7f59710.content: The public announcements defined in A.3.9 - Measures For Endgame Transition - Offboarding Process - Technical Process must still be carried out. However, the timing of these announcements no longer constrains the modification of parameters. These announcements must also state that the offboarding is being expedited and explain the reasons for this accelerated process.

a3b60814:32033baf84d089d9c99b34192db3e99.content:
