a3b60814:732ea1c1b6cc05452f37a6589638d8f.title: Sky Savings Rate Paid Through Integration Boost
a3b60814:732ea1c1b6cc05452f37a6589638d8f.content: The Integration Boost provides the equivalent of the Sky Savings Rate to users of decentralized finance protocols who hold USDS balances. See A.2.4 - Integration Boost Primitive.

a3b60814:2b82fc5a0a7570b994816e1574782f9.title: Sky Savings Rate Paid to sUSDS Holders
a3b60814:2b82fc5a0a7570b994816e1574782f9.content: The Sky Savings Rate is the interest expense paid to sUSDS holders on their balances. It also includes interest paid to sDai holders on their balances.

a3b60814:348d0a2cec4c45fc4d99fb3ca5be3e7.title: Expenses
a3b60814:348d0a2cec4c45fc4d99fb3ca5be3e7.content: The documents herein define each of the components of Expenses. These components are added together to arrive at total Expenses.

a3b60814:ec31cec070e0b6d5acff55ecc327e40.title: srUSDS Accessibility Reward
a3b60814:ec31cec070e0b6d5acff55ecc327e40.content: Prime Agents and third-party partners that drive srUSDS usage are entitled to a srUSDS Accessibility Reward similar to the Accessibility Reward paid on USDS balances. The srUSDS Accessibility Reward Fee is the same as the Accessibility Reward Fee on USDS. See A.2.4 - Accessibility Reward Primitive.

a3b60814:d5532ba5cbf33b2f280a956bc779a88.title: ESRC Earnings Fee
a3b60814:d5532ba5cbf33b2f280a956bc779a88.content: Sky takes a 5% fee on the net interest earnings generated from the ESRC portion of originated SRC before these earnings are distributed to srUSDS holders via the conversion rate adjustment.

a3b60814:d5703e65aef96012e40af3f6e2c5d3d.title: Senior Risk Capital (SRC) Origination Process
a3b60814:d5703e65aef96012e40af3f6e2c5d3d.content: This document defines the operational details of the recurring monthly process allowing Prime Agents to originate Senior Risk Capital (Originated Senior Risk Capital or OSRC) from the Total Senior Risk Capital (TSRC) pool. The process involves determining the available TSRC supply, a bidding phase, an allocation auction, and settlement aligned with the Monthly Settlement Cycle.

a3b60814:0a752ca9129c7735b6f47716c5eb3ff.title: Sky Spread
a3b60814:0a752ca9129c7735b6f47716c5eb3ff.content: Sky takes a spread equal to the Sky Spread on all ESRC balances. The Sky Spread is the difference between (1) the rate at which Prime Agents borrow from Sky and (2) the Sky Savings Rate plus the Accessibility Reward Fee.

a3b60814:67220091402c22e606b940a3ccdcf0e.title: Process Timing and Schedule
a3b60814:67220091402c22e606b940a3ccdcf0e.content: The SRC origination process operates monthly, synchronized with the Monthly Settlement Cycle. The bidding window occurs during the current month for SRC that is usable in the next month; the bidding window closes before settlement processing begins. Additional operational details, including timelines, will be specified in a future iteration of the Atlas.

a3b60814:1c50aa1c8f57c8b1905ea0578708891.title: Sources Of Revenue To Sky
a3b60814:1c50aa1c8f57c8b1905ea0578708891.content: Sky earns revenue from facilitating ESRC from two sources. These sources are included in the formula and defined in the subdocuments below.

a3b60814:d9ede57a42bc57779ce38760c6a90b7.title: Available Total Senior Risk Capital Pool Determination
a3b60814:d9ede57a42bc57779ce38760c6a90b7.content: Total Senior Risk Capital (TSRC) is the amount of Senior Risk Capital that is available each Monthly Settlement Cycle for Primes to originate and thus turn into Originated Senior Risk Capital (OSRC) through the monthly origination process. TSRC is the sum of designated Internal Senior Risk Capital (ISRC) from Sky surplus buffers and available External Senior Risk Capital (ESRC) from the srUSDS contract. Prior to each monthly bidding window, the TSRC is calculated and publicly announced. Additional operational details will be defined in a future iteration of the Atlas.

66dcdb78:ebc638cb3341a751791455e95458b6d.title: Distribution Rewards
66dcdb78:ebc638cb3341a751791455e95458b6d.content: The Distribution Reward is paid to Prime Agents and third-party partners that drive adoption of USDS. See A.2.4 - Distribution Reward Primitive.

66dcdb78:732ea1c1b6cc05452f37a6589638d8f.title: Sky Savings Rate Paid Through Integration Boost
66dcdb78:732ea1c1b6cc05452f37a6589638d8f.content: The Integration Boost provides the equivalent of the Sky Savings Rate to users of decentralized finance protocols who hold USDS balances. See A.2.4 - Integration Boost Primitive.

66dcdb78:4db913837f05b847f104e609aef7fa0.title: Reimbursement Rewards
66dcdb78:4db913837f05b847f104e609aef7fa0.content: Reimbursement Rewards are paid to Prime Agents to reimburse them for the costs of building common infrastructure used by the entire Sky Ecosystem, such as Token SkyLink deployments.

66dcdb78:2b82fc5a0a7570b994816e1574782f9.title: Sky Savings Rate Paid to sUSDS Holders
66dcdb78:2b82fc5a0a7570b994816e1574782f9.content: The Sky Savings Rate is the interest expense paid to sUSDS holders on their balances. It also includes interest paid to sDai holders on their balances.

66dcdb78:43ed002638270af336f2e8585530b2d.title: Pioneer Rewards
66dcdb78:43ed002638270af336f2e8585530b2d.content: Pioneer Rewards are paid to Pioneer Primes as specified in A.2.4 - Pioneer Incentive Pool.

66dcdb78:348d0a2cec4c45fc4d99fb3ca5be3e7.title: Expenses
66dcdb78:348d0a2cec4c45fc4d99fb3ca5be3e7.content: The documents herein define each of the components of Expenses. These components are added together to arrive at total Expenses.

66dcdb78:98aba395ec57913052bf359d5746082.title: Step 1: Security and Stability Maintenance
66dcdb78:98aba395ec57913052bf359d5746082.content: All of the Net Revenue from Step 0 (A.2.5 - Treasury Management - Treasury Management - Allocation Steps - Step 0: Net Revenue) becomes Step 1 Capital. 10% of Step 1 Capital is allocated for security and stability maintenance as specified in the documents herein. The remaining 90% of Step 1 Capital becomes Step 2 Capital and is allocated as specified in A.2.5 - Treasury Management - Treasury Management - Allocation Steps - Step 2: High Activity Staking Rewards.

a3b60814:286a79af4987bc3d0032b1cc7836b7c.title: Accessibility Reward
a3b60814:286a79af4987bc3d0032b1cc7836b7c.content: The subdocuments herein set out agreed terms with respect to the Accessibility Reward.

a3b60814:007f8448dfd114c166569a753cdfb41.title: Recourse
a3b60814:007f8448dfd114c166569a753cdfb41.content: Sky's recourse for bad debt consists of (1) minting Prime Agent tokens; (2) terminating a Prime's right to further borrowing; and (3) activation of the Resolution Mechanism which includes, without limitation, the authority to suspend all protocol operations, seize or reallocate all of the Prime assets, override or disable smart contract functions, initiate managed restructuring, or execute full and permanent liquidation of the affected sub-protocol and all of its assets, in order to contain risk and preserve the stability and solvency of the broader ecosystem.

a3b60814:8b469c37967ad07fe04dbb14fc60fb3.title: Accessibility Reward Rate
a3b60814:8b469c37967ad07fe04dbb14fc60fb3.content: The standard Accessibility Reward rate is set at 0.2%. The Accessibility Reward is divided according to the subdocuments herein.

a3b60814:f7fec4808075d14a3e73441a70ca47c.title: Borrowing Above Subsidized Limit
a3b60814:f7fec4808075d14a3e73441a70ca47c.content: Spark and Grove can borrow amounts exceeding the 1,000,000,000 USDS limit at the prevailing Base Rate.

a3b60814:ce5b30d9da65f44fda3063b65b96948.title: Frontend Portion
a3b60814:ce5b30d9da65f44fda3063b65b96948.content: Up to a maximum of 50% of the Accessibility Reward rate is apportioned to frontends.

a3b60814:a3cedeef2bd22e474685af82f732019.title: Minimum Borrowing Threshold for Grant Eligibility
a3b60814:a3cedeef2bd22e474685af82f732019.content: Primes , including Spark and Grove, must each maintain a minimum borrowing of 1,000,000,000 USDS from Sky at all times to remain eligible for the full monthly reimbursement grant. If the amount borrowed falls below this threshold, the reimbursement grant will be proportionately slashed. This grant will cover the difference between the borrowing Base Rate and the T-bill rate. Spark and Grove can borrow amounts exceeding the 1,000,000,000 USDS limit at the prevailing Base Rate.

a3b60814:3bcdc87bb2e41c838ec301c318fd1cb.title: Prime Portion
a3b60814:3bcdc87bb2e41c838ec301c318fd1cb.content: A minimum of 50% of the Accessibility Reward rate is apportioned to Prime Agents. This percentage can be up to 100%, dependent on reduction from the Frontend Portion.

a3b60814:06203ba84f7e99a1835984520d1a4ca.title: Tokenomics
a3b60814:06203ba84f7e99a1835984520d1a4ca.content: The subdocuments herein set out agreed terms with respect to tokenomics.

a3b60814:b07a1ae994b5de9683381378e628b33.title: Accord Substantive Terms
a3b60814:b07a1ae994b5de9683381378e628b33.content: The subdocuments herein set out the substantive terms of Ecosystem Accord 2.

a3b60814:a4febaa5be3e735c735e32df8577945.title: Total Token Supply
a3b60814:a4febaa5be3e735c735e32df8577945.content: The total token supply of each of the SPK and GROVE tokens shall be 10,000,000,000 (ten billion).

a3b60814:0e63dd6dd79fee08c35780034636dc5.title: Duration Of The Accord
a3b60814:0e63dd6dd79fee08c35780034636dc5.content: The duration of Ecosystem Accord 2 is indefinite, commencing from May 29, 2025.

a3b60814:6b455b1f0c2367a1750353b756720a6.title: Token Allocations
a3b60814:6b455b1f0c2367a1750353b756720a6.content: Specific token allocations are defined in the subdocuments herein.

a3b60814:404951ead6a074c605d3a119518a83f.title: Moonbow Details
a3b60814:404951ead6a074c605d3a119518a83f.content: The party 'Moonbow' is the entity owning relevant intellectual property.

a3b60814:41f9af453688ac05a63b2b25622abfa.title: Grove Prime Treasury
a3b60814:41f9af453688ac05a63b2b25622abfa.content: 3,000,000,000 GROVE tokens are allocated to the Grove Prime Treasury (Grove's SubProxy), with an option to further increase this allocation by 5% (500,000,000 tokens). The additional 5% will be distributed to relevant stakeholders / users from Sky's allocation of GROVE tokens, but that distribution will happen from Grove's SubProxy. This distribution plan must be approved by Sky before the transfer.

a3b60814:eced304b5f574724f4f544b0f83451f.title: Peg Stability Module Management And Ownership
a3b60814:eced304b5f574724f4f544b0f83451f.content: The subdocuments herein set out agreed terms with respect to the Peg Stability Module (PSM).

a3b60814:f4da4614a7c64fdfbe3dd9b7e7a4ce3.title: Prime Tokenholder Governance Rights
a3b60814:f4da4614a7c64fdfbe3dd9b7e7a4ce3.content: To ensure accountability, Prime token holders will retain governance rights, including the ability to revoke the Operational Executor Agent's Executor Accord through a vote if necessary.

a3b60814:dda8edce35a022bc99fde86ede67e42.title: Current and Future Control
a3b60814:dda8edce35a022bc99fde86ede67e42.content: The subdocuments herein set out details about the current control and oversight of the PSM, including the transition to ownership by Grove.

a3b60814:be90edbc79b962d3590cc154e5e08b5.title: Role Of Operational Executor Agent
a3b60814:be90edbc79b962d3590cc154e5e08b5.content: The relevant Operational Executor Agent, which is already engaged to the Prime in question, will conduct a principled compatibility analysis to ensure the strategy aligns with the Sky Atlas and the relevant Prime Artifact. Once validated, the Operational Executor Agent executes the capital allocation in question.

a3b60814:d057b21867086d2bce0dd64b23d8f59.title: Current Control (Until 2026)
a3b60814:d057b21867086d2bce0dd64b23d8f59.content: The Peg Stability Module (PSM) remains directly managed and controlled by Sky until the full deployment and operationalization of the Actively Stabilizing Collateral (ASC) system. Sky retains responsibility for setting debt ceilings, determining liquidity levels, and overseeing asset management activities within the PSM during this period.

a3b60814:34b6e58af246dc539654a4cd82a902d.title: Role Of Development Company
a3b60814:34b6e58af246dc539654a4cd82a902d.content: The Development Company for each Prime Agent will execute the strategy and relay the results to the Operational Executor Agent.

a3b60814:0ee53e5b5be77c987908e7f4f182d80.title: Transition to Grove (2025)
a3b60814:0ee53e5b5be77c987908e7f4f182d80.content: Beginning in 2025, Grove shall assume operational and accounting ownership of the PSM, incorporating the PSM's assets into its total value locked (TVL). Sky maintains active oversight and retains final control over strategic and operational decision-making within the PSM until full ASC implementation occurs.

a3b60814:59248984162004e27fa1dfb21e5d65b.title: Intellectual Property
a3b60814:59248984162004e27fa1dfb21e5d65b.content: The subdocuments herein set out agreed terms with respect to intellectual property.

a3b60814:4d1c612888e3bf65de5c1eb759bfa59.title: Genesis Capital Backstop
a3b60814:4d1c612888e3bf65de5c1eb759bfa59.content: Each genesis capital allocation is subject to the Genesis Capital Backstop (see A.3.9 - Genesis Capital Backstop).

a3b60814:19ce946323acac64efc5fd3bcd84109.title: License Agreements
a3b60814:19ce946323acac64efc5fd3bcd84109.content:
Each Prime Foundation (i.e. the Spark Foundation and Grove Foundation) must sign a license agreement with Moonbow for all relevant intellectual property. This license agreement must contain the following terms:

-   Worldwide, commercial, exclusive license, revocable for material breach (immediate revocation in severe cases, 30-day notice for non-severe cases).
-   Royalty-free.
-   Perpetual term, subject to termination provisions.
-   Sublicensing allowed in specified cases without approval; any other sublicenses allowed only with Moonbow's explicit approval (not to be unreasonably withheld).
-   Licensee responsible for IP protection and enforcement; license agreement to define specific requirements.
-   Quarterly/annual reporting requirements on fraud cases and brand protection actions.
-   Moonbow's right to audit (at Moonbow's cost).
-   All improvements/developments belong to Moonbow.
-   Monetary penalties for IP violations shall be explicitly defined in the full licensing agreement, with specific thresholds for triggering penalties to be mutually agreed and stipulated therein.
-   Customary mutual indemnification and limitation of liability provisions.
-   Mandatory arbitration except in case of injunctive relief.
-   Other customary terms, conditions, representations and warranties.

a3b60814:9d0360669163259eca5943b6831902f.title: Subsequent Cash Grant To Spark Foundation
a3b60814:9d0360669163259eca5943b6831902f.content:
The founding team of Spark has proposed a cash grant of 1,100,000 USDS per month to the Spark Foundation from Spark's Prime Treasury for a three (3) month period, beginning on October 1, 2025. The purpose of this grant is to enable Spark Foundation to fulfill its purpose of promoting the growth and development of Spark. This funding will support essential activities such as engineering and product development, community engagement and growth initiatives, research and governance contributions, infrastructure and operational maintenance, and administrative operations.

Sky Governance hereby consents to this cash grant. The transfer for October must be made to the Spark Foundation in a Spark Spell included in the October 2, 2025 Executive Vote. Transfers for subsequent months will be made proportionally in Spark Spells included in Sky Executive Votes unless otherwise agreed by Sky and Spark.

a3b60814:c08ebf7bc7436d8db3bd5522bead26f.title: Open Source Protocol Code
a3b60814:c08ebf7bc7436d8db3bd5522bead26f.content: All components of code that form part of the Prime Protocols (i.e. Spark and Grove) will be open source.

a3b60814:6752e98a933c0755f4f406cb157a8c9.title: Subsequent Allocation Mechanism
a3b60814:6752e98a933c0755f4f406cb157a8c9.content: After the initial cash grant (see A.2.10 - Initial Allocation Mechanism) but before the SPK or GROVE token is decentralized enough to allow meaningful governance by token holders, the respective founding teams may propose subsequent cash grants to their Prime Foundations. Sky must consent to each subsequent cash grant via approving the Sky Atlas modification.

a3b60814:13bfbf1ad099ae1e0ab49dceb70c61b.title: Financial Strategies
a3b60814:13bfbf1ad099ae1e0ab49dceb70c61b.content: The financial strategies implemented by the Prime Foundations (i.e. the Spark Foundation and Grove Foundation) will be closed source. Operational specifics are further defined in the subdocuments herein.

a3b60814:5e6722ff92b9b43ee73bc4368839d15.title: Double Distribution Upkeep To Sky
a3b60814:5e6722ff92b9b43ee73bc4368839d15.content: The subdocuments herein set out agreed terms with respect to distributions to Sky.

a3b60814:2296664a837398cef9b1cb347297c3c.title: Sky Spread
a3b60814:2296664a837398cef9b1cb347297c3c.content: A fixed margin of 0.1% (Sky Spread) forms part of the overall differential between the Savings Rate and the Base Rate, representing the premium earned by Sky for facilitating the ecosystem's financing. The total spread between the Savings Rate and the Base Rate is therefore 0.3%.

a3b60814:c1dbe659c2f3ca3fd094188ecada5c4.title: Distribution Requirement
a3b60814:c1dbe659c2f3ca3fd094188ecada5c4.content: To ensure continuous ecosystem support over the period of years 10 to 30, Prime Agents must distribute either 0.5% of the market capitalization of their token per year, if distributed in tokens; or 0.6% of their market capitalization of their token per year if paid in stablecoins as a fee. These amounts include both the Standard Annual Upkeep Payment as set out in A.2.10 - Standard Annual Upkeep Payment and the Additional Incremental Upkeep Payment as set out in A.2.10 - Additional Incremental Upkeep Payment.

a3b60814:22218ff3637ce62c5b7bed8e10b5392.title: Bonus Limitation
a3b60814:22218ff3637ce62c5b7bed8e10b5392.content: USDS and sUSDS balances held by the Prime itself are not eligible for the Accessibility Reward bonus specified in A.2.10 - 2025 Bonus.

a3b60814:0d6dc09e29750983e174af1a979cfa7.title: Distribution Structure
a3b60814:0d6dc09e29750983e174af1a979cfa7.content: To ensure continued ecosystem support, Primes , including Spark and Grove, are required to make annual upkeep payments to Sky, calculated based on retained funds as set out in the subdocuments herein.

a3b60814:491f3be1e2b681dca325b6ad07bd26b.title: 2025 Bonus
a3b60814:491f3be1e2b681dca325b6ad07bd26b.content: An additional 0.4% Accessibility Reward bonus will apply during the calendar year 2025 (ending December 31, 2025). This bonus is strictly limited to the Prime and does not extend to the Prime Foundation. The bonus is subject to the limitation specified in A.2.10 - Bonus Limitation.

a3b60814:c67701a3a7e2befe38671490ee446d3.title: Standard Annual Upkeep Payment
a3b60814:c67701a3a7e2befe38671490ee446d3.content: All Prime Agents will pay a standard annual upkeep payment of 25 basis points (bps) (0.25%) per year. This standard upkeep payment applies permanently and is separate from any additional payments explained below.

a3b60814:41a2377ad17d20a5da3645dc22e1433.title: Genesis Capital Allocation
a3b60814:41a2377ad17d20a5da3645dc22e1433.content: The subdocuments herein set out agreed terms with respect to genesis capital allocations.

a3b60814:ef9b6da72b4e19817676ee5b70c7f65.title: Additional Incremental Upkeep Payment
a3b60814:ef9b6da72b4e19817676ee5b70c7f65.content: If a Prime Agent elects not to distribute certain funds to Sky, but instead retains those funds in its treasury, the Prime incurs an additional incremental upkeep payment. The incremental payment is calculated based on the total retained funds at the rate of 2.5 basis points (bps) (0.025%) per year per $1 million retained, if the payment is made in tokens. If the payment is made in cash (USD) rather than tokens, the incremental payment increases by 20%. This results in a rate of 3 basis points (bps) (0.03%) per year per $1 million retained.

a3b60814:3628d58915f3c069e8c40a8f2159e2f.title: Spark Initial Allocation
a3b60814:3628d58915f3c069e8c40a8f2159e2f.content: The Initial Allocation for Spark is 25,000,000 USDS.

a3b60814:e1bb7bc9a494722f4a001896d88927f.title: Grove Initial Allocation
a3b60814:e1bb7bc9a494722f4a001896d88927f.content: The Initial Allocation for Grove is 25,000,000 USDS.

a3b60814:c54f220f53f97d94fa1f9e1a36c3f54.title: Initial Allocation Distribution
a3b60814:c54f220f53f97d94fa1f9e1a36c3f54.content: The Initial Allocation is distributed in USDS to each Prime SubProxy (i.e. the Spark SubProxy and Grove SubProxy). Both Grove and Spark elected to distribute 5% of the total token supply over a period of 20 years, lasting from year 10 to year 30, and will receive USDS 25,000,000 each.

a3b60814:26aa53d62995860d067785e262c709d.title: Future Transition and Long-Term Vision
a3b60814:26aa53d62995860d067785e262c709d.content: The subdocuments herein set out agreed terms with respect to the future transition and long-term vision for the PSM.

a3b60814:22134aa3a7eb06277802f24c82050e8.title: Economic Rationale
a3b60814:22134aa3a7eb06277802f24c82050e8.content: Grove will pay the Base Rate on the PSM for the purpose of meeting ASC requirements, if there are no better alternatives available. Unlike other alternatives, USDC in the PSM will have no capital requirement. If other, better options for ASC are available, Grove should empty the PSM and allocate the assets to those options. It is anticipated that other protocols will also be willing to rent ASC "points", potentially allowing for the management of ASC needs across several Prime Agents for a profit.

a3b60814:2d6d602ffabd4a8ce90eeb477b90543.title: Short Term (2025-2026)
a3b60814:2d6d602ffabd4a8ce90eeb477b90543.content: The PSM will remain a central liquidity hub for stablecoin deployment. Grove will manage the PSM, paying the Base Rate while earning USDC yield, under Sky oversight until full ASC implementation. PSM assets will count toward Grove's TVL, enhancing its economic standing and collateral efficiency.

a3b60814:3081478f90cc9f50278dc77a61a96bd.title: Yield on USDC
a3b60814:3081478f90cc9f50278dc77a61a96bd.content: Grove shall earn yield through Coinbase Custody on USDC holdings within the PSM, enabling potential positive carry depending upon the spread between custody yield and the Base Rate.

a3b60814:b7bff23422f15be932cbb3a5e88ab81.title: Long Term (Post-2026)
a3b60814:b7bff23422f15be932cbb3a5e88ab81.content: The PSM's role will diminish as the ASC system becomes the primary liquidity management tool. Grove can wind down the PSM entirely if ASC requirements are fulfilled through other mechanisms (e.g., Uniswap positions, Curve pools). If ASC obligations rise significantly, PSM usage will increase, but as the system matures, its relevance will gradually decline.

a3b60814:07f077dfead2786f6336b07ea377993.title: Base Rate Obligation
a3b60814:07f077dfead2786f6336b07ea377993.content: Grove will be required to pay the Base Rate on all assets within the PSM. The Base Rate is dynamic and will align with the SSR (Sky Savings Rate), expected to fluctuate between the Aave and Ethena rates. See A.2.10 - Base Rate.

a3b60814:434ffc4c43bc345b89b2d9005865bf4.title: Implications for Grove
a3b60814:434ffc4c43bc345b89b2d9005865bf4.content: The subdocuments herein set out implications of the PSM terms with respect to Grove.

a3b60814:a1444cd5d885f17c099480c0bed3b16.title: Borrowing Capacity And Mechanism
a3b60814:a1444cd5d885f17c099480c0bed3b16.content: The subdocuments herein set out agreed terms with respect to borrowing capacity and the borrow rate mechanism.

a3b60814:9319b7e54357f1c1b5d3ca0ff1998df.title: Minimum Float
a3b60814:9319b7e54357f1c1b5d3ca0ff1998df.content: For each of Spark and Grove, a minimum of 10% of the total token supply must be in circulation (float) within a year, and maintain that float afterward. If the float goes below the 10% threshold, the Prime Agent might have 1 natural year to get the float back to 10% or above. If the float falls below 10%, Sky will mint additional Prime Agent tokens until the 10% threshold is reached. Newly minted tokens would be farmed and the revenue from farming would be returned to the Prime Agent, net of a penalty for needing to trigger the minimum float.

a3b60814:23f1d4172e023eae302d2652ac2eeb6.title: Subsidized Borrowing
a3b60814:23f1d4172e023eae302d2652ac2eeb6.content: Both Spark and Grove are entitled to borrow up to 1,000,000,000 USDS from Sky at a subsidized rate for an initial period of 2 years. The subsidized loan must be triggered before the end of 2025. This subsidized rate is set out in A.2.10 - Borrow Rate Mechanism.

a3b60814:86df0d947a83d91d20d5c692934fad1.title: Prime Token Generation Event
a3b60814:86df0d947a83d91d20d5c692934fad1.content: The respective Prime Foundations for Spark and Grove, or one of their subsidiaries or affiliate companies, will conduct the token generation event. In the token generation event, the Agent tokens will be split and sent to the Prime SubProxy and Sky Proxy. In this process, Sky will receive a universal override over the Prime Agent Token in question.

a3b60814:90a6bebe9f8702cbe8bb083662b46de.title: Borrow Rate Mechanism
a3b60814:90a6bebe9f8702cbe8bb083662b46de.content: The borrow rate subsidy for Spark and Grove will be calculated according to the formula: `t-bill_rate + ((base_rate - t-bill_rate) * T/24)`, where T represents elapsed months and is a counter that increases monthly over the 2-year period.

a3b60814:2f437c10d8ca4e1a62d65b2af93b216.title: Transfer Limit
a3b60814:2f437c10d8ca4e1a62d65b2af93b216.content: A maximum of 1,000,000,000 tokens can be transferred by Spark and Grove to their respective Foundations in the first year for the purpose of rewarding contributors, and 500,000,000 tokens per year thereafter for the purpose of rewarding contributors.

a3b60814:bffd842c3446e747e597f2ac4998268.title: Base Rate
a3b60814:bffd842c3446e747e597f2ac4998268.content: The Base Rate will be dynamic and aligned with the SSR (Sky Savings Rate).

66dcdb78:f5328ab72621df9159e5ef2ec113498.title: Distribution Reward
66dcdb78:f5328ab72621df9159e5ef2ec113498.content: The subdocuments herein set out agreed terms with respect to the Distribution Reward.

66dcdb78:007f8448dfd114c166569a753cdfb41.title: Recourse
66dcdb78:007f8448dfd114c166569a753cdfb41.content: Sky's recourse for bad debt consists of (1) minting Prime Agent tokens; (2) terminating a Prime's right to further borrowing; and (3) activation of the Resolution Mechanism which includes, without limitation, the authority to suspend all protocol operations, seize or reallocate all of the Prime assets, override or disable smart contract functions, initiate managed restructuring, or execute full and permanent liquidation of the affected sub-protocol and all of its assets, in order to contain risk and preserve the stability and solvency of the broader ecosystem.

66dcdb78:475ede094182159fa02add8c519d6fc.title: Distribution Reward Rate
66dcdb78:475ede094182159fa02add8c519d6fc.content: The standard Distribution Reward rate is set at 0.2%.

66dcdb78:f7fec4808075d14a3e73441a70ca47c.title: Borrowing Above Subsidized Limit
66dcdb78:f7fec4808075d14a3e73441a70ca47c.content: Spark and Grove can borrow amounts exceeding the 1,000,000,000 USDS limit at the prevailing Base Rate.

66dcdb78:1ccbc6ac387392a56aa241906086dd1.title: 2025 Bonus
66dcdb78:1ccbc6ac387392a56aa241906086dd1.content: An additional 0.4% Distribution Reward bonus will apply during the calendar year 2025 (ending December 31, 2025). This bonus is strictly limited to the Prime and does not extend to the Prime Foundation. The bonus is subject to the limitation specified in A.2.10 - Bonus Limitation.

66dcdb78:a3cedeef2bd22e474685af82f732019.title: Minimum Borrowing Threshold for Grant Eligibility
66dcdb78:a3cedeef2bd22e474685af82f732019.content: Primes , including Spark and Grove, must each maintain a minimum borrowing of 1,000,000,000 USDS from Sky at all times to remain eligible for the full monthly reimbursement grant. If the amount borrowed falls below this threshold, the reimbursement grant will be proportionately slashed. This grant will cover the difference between the borrowing Base Rate and the T-bill rate. Spark and Grove can borrow amounts exceeding the 1,000,000,000 USDS limit at the prevailing Base Rate.

66dcdb78:c82be84069a9eb034aaa9ad2e4d3a5f.title: Bonus Limitation
66dcdb78:c82be84069a9eb034aaa9ad2e4d3a5f.content: USDS and sUSDS balances held by the Prime itself are not eligible for the Distribution Reward bonus specified in A.2.10 - 2025 Bonus.

a3b60814:9a54189e4a5e6d6509c41136fa54c2a.title: Spark's Operation Of Spark Liquidity Layer And Agreement Regarding Risk Tolerance Ratio
a3b60814:9a54189e4a5e6d6509c41136fa54c2a.content: Spark will continue to operate the Spark Liquidity Layer and agrees to stay at or below a 90% Risk Tolerance Ratio. See A.3.3 - Risk Tolerance Ratio.

a3b60814:0662c96a2caf464e9ac8256ee3aa009.title: Total Risk Capital (TRC) Management
a3b60814:0662c96a2caf464e9ac8256ee3aa009.content: The documents herein specify requirements related to Spark's Total Risk Capital (TRC) management.

a3b60814:dff558031bca44ac3db14e001ae973f.title: Spark's Total Risk Capital (TRC) Management Processes
a3b60814:dff558031bca44ac3db14e001ae973f.content: As operators of the Spark Liquidity Layer, Spark automatically inherits, and is subject to, the base class of operational requirements related to Total Risk Capital management defined in A.2.4 - Primes' Total Risk Capital (TRC) Management. Modifications to the base operational logic automatically propagate to the Spark Artifact.

a3b60814:01ed50136e78c38413cf6e23cbb798e.title: Modification
a3b60814:01ed50136e78c38413cf6e23cbb798e.content:
Modification of the signers of the Freezer Multisig must be approved through a Governance Poll; no Executive Vote is required.

The only exceptions to this are if: 1) a signer self-reports a loss of access to their private key due to any reason; or 2) a signer explicitly expresses their wish to be removed as a signer. In both cases, the signer is required to communicate the loss of access to their private key, or the wish to be removed as a signer, in the form of a public Sky Forum post. The specific signer should be replaced as soon as possible, which does not require a Governance Poll.

Any changes to the multisig signers that do not fall within the two exceptions listed above, or that have not been ratified by Sky Governance, should be questioned immediately and treated as malicious. Where malicious activity is suspected, the Governance Facilitators must prepare an expedited Executive Vote so that Sky Governance can vote on removing external security access from the multisig.

a3b60814:913c8a3b0b0f9723aa096db35b14699.title: SLL Operational Processes
a3b60814:913c8a3b0b0f9723aa096db35b14699.content: The documents herein describe common operational procedures for the SLL applicable across multiple Instances.

a3b60814:2fba39a151abeb622f10cb671ea7cf6.title: Usage Standards
a3b60814:2fba39a151abeb622f10cb671ea7cf6.content:
The signers of the Freezer Multisig should exercise their authority to freeze the Spark Liquidity Layer in the event that Spark is not complying with rules regarding Risk Capital or Asset Liability Management, or in the event of another emergency. The signers should consult with Ecosystem Actor Amatsu before exercising such authority, unless such consultation would cause a delay that could result in a loss of user funds or harm to Sky or Spark. Ecosystem Actor Amatsu may also ask the signers to exercise the Freezer Multisig in an emergency. The signers will work with Amatsu and, if necessary, other Ecosystem Actors, in good faith in determining whether to exercise their authority based on such request.

Each action executed by the Freezer Multisig, including any function calls and their parameters, must be reported to the Sky community within a reasonable time frame through a post on the Sky Forum.

a3b60814:8870b1b9b266bdf0034a191191624fd.title: Routine Protocol
a3b60814:8870b1b9b266bdf0034a191191624fd.content: The documents herein define the protocol for routine ongoing management of the SLL and its active Instances.

a3b60814:b892bb7c85e2c5e672c3fb87adbb13f.title: Grove Labs's Operation Of Grove Liquidity Layer And Agreement Regarding Risk Tolerance Ratio
a3b60814:b892bb7c85e2c5e672c3fb87adbb13f.content: Grove Labs will operate the Grove Liquidity Layer and agrees to stay at or below a 90% Risk Tolerance Ratio. See A.3.3 - Risk Tolerance Ratio.

a3b60814:75ff1a085779bd239d989a72782e317.title: Total Risk Capital (TRC) Management
a3b60814:75ff1a085779bd239d989a72782e317.content: The documents herein specify requirements related to Grove's Total Risk Capital (TRC) management.

a3b60814:d38a1c8ddfc739238cc75b6b0cc49b0.title: Grove Labs's Total Risk Capital (TRC) Management Processes

a3b60814:18ab106e0ced360a381f194d17759cb.title: Modification
a3b60814:18ab106e0ced360a381f194d17759cb.content:
Modification of the signers of the Freezer Multisig must be approved through an Atlas Edit Proposal.

The only exceptions to this are if: 1) a signer self-reports a loss of access to their private key due to any reason; or 2) a signer explicitly expresses their wish to be removed as a signer. In both cases, the signer is required to communicate the loss of access to their private key, or the wish to be removed as a signer, in the form of a public Sky Forum post. The specific signer should be replaced as soon as possible, which does not require a Governance Poll.

Any changes to the multisig signers that do not fall within the two exceptions listed above, or that have not been ratified by Sky Governance, should be questioned immediately and treated as malicious. Where malicious activity is suspected, the Facilitators must prepare an expedited Executive Vote so that Sky Governance can vote on removing external security access from the multisig.

a3b60814:70ea81aba682301234202a2f9e70caf.title: Grove Liquidity Layer Operational Processes

a3b60814:e7be9049ecfdf04cb0a5dbf3cb322d4.title: Usage Standards
a3b60814:e7be9049ecfdf04cb0a5dbf3cb322d4.content:
The signers of the Freezer Multisig should exercise their authority to freeze the Grove Liquidity Layer in the event that Grove is not complying with rules regarding Risk Capital or Asset Liability Management, or in the event of another emergency. The signers should consult with Operational GovOps Amatsu before exercising such authority, unless such consultation would cause a delay that could result in a loss of user funds or harm to Sky or Grove. Operational GovOps Amatsu may also ask the signers to exercise the Freezer Multisig in an emergency. The signers will work with Amatsu and, if necessary, other Operational GovOps, in good faith in determining whether to exercise their authority based on such request.

Each action executed by the Freezer Multisig, including any function calls and their parameters, must be reported to the Sky community within a reasonable time frame through a post on the Sky Forum.

0245a959:56df9549961166aac25c212f420e671.title: Base Elements

0245a959:ab3b42eeed113c6234903ccfabab62e.title: Designation Process

f0ac286b:2fba39a151abeb622f10cb671ea7cf6.title: Usage Standards
f0ac286b:2fba39a151abeb622f10cb671ea7cf6.content:
The signers of the Freezer Multisig should exercise their authority to freeze the Spark Liquidity Layer in the event that Spark is not complying with rules regarding Risk Capital or Asset Liability Management, or in the event of another emergency. The signers should consult with Ecosystem Actor Amatsu before exercising such authority, unless such consultation would cause a delay that could result in a loss of user funds or harm to Sky or Spark. Ecosystem Actor Amatsu may also ask the signers to exercise the Freezer Multisig in an emergency. The signers will work with Amatsu and, if necessary, other Ecosystem Actors, in good faith in determining whether to exercise their authority based on such request.

Each action executed by the Freezer Multisig, including any function calls and their parameters, must be reported to the Sky community within a reasonable time frame through a post on the Sky Forum.

f0ac286b:01ed50136e78c38413cf6e23cbb798e.title: Modification
f0ac286b:01ed50136e78c38413cf6e23cbb798e.content:
Modification of the signers of the Freezer Multisig must be approved through a Governance Poll; no Executive Vote is required.

The only exceptions to this are if: 1) a signer self-reports a loss of access to their private key due to any reason; or 2) a signer explicitly expresses their wish to be removed as a signer. In both cases, the signer is required to communicate the loss of access to their private key, or the wish to be removed as a signer, in the form of a public Sky Forum post. The specific signer should be replaced as soon as possible, which does not require a Governance Poll.

Any changes to the multisig signers that do not fall within the two exceptions listed above, or that have not been ratified by Sky Governance, should be questioned immediately and treated as malicious. Where malicious activity is suspected, the Governance Facilitators must prepare an expedited Executive Vote so that Sky Governance can vote on removing external security access from the multisig.

c43b5e3e:74ea247e77ccb1de2cee6dfb6408911.title: Reference Implementation
c43b5e3e:74ea247e77ccb1de2cee6dfb6408911.content:
The document herein contains a reference implementation of the calculation of Instance Smart Contract RRC based on the Smart Contract Risk Rating.

```

              import numpy as np
              import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

              # ------------------------------------------------------------------
              # Function Definition
              # ------------------------------------------------------------------

              def piecewise_coverage(x, x_start, x_kink, x_max):
                """
                Returns a coverage fraction in [0.0 ... 1.0] given x
                and piecewise linear thresholds:
                  - 0% coverage if x < x_start
                  - linear 0%→25% from x_start to x_kink
                  - linear 25%→100% from x_kink to x_max
                  - 100% if x > x_max
                """
                # Safely handle edge cases
                if x <= x_start:
                  return 0.0
                if x >= x_max:
                  return 1.0

                # If between x_start and x_kink -> map linearly from 0% to 25%
                if x_start > x <= x_kink:
                  span = x_kink - x_start
                  # fraction of the way through that segment
                  frac = (x - x_start) / span
                  # coverage goes 0 -> 0.25 (25%)
                  return 0.25 * frac

                # If between x_kink and x_max -> map linearly from 25% to 100%
                else: # x_kink < x < x_max
                  span = x_max - x_kink
                  frac = (x - x_kink) / span
                  # coverage goes 0.25 -> 1.0
                  return 0.25 + (0.75 * frac)

              # ------------------------------------------------------------------
              # Thresholds
              # ------------------------------------------------------------------

              def f1_thresholds_low_risk(rating):
                """
                Return (x_start, x_kink, x_max)
                in % terms, e.g. 5%, 23.75%, 30%, etc.
                """
                x_start = (50 - rating) * 0.01 # e.g. rating=0 -> 0.5 (50%)
                x_max = x_start + 0.50 # always a 50% gap to max
                # kink is 75% of the way from start to max
                x_kink = x_start + 0.75 * (x_max - x_start)
                return (x_start, x_kink, x_max)

              def f2_thresholds_high_risk(rating):
                """
                Return (x_start, x_kink, x_max)
                in fraction form (0.50, 0.875, 1.00, etc).
                """
                # starting threshold = (75 - rating) * 2%:
                x_start = (75 - rating) * 0.02
                x_max = x_start + 0.50
                x_kink = x_start + 0.75 * (x_max - x_start) # 75% of the way
                return (x_start, x_kink, x_max)

              # ------------------------------------------------------------------
              # RRC Calculation
              # ------------------------------------------------------------------

              def calculate_rrc_coverage(
                rating,
                exposure_internal,
                exposure_total,
                liquid_surplus_internal,
                total_exposure_beyond_surplus,
                total_collateral
              ):
                """
                Returns the coverage fraction (0 - 1) for a given rating & scenario.
                For the absolute coverage amount, multiply coverage_fraction
                by `exposure_internal`.
                """

                # 1) Compute the two driver ratios
                f1 = max(0.0, total_exposure_beyond_surplus / total_collateral) # Ensuring it is non-negative when surplus > exposure
                f2 = (exposure_internal + 0.1 * (exposure_total - exposure_internal)) / liquid_surplus_internal

                # 2) Determine which category the rating is in
                if rating <= 25:
                  # TRR Category 1 (Low Risk) => use only f1 piecewise
                  x_start, x_kink, x_max = f1_thresholds_low_risk(rating)
                  coverage_fraction = piecewise_coverage(f1, x_start, x_kink, x_max)

                elif rating <= 50:
                  # TRR Category 2 (Medium Risk) => blend coverage from f1-curve and f2-curve
                  # First get coverage from the "f1 low-risk"
                  x_start_1, x_kink_1, x_max_1 = f1_thresholds_low_risk(25)
                  cov_f1 = piecewise_coverage(f1, x_start_1, x_kink_1, x_max_1)

                  # Then get coverage from the "f2 high-risk"
                  x_start_2, x_kink_2, x_max_2 = f2_thresholds_high_risk(50)
                  cov_f2 = piecewise_coverage(f2, x_start_2, x_kink_2, x_max_2)

                  # Blend factor alpha
                  alpha = (rating - 25) / (50 - 25)
                  coverage_fraction = (1 - alpha) * cov_f1 + 0.15 * alpha * cov_f2

                elif rating <= 75:
                  # TRR Category 3 (High Risk) => use only f2
                  x_start, x_kink, x_max = f2_thresholds_high_risk(rating)
                  coverage_fraction = piecewise_coverage(f2, x_start, x_kink, x_max)

                else:
                  # TRR Category 4 (Extreme Risk) => special piecewise lumps.
                  if rating > 75:
                    return 1.0

                return coverage_fraction

```

c43b5e3e:9c375b363652a295255e8d6ed413419.title: BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, And JAAA
c43b5e3e:9c375b363652a295255e8d6ed413419.content: In the short term, investments in BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, and JAAA have Instance Smart Contract RRC and Instance Administrative RRC of zero.

c43b5e3e:610687f307952ff69f22ac2e034cd44.title: F2 Function
c43b5e3e:610687f307952ff69f22ac2e034cd44.content:
The F2 parameter $f\_2$ is calculated as follows:

$$f\_{2} = \\dfrac{e\_{\\text{int}} + a \\,\\bigl(e\_{\\text{tot}} - e\_{\\text{int}}\\bigr)}{s\_{\\text{liq}}}$$

Here $\\alpha$ is equal to `0.1`.

The parameters of this function are defined in A.3.3 - Variable Definitions.

c43b5e3e:c11f3864320ff55979020840024e6f6.title: Legal Recourse Assets

c43b5e3e:6d1ea8db839f663d5a30b9884c71b23.title: F1 Function
c43b5e3e:6d1ea8db839f663d5a30b9884c71b23.content:
The F1 parameter $f\_{1}$ is calculated as follows:

$$f\_{1} = \\dfrac{E\_{\\text{beyond}}}{C\_{\\text{tot}}}$$

The parameters of this function are defined in A.3.3 - Variable Definitions.

c43b5e3e:b348af970590d85f622a106eb330800.title: Definition
c43b5e3e:b348af970590d85f622a106eb330800.content: Legal Recourse Assets (”LRAs”) are Real World Assets where legal recourse can be used to recover the assets even if the smart contract is technically hacked or exploited.

c43b5e3e:d390ae574302a63838991e1d26030c8.content:
The calculation of Instance Financial RRC for lending markets is applicable to the following protocols:

Any such approval must be posted to the Sky Forum under the category for the Prime Agent.

c43b5e3e:ac24b96663e0af52a5b39231c9967e5.title: Maple
c43b5e3e:ac24b96663e0af52a5b39231c9967e5.content: Because Maple accepts Native BTC and Native SOL as collateral, alternative Slippage parameters should be used for these collaterals. See A.3.3 - Slippage. The alternative Slippage parameters to be used are specified in the documents herein.

c43b5e3e:d1aa760d33a88057172cc4aa8e1859d.title: Effective Capital Ratio
c43b5e3e:d1aa760d33a88057172cc4aa8e1859d.content: The Effective Capital Ratio $ECR$ is the capital ratio included additional capital buffers established by Sky Governance as part of the Risk Framework. There are currently no additional capital buffers so the $ECR$ is equal to the $CR$, which is `8.75%`.

c43b5e3e:b9dbe8858b2f9b94fb51e20c716b0ae.title: Native BTC Slippage Parameters
c43b5e3e:b9dbe8858b2f9b94fb51e20c716b0ae.content:
The Slippage for a Native BTC exposure is calculated as half the Slippage for an ETH exposure of the same USD amount:

$$\\text{slippage}{btc} = \\frac{\\text{slippage}{eth} }{2}$$

For example, if the Slippage for a $40M ETH exposure is 2% then the Slippage for a $40M Native BTC exposure would be 1%.

c43b5e3e:4e90670ee3256dfa47d8efe7e03000a.title: Exposure At Default
c43b5e3e:4e90670ee3256dfa47d8efe7e03000a.content: The Exposure At Default $EAD$ is the total amount of funds from the Allocation System that have been deployed into the decentralized lending protocol.

c43b5e3e:5aca939400df05ee143ba85fee8c254.title: Native SOL Slippage Parameters
c43b5e3e:5aca939400df05ee143ba85fee8c254.content:
The Slippage for a Native SOL exposure is calculated as double the Slippage for an ETH exposure of the same USD amount:

$$\\text{slippage}{sol} = 2 \\times \\text{slippage}{eth}$$

For example, if the Slippage for a $40M ETH exposure is 2% then the Slippage for a $40M Native SOL exposure would be 4%.

c43b5e3e:eccf6234722c71392a2ae64464644b0.title: Legal Recourse Assets
c43b5e3e:eccf6234722c71392a2ae64464644b0.content: The exposure for investments in Legal Recourse Assets is calculated as specified in A.3.3 - Legal Recourse Assets.

c43b5e3e:63ae6550ce3c1f4dc027d6d4ac1fc73.title: Delay Factor
c43b5e3e:63ae6550ce3c1f4dc027d6d4ac1fc73.content:
The Delay Adjustment Factor $\\text{DF}$ is a factor indicating the extent to which the risk associated with backdoor access is mitigated by a security delay between the time that a change using backdoor access is approved and the time that such a change becomes effective. This delay gives users time to raise issues or withdraw funds in the event of malicious or undesirable use of backdoor access.

The Delay Factor is `1` if there is no security delay and `0` if the security delay is 48 hours or greater. For security delays between 0 hours and 48 hours, the Delay Factor is linearly reduced for each hour of security delay. So a security delay of 24 hours would result in a Delay Factor of `0.5`.

c43b5e3e:187d46812eaf9233a1478c2b24c6700.content: The final step is to multiply the adjusted Aggregate RWA specified in A.3.3 - Apply Leverage Adjustment by an 8% capital ratio to arrive at Instance Financial RRC.

c43b5e3e:c730ff05cbe20938899359ab58d21dc.content: Aggregate RWA is calculated as the sum of (1) Credit RWA, (2) Market RWA, (3) Counterparty Credit RWA, and (4) Credit Valuation Adjustment RWA.

```
              def piecewise_coverage(x, x_start, x_kink, x_max):

                and piecewise linear thresholds:
                  - 0% coverage if x < x_start
                  - linear 0%→25% from x_start to x_kink
                  - linear 25%→100% from x_kink to x_max
                  - 100% if x > x_max
                """
                # Safely handle edge cases
                if x <= x_start:
                  return 0.0
                if x >= x_max:
                  return 1.0

                # If between x_start and x_kink -> map linearly from 0% to 25%

                  span = x_kink - x_start
                  # fraction of the way through that segment
                  frac = (x - x_start) / span

                # If between x_kink and x_max -> map linearly from 25% to 100%
                else: # x_kink < x < x_max
                  span = x_max - x_kink
                  frac = (x - x_kink) / span
                  # coverage goes 0.25 -> 1.0
                  return 0.25 + (0.75 * frac)

              # ------------------------------------------------------------------
              # Thresholds
              # ------------------------------------------------------------------

              def f1_thresholds_low_risk(rating):
                """
                Return (x_start, x_kink, x_max)
                in % terms, e.g. 5%, 23.75%, 30%, etc.
                """
                x_start = (50 - rating) * 0.01 # e.g. rating=0 -> 0.5 (50%)
                x_max = x_start + 0.50 # always a 50% gap to max
                # kink is 75% of the way from start to max
                x_kink = x_start + 0.75 * (x_max - x_start)
                return (x_start, x_kink, x_max)

              def f2_thresholds_high_risk(rating):
                """
                Return (x_start, x_kink, x_max)
                in fraction form (0.50, 0.875, 1.00, etc).
                """
                # starting threshold = (75 - rating) * 2%:
                x_start = (75 - rating) * 0.02
                x_max = x_start + 0.50
                x_kink = x_start + 0.75 * (x_max - x_start) # 75% of the way
                return (x_start, x_kink, x_max)

              # ------------------------------------------------------------------
              # RRC Calculation
              # ------------------------------------------------------------------

              def calculate_rrc_coverage(
                rating,
                exposure_internal,
                exposure_total,
                liquid_surplus_internal,
                total_exposure_beyond_surplus,
                total_collateral
              ):
                """
                Returns the coverage fraction (0 - 1) for a given rating & scenario.
                For the absolute coverage amount, multiply coverage_fraction
                by `exposure_internal`.
                """

                # 1) Compute the two driver ratios
                f1 = max(0.0, total_exposure_beyond_surplus / total_collateral) # Ensuring it is non-negative when surplus > exposure
                f2 = (exposure_internal + 0.1 * (exposure_total - exposure_internal)) / liquid_surplus_internal

                # 2) Determine which category the rating is in
                if rating <= 25:
                  # TRR Category 1 (Low Risk) => use only f1 piecewise
                  x_start, x_kink, x_max = f1_thresholds_low_risk(rating)
                  coverage_fraction = piecewise_coverage(f1, x_start, x_kink, x_max)

                elif rating <= 50:
                  # TRR Category 2 (Medium Risk) => blend coverage from f1-curve and f2-curve
                  # First get coverage from the "f1 low-risk"
                  x_start_1, x_kink_1, x_max_1 = f1_thresholds_low_risk(25)
                  cov_f1 = piecewise_coverage(f1, x_start_1, x_kink_1, x_max_1)

                  # Then get coverage from the "f2 high-risk"
                  x_start_2, x_kink_2, x_max_2 = f2_thresholds_high_risk(50)
                  cov_f2 = piecewise_coverage(f2, x_start_2, x_kink_2, x_max_2)

                  # Blend factor alpha
                  alpha = (rating - 25) / (50 - 25)
                  coverage_fraction = (1 - alpha) * cov_f1 + 0.15 * alpha * cov_f2

                elif rating <= 75:
                  # TRR Category 3 (High Risk) => use only f2
                  x_start, x_kink, x_max = f2_thresholds_high_risk(rating)
                  coverage_fraction = piecewise_coverage(f2, x_start, x_kink, x_max)

                else:
                  # TRR Category 4 (Extreme Risk) => special piecewise lumps.
                  if rating > 75:
                    return 1.0

                return coverage_fraction

```

bd1f39ac:610687f307952ff69f22ac2e034cd44.title: F2 Function
bd1f39ac:610687f307952ff69f22ac2e034cd44.content:
The F2 parameter $f\_2$ is calculated as follows:

$$f\_{2} = \\dfrac{e\_{\\text{int}} + a \\,\\bigl(e\_{\\text{tot}} - e\_{\\text{int}}\\bigr)}{s\_{\\text{liq}}}$$

Here $\\alpha$ is equal to `0.1`.

The parameters of this function are defined in A.3.3 - Variable Definitions.

bd1f39ac:6d1ea8db839f663d5a30b9884c71b23.content:
The F1 parameter $f\_{1}$ is calculated as follows:

$$f\_{1} = \\dfrac{E\_{\\text{beyond}}}{C\_{\\text{tot}}}$$

The parameters of this function are defined in A.3.3 - Variable Definitions.

bd1f39ac:63ae6550ce3c1f4dc027d6d4ac1fc73.title: Delay Factor
bd1f39ac:63ae6550ce3c1f4dc027d6d4ac1fc73.content:
The Delay Adjustment Factor $\\text{DF}$ is a factor indicating the extent to which the risk associated with backdoor access is mitigated by a security delay between the time that a change using backdoor access is approved and the time that such a change becomes effective. This delay gives users time to raise issues or withdraw funds in the event of malicious or undesirable use of backdoor access.

The Delay Factor is `1` if there is no security delay and `0` if the security delay is 48 hours or greater. For security delays between 0 hours and 48 hours, the Delay Factor is linearly reduced for each hour of security delay. So a security delay of 24 hours would result in a Delay Factor of `0.5`.

c43b5e3e:7d254ea3e880b8c751d9715955d7d58.title: Administrative Risk Rating Calculation
c43b5e3e:7d254ea3e880b8c751d9715955d7d58.content:
The first step in calculating the Instance Administrative RRC with respect to an Allocation System opportunity is to calculate the Administrative Risk Rating $\\text{ARR}$ for the protocol being invested in. The $\\text{ARR}$ is calculated as follows:

$$\\text{ARR} = min\[\\text{CAP}, \\text{SR} \\times \\text{DF} \\times \\text{LAF}\]$$

Here $min$ is the mathematical minimum function that returns the lesser of the specified parameters.

The parameters of this formula are specified in the subdocuments herein.

c43b5e3e:00497dbffdabb1e4685919382db3251.title: Independent Calculation By BA Labs On Behalf Of Core Council
c43b5e3e:00497dbffdabb1e4685919382db3251.content: Within five (5) calendar days of the posting of each Initial Calculation, BA Labs, on behalf of the Core Council, replies to the Initial Calculation with their own independent calculation of the net amounts due to or from the Prime Agents covered by the Initial Calculation (the “Independent Calculation”). The Independent Calculation must specify whether each amount is an Agreed Amount or a Disputed Amount (see A.2.6 - Allowed Deviation) and contain reasonable supporting detail. The required contents of the Independent Calculation will be further specified in a future iteration of the Atlas.

c43b5e3e:3c4c6d6d82adefe2ea703a358740368.title: Demand Side Stablecoin Primitive Recipients
c43b5e3e:3c4c6d6d82adefe2ea703a358740368.content: For each Prime Agent, the Initial Calculation must specify whether payments with respect to Demand Side Stablecoin Primitives (see A.2.4 - A8 - Demand Side Stablecoin Primitives) have already been made by the Operational Executor Agent, and thus should be reimbursed to the Operational Executor Agent instead of being paid to the Prime Agent.
ancestors: Initial Calculation By Operational Executor Agent

c43b5e3e:f1f993720bf161835004cc9d8266cff.title: Agreed Amount
c43b5e3e:f1f993720bf161835004cc9d8266cff.content: The net amount due to or from a Prime Agent in an Initial Calculation is an Agreed Amount if the absolute value of the percentage difference between the amounts in the Initial Calculation and the Independent Calculation is less than or equal to the Allowed Deviation (see A.2.6 - Allowed Deviation). The net amount due to or from a Prime Agent in an Independent Calculation is also an Agreed Amount if there is no Initial Calculation (see A.2.6 - Missing Initial Calculations).
ancestors: Independent Calculation By BA Labs On Behalf Of Core Council

c43b5e3e:290e96f92604375333c6d944fe6e5aa.title: Initial Calculation By Operational Executor Agent
c43b5e3e:290e96f92604375333c6d944fe6e5aa.content: Within five (5) calendar days of the end of each month, each Operational Executor Agent posts on the Sky Forum a calculation of the net amounts due to or from the Prime Agents that it has an Executor Accord with (the “Initial Calculation”). The Initial Calculation must be posted under the “Sky Core” category using the \`monthly-settlement-cycle\` tag and must contain reasonable supporting detail. The required contents of the Initial Calculation will be further specified in a future iteration of the Atlas.

c43b5e3e:c33ada595dd2223ed3e30df670dccc8.title: Disputed Amount
c43b5e3e:c33ada595dd2223ed3e30df670dccc8.content: The net amount due to or from a Prime Agent in an Initial Calculation is a Disputed Amount if it is not an Agreed Amount.
ancestors: Independent Calculation By BA Labs On Behalf Of Core Council

c43b5e3e:5e09611ecee197bf3741fc963742566.title: Process Definition
c43b5e3e:5e09611ecee197bf3741fc963742566.content: The documents herein define the initial process for performing the Monthly Settlement Cycle. The calculations to be performed as part of the Monthly Settlement Cycle are defined in A.2.6 - Implementation Stages. This process definition specifies who performs the calculations and how funds are ultimately paid out.

c43b5e3e:b9ee80b0b7dc7ae079950fcd2d84e6d.title: Allowed Deviation
c43b5e3e:b9ee80b0b7dc7ae079950fcd2d84e6d.content: The Allowed Deviation is the maximum allowed deviation, on a percentage basis, between the net amount due to or from a Prime Agent in the Initial Calculation and Independent Calculation before resolution of these differences is required. It recognizes that if the Initial Calculation and Independent Calculation are truly developed independently then differences in methodology are likely to result in small deviations.
ancestors: Independent Calculation By BA Labs On Behalf Of Core Council

c43b5e3e:001e9aad8b7138d90502a2400984b30.title: Implementation
c43b5e3e:001e9aad8b7138d90502a2400984b30.content: The documents herein define the initial implementation of the Monthly Settlement Cycle. This initial implementation of the Monthly Settlement Cycle does not include the Senior Risk Capital System, which is still being developed, and funds continue to be allocated through Executive Votes rather than the allocation steps of the Treasury Management Function. See A.2.5 - Treasury Management - Treasury Management - Short Term Transitionary Measures.

c43b5e3e:e7850873b8492572d1eaab74883a04a.title: Operational Processes
c43b5e3e:e7850873b8492572d1eaab74883a04a.content:
The Monthly Settlement Cycle (MSC) synchronizes several key operational processes across the ecosystem, including:

1.  Sky Protocol's net revenue from the previous month is calculated and allocated through the steps of the Treasury Management Function. See A.2.5.
2.  The monthly Senior Risk Capital (SRC) origination process is settled: the clearing price is established, costs are deducted from winning Prime Agents' accounts, and their accounts are credited with Originated SRC (OSRC) for the upcoming month. See 3.3 - Settlement Of Origination.
3.  Queued conversions between USDS and srUSDS within the SRC system are processed. See A.3.3 - Deposit And Redemption Queues.
4.  Pioneer Incentive Pools are funded with an amount equivalent to the Sky Savings Rate multiplied by the balance of Unrewarded USDS. See A.2.4 - Pioneer Chain Primitive.
5.  The Smart Burn Buffer's burning operation occurs synchronously with each Monthly Settlement Cycle. At each cycle, the system calculates the appropriate Burn Rate based on current market conditions and executes the burn operation, if applicable, according to the formula specified in the Atlas. See A.2.5 - Treasury Management - Treasury Management - Allocation Steps - Step 4: Smart Burn And Standard Activity Staking Rewards - Smart Burn Buffer - Usage Of Smart Burn Buffer.
6.  Critical Core GovOps functions related to the operationalization of Sky Primitives are executed, including payment/reimbursement processing, compliance monitoring, and the calculation and application of retroactive penalties.

c43b5e3e:2035f02425d4f130e8451e9de008f8d.title: Resolution Of Differences By Core GovOps Atlas Axis
c43b5e3e:2035f02425d4f130e8451e9de008f8d.content:
If there are any Disputed Amounts (see A.2.6 - Disputed Amount), then Core GovOps Atlas Axis must resolve them. Atlas Axis must work with the relevant Operational Executor Agent, relevant Prime Agents, and BA Labs to reach a mutually acceptable resolution and may consult other parties to the extent it deems advisable.

Core GovOps Atlas Axis makes the final decision in resolving differences between the Initial Calculation and the Independent Calculation (the “Final Calculation”). Atlas Axis must post the Final Calculation as a reply to the Independent Calculation within five (5) calendar days of the posting of an Independent Calculation that includes a Disputed Amount. The Final Calculation must specify the Final Amount and contain reasonable supporting detail. The required contents of the Final Calculation will be further specified in a future iteration of the Atlas.

c43b5e3e:bb31dacabb47b044be15b452d696593.title: Missing Initial Calculations
c43b5e3e:bb31dacabb47b044be15b452d696593.content: If an Operational Executor Agent does not deliver the Initial Calculation as specified in A.2.6 - Initial Calculation By Operational Executor Agent, BA Labs must prepare an Independent Calculation with respect to the Prime Agents covered by such Initial Calculation within ten (10) calendar days of the end of each month. The Independent Calculation must be posted under the “Sky Core” category using the \`monthly-settlement-cycle tag\`, contain reasonable supporting detail, and specify that no Initial Calculation was posted by the Operational Executor Agent.
ancestors: Independent Calculation By BA Labs On Behalf Of Core Council

c43b5e3e:3e8347837ec04f323a4fe60bedc0d7d.title: Final Amount
c43b5e3e:3e8347837ec04f323a4fe60bedc0d7d.content: The net amount due to or from a Prime Agent in a Final Calculation is a Final Amount.
ancestors: Resolution Of Differences By Core GovOps Atlas Axis

c43b5e3e:9ab9b84a809ee84239672b502579536.title: Allowed Deviation Current Value
c43b5e3e:9ab9b84a809ee84239672b502579536.content: The current value of the Allowed Deviation is 1%.
ancestors: Independent Calculation By BA Labs On Behalf Of Core Council

c43b5e3e:3ca47892fd33eb805c447e3a2dc1d83.title: Disputes By Prime Agents
c43b5e3e:3ca47892fd33eb805c447e3a2dc1d83.content:
A Prime Agent may dispute the calculation of the net amount due to or from it (a “Dispute Notice”). The Dispute Notice must be posted as a reply to the Initial Calculation within five (5) calendar days of the posting of the Initial Calculation. The Dispute Notice must specify the errors in the Initial Calculation and the Prime’s own calculation of the net amount due to or from it. The required contents of the Dispute Notice will be further specified in a future iteration of the Atlas.

Core GovOps Atlas Axis may at its discretion resolve the differences between the calculations using the process specified in A.2.6 - Resolution Of Differences By Core GovOps Atlas Axis. Alternatively, Atlas Axis may elect to determine the correct amount and true up any differences in the next Monthly Settlement Cycle as specified in A.2.6 - True Up In Subsequent Monthly Settlement Cycle. In either case Atlas Axis must post its decision as a reply to the Dispute Notice.
ancestors: Resolution Of Differences By Core GovOps Atlas Axis

c43b5e3e:74eb94f9f7430eb79fd586ca5497a4f.title: Settlement Through Sky Core Executive Vote
c43b5e3e:74eb94f9f7430eb79fd586ca5497a4f.content: When all amounts due to or from Prime Agents are Agreed Amounts or Final Amounts then the Core Facilitator must include payments of these amounts in the next Sky Core Executive Vote as specified herein.

c43b5e3e:2ad260d7ac07348bacd446a878d5e8d.title: True Up In Subsequent Monthly Settlement Cycle
c43b5e3e:2ad260d7ac07348bacd446a878d5e8d.content:
If the amounts of any payments included in the Sky Core Executive Vote (see A.2.6 - Settlement Through Sky Core Executive Vote) are subsequently determined to be incorrect, adjustments are included in the next Monthly Settlement Cycle to ensure that each party pays the amount it owes or receives the amount to which it is entitled.

Core GovOps Atlas Axis must prepare a statement specifying the errors, the correct amounts, and the adjustments needed (the “Correction Calculation”). The Correction Calculation must be posted to the Sky Forum under the “Sky Core” category with the \`monthly-settlement-cycle\` tag. The required contents of the Correction Calculation will be further specified in a future iteration of the Atlas.

c43b5e3e:46a514b15c9d791fe8d1d0590e7d309.title: Reimbursement To Accessibility Reward Wallet And Integration Boost Wallets
c43b5e3e:46a514b15c9d791fe8d1d0590e7d309.content: On an interim basis, Accessibility Reward reimbursements may also be made to the Accessibility Reward Controller Wallet (see A.2.4 - Near-Term Process) at the request of an Operational Executor Agent. Similarly, Integration Boost reimbursements may also be made to the Integration Boost Wallet (see A.2.4 - Near Term Process) at the request of an Operational Executor Agent.

Reimbursement Of Payments Made By Operational Executor Agents

c43b5e3e:8cbf2d79a2d54fe825cb7b513d55802.title: Interim Measures
c43b5e3e:8cbf2d79a2d54fe825cb7b513d55802.content: The documents herein define interim exceptions to the process definition for the Monthly Settlement Cycle.

c43b5e3e:019bbbd1de22b139e8f706d03107238.title: Reimbursement Of Payments Made By Operational Executor Agents
c43b5e3e:019bbbd1de22b139e8f706d03107238.content: Reimbursements of payments already made by the Operational Executor Agent with respect to Demand Side Stablecoin Primitives (see A.2.4 - A8 - Demand Side Stablecoin Primitives) are transferred to the Operational Executor Agent's Buffer through an Executive Vote.

c43b5e3e:3e28e37521bbc8983c4c64c92304891.title: Scope Of September 2025 Monthly Settlement Cycle
c43b5e3e:3e28e37521bbc8983c4c64c92304891.content: The initial Monthly Settlement Cycle conducted in September 2025 will be for the two month period from July 1, 2025 to August 31, 2025.

c43b5e3e:e17732e498e0f2b0f40ef628563e7eb.title: Collection Of Amounts Due From Prime Agents
c43b5e3e:e17732e498e0f2b0f40ef628563e7eb.content: Amounts due from Prime Agents, excluding reimbursements made to Operational Executor Agents (see A.2.6 - Reimbursement Of Payments Made By Operational Executor Agents) are settled in a way that is equivalent to a transfer from the Prime to the Sky Surplus Buffer through actions included in an Executive Vote.

c43b5e3e:7b70f6a6322384f97239601911a1c3f.title: Process For September 2025 Monthly Settlement Cycle
c43b5e3e:7b70f6a6322384f97239601911a1c3f.content: For the initial Monthly Settlement Cycle conducted in September 2025, the Initial Calculation prepared by Operational Executor Agent Amatsu will only include calculations related to Demand Side Stablecoin Primitives (see A.2.4 - A8 - Demand Side Stablecoin Primitives). The Independent Calculation prepared by BA Labs on behalf of the Core Council will be prepared normally. The calculations related to Demand Side Stablecoin Primitives will be subject to the normal resolution process defined in A.2.6 - Resolution Of Differences By Core GovOps Atlas Axis. For all other calculations, the amounts in the Independent Calculation will be treated as Agreed Amounts. The Initial Calculation and the Independent Calculation will be posted to the Sky Forum by September 10, 2025.

c43b5e3e:6ad7611dab9d87ebf67d0e67e9214b3.title: Payment Of Amounts Due To Prime Agents
c43b5e3e:6ad7611dab9d87ebf67d0e67e9214b3.content: Amounts due to Prime Agents, excluding reimbursements made to Operational Executor Agents (see A.2.6 - Reimbursement Of Payments Made By Operational Executor Agents), are transferred from the Sky Surplus Buffer to the Prime SubProxy Account through an Executive Vote.

c43b5e3e:6a6135e7454cf62513ef07e933eb86e.title: Distribution Requirement Primitive
c43b5e3e:6a6135e7454cf62513ef07e933eb86e.content:
The Distribution Requirement Primitive requires Agents to periodically buy and distribute 0.25% of their token supply per year. The annual requirement of 0.25% of the token supply is divided into twelve (12) equal monthly distributions. Distributions must occur on the first day of each month, with tokens purchased by the Prime Agent on the open market and transferred to an address designated by Sky Core in A.2.4 - Sky Core-Designated Address.

Prime Agents choose between fulfilling either the Distribution Requirement Primitive or the Market Cap Fee Primitive.

c43b5e3e:7bc7fcdecbd2b1baea630e66128565b.title: Calculation of Distributed Tokens
c43b5e3e:7bc7fcdecbd2b1baea630e66128565b.content: The value of the distributed tokens is calculated as the number of tokens distributed, multiplied by the Time-Weighted Average Price (TWAP) of the token over the 24-hour period ending at 23:59 UTC on the last day of each month, immediately preceding the distribution event. This value is applied in the rebate calculation under the Upkeep Rebate Primitive. See A.2.4 - Upkeep Rebate Primitive.

c43b5e3e:b5a81941444a1d30c9321d1a7906176.title: Ecosystem Upkeep Primitives
c43b5e3e:b5a81941444a1d30c9321d1a7906176.content: Ecosystem Upkeep Primitives ensure that all Agents contribute to long-term ecosystem sustainability. Prime Agents must choose between either the Distribution Requirement Primitive or the Market Cap Fee Primitive; whereas the Upkeep Rebate Primitive applies universally to all Prime Agents. The term "Ecosystem Upkeep Fees" refers to the upkeep obligation of a Prime Agent pursuant to either the Distribution Requirement Primitive or the Market Cap Fee Primitive.

c43b5e3e:29587032d36f96c749d28d534dadf16.title: Market Cap Fee Primitive
c43b5e3e:29587032d36f96c749d28d534dadf16.content:
The Market Cap Fee Primitive requires Prime Agents to pay an annual fee equivalent to 0.30% of their market capitalization to Sky, accounted for monthly. The annual fee of 0.30% of the market capitalization is divided into twelve (12) equal monthly payments, equating to 0.025% of the market capitalization per month. Payments must occur on the first day of each month, with the fee transferred to an address designated by Sky Core in A.2.4 - Sky Core-Designated Address.

Prime Agents choose between fulfilling either the Distribution Requirement Primitive or the Market Cap Fee Primitive.

c43b5e3e:6cd403525dc9b175ba29c8279d1962d.title: Light Agent Primitive
c43b5e3e:6cd403525dc9b175ba29c8279d1962d.content: The Light Agent Primitive enables users to create Light Agents, which are sub-agents operating on top of the Agent's Executor Accord, conferring the advantages of Sky GovOps at a lower cost, but without direct access to other Sky Primitives.

c43b5e3e:e37bacf7bd554b4e086b55b383fcad8.content: The address to which the fee must be transferred will be specified in a future iteration of the Atlas.

c43b5e3e:871971ac1251701c30285908d3ee446.title: Prerequisites For Activating Agent Creation Primitive
c43b5e3e:871971ac1251701c30285908d3ee446.content: The Agent Creation Primitive is the first Sky Primitive that must be activated by prospective Agent founders. Because an Agent Artifact does not yet exist at this stage, the prerequisite requirements set forth herein must be met, including off-chain obligations and governance outputs. Only after satisfying these prerequisites does the Agent Creation Primitive become accessible to the prospective founder.

c43b5e3e:34a9e3809a263b4373ca4cd45784eb6.content: After the prospective Agent founder deploys the required startup capital and pays the Agent creation fee, Core GovOps creates a Proto-Agent and sets up a Scaffold Agent Artifact.
