c43b5e3e:cf109162306586c1ef4ead5077200d7.title: Agent Artifact Document Specification
c43b5e3e:cf109162306586c1ef4ead5077200d7.content: In the Sky Primitives Data Schema, references to an Agent Artifact Document are made in terms of the generic Document type. See A.1.2 - Atlas Documents - Structure, Categories, And Types Of Atlas Documents - List Of Document Types And Their Specifications. In practice, each Agent has its own Instance of that Document type in its Artifact. Thus, when a Primitive's process flow indicates that an Agent Artifact Document must be updated, it is to be interpreted as referring to the specific Instance of that Document type in the Prime Agent's Artifact.

c43b5e3e:f0ed83bd56bfb4f3980f23138322543.title: Proto-Agent Creation
c43b5e3e:f0ed83bd56bfb4f3980f23138322543.content: Core GovOps creates a Proto-Agent with no specific functionality in the ecosystem.
c43b5e3e:f0ed83bd56bfb4f3980f23138322543.parentTitle: Prerequisites For Activating Agent Creation Primitive

c43b5e3e:436b56c9d42de16881ee31a4772e757.title: Valuation
c43b5e3e:436b56c9d42de16881ee31a4772e757.content: The market capitalization is determined as the total token supply multiplied by the TWAP of the token over the 24-hour period ending at 23:59 UTC on the last day of each month, immediately preceding the payment event. This value is applied in the rebate calculation under the Upkeep Rebate Primitive. See A.2.4 - Upkeep Rebate Primitive.

c43b5e3e:cc23c277197c2fb3866bf17bf8f2bf0.title: Upkeep Rebate Primitive
c43b5e3e:cc23c277197c2fb3866bf17bf8f2bf0.content:
The Upkeep Rebate Primitive allows a Prime Agent (”Holding Agent”) to claim a rebate on its Ecosystem Upkeep Fees when it holds any portion of the token supply of another Prime Agent (”Issuing Agent”).

Ecosystem Upkeep Fees are accounted on a monthly basis. The Upkeep Rebate is calculated on the same cadence per Holding Agent as follows:

1.  The Holding Agent’s share of the Issuing Agent’s token supply at the time the Issuing Agent pays its Ecosystem Upkeep Fees, multiplied by
2.  The total monthly Ecosystem Upkeep Fees paid by the Issuing Agent. For a Prime Agent deploying the Distribution Requirement Primitive, the value of its total monthly Ecosystem Upkeep Fee is calculated pursuant to A.2.4 - Calculation of Distributed Tokens. For a Prime Agent deploying the Market Cap Fee Primitive, the value of its total monthly Ecosystem Upkeep Fee is calculated pursuant to A.2.4 - Valuation.

This resulting rebate amount is applied against the Holding Agent’s Ecosystem Upkeep Fees due in the calendar month immediately following the Issuing Agent’s payment.

c43b5e3e:332c874b5257929bd28232466c29b00.title: SkyLink Primitives
c43b5e3e:332c874b5257929bd28232466c29b00.content: SkyLink Primitives are Sky Primitives that are technical infrastructure that extends the Sky Protocol. SkyLink Primitives are built autonomously by Prime Agents, but owned by Sky Core and shared among all Prime Agents. Prime Agents are reimbursed for the cost of setting up SkyLink Primitives and given additional first-mover incentives.

bd1f39ac:f710e05a7fccfdf592bc2befbb36a7b.title: Independent Calculation By Core Council Risk Advisor On Behalf Of Core Council
bd1f39ac:f710e05a7fccfdf592bc2befbb36a7b.content: Within five (5) calendar days of the posting of each Initial Calculation, the Core Council Risk Advisor, on behalf of the Core Council, replies to the Initial Calculation with their own independent calculation of the net amounts due to or from the Prime Agents covered by the Initial Calculation (the “Independent Calculation”). The Independent Calculation must specify whether each amount is an Agreed Amount or a Disputed Amount (see A.2.6 - Allowed Deviation) and contain reasonable supporting detail. The required contents of the Independent Calculation will be further specified in a future iteration of the Atlas.

bd1f39ac:3c4c6d6d82adefe2ea703a358740368.title: Demand Side Stablecoin Primitive Recipients
bd1f39ac:3c4c6d6d82adefe2ea703a358740368.content: For each Prime Agent, the Initial Calculation must specify whether payments with respect to Demand Side Stablecoin Primitives (see A.2.4 - A8 - Demand Side Stablecoin Primitives) have already been made by the Operational Executor Agent, and thus should be reimbursed to the Operational Executor Agent instead of being paid to the Prime Agent.
ancestors: Initial Calculation By Operational Executor Agent

bd1f39ac:f1f993720bf161835004cc9d8266cff.title: Agreed Amount
bd1f39ac:f1f993720bf161835004cc9d8266cff.content: The net amount due to or from a Prime Agent in an Initial Calculation is an Agreed Amount if the absolute value of the percentage difference between the amounts in the Initial Calculation and the Independent Calculation is less than or equal to the Allowed Deviation (see A.2.6 - Allowed Deviation). The net amount due to or from a Prime Agent in an Independent Calculation is also an Agreed Amount if there is no Initial Calculation (see A.2.6 - Missing Initial Calculations).
ancestors: Independent Calculation By Core Council Risk Advisor On Behalf Of Core Council

bd1f39ac:290e96f92604375333c6d944fe6e5aa.title: Initial Calculation By Operational Executor Agent
bd1f39ac:290e96f92604375333c6d944fe6e5aa.content: Within five (5) calendar days of the end of each month, each Operational Executor Agent posts on the Sky Forum a calculation of the net amounts due to or from the Prime Agents that it has an Executor Accord with (the “Initial Calculation”). The Initial Calculation must be posted under the “Sky Core” category using the \`monthly-settlement-cycle\` tag and must contain reasonable supporting detail. The required contents of the Initial Calculation will be further specified in a future iteration of the Atlas.

bd1f39ac:c33ada595dd2223ed3e30df670dccc8.title: Disputed Amount
bd1f39ac:c33ada595dd2223ed3e30df670dccc8.content: The net amount due to or from a Prime Agent in an Initial Calculation is a Disputed Amount if it is not an Agreed Amount.
ancestors: Independent Calculation By Core Council Risk Advisor On Behalf Of Core Council

bd1f39ac:5e09611ecee197bf3741fc963742566.title: Process Definition
bd1f39ac:5e09611ecee197bf3741fc963742566.content: The documents herein define the initial process for performing the Monthly Settlement Cycle. The calculations to be performed as part of the Monthly Settlement Cycle are defined in A.2.6 - Implementation Stages. This process definition specifies who performs the calculations and how funds are ultimately paid out.

bd1f39ac:b9ee80b0b7dc7ae079950fcd2d84e6d.title: Allowed Deviation
bd1f39ac:b9ee80b0b7dc7ae079950fcd2d84e6d.content: The Allowed Deviation is the maximum allowed deviation, on a percentage basis, between the net amount due to or from a Prime Agent in the Initial Calculation and Independent Calculation before resolution of these differences is required. It recognizes that if the Initial Calculation and Independent Calculation are truly developed independently then differences in methodology are likely to result in small deviations.
ancestors: Independent Calculation By Core Council Risk Advisor On Behalf Of Core Council

c43b5e3e:aed42a9093a49a26051313b1569f10f.title: Sale Of Investments When Ethena Exposure Limit Is Exceeded
c43b5e3e:aed42a9093a49a26051313b1569f10f.content: If a Prime Agent's Ethena Exposures exceed its Ethena Exposure Limit, then the Core Council may direct the Agent to sell Ethena Exposures to reduce its Ethena Exposures below its Ethena Exposure Limit.

c43b5e3e:f2ba78b01ae50264bda16b82c7df2e1.content: Superstate Aggregate Exposure is the sum of Superstate Exposures (see A.3.3 - Superstate Required Risk Capital) across all Prime Agents in the Sky Ecosystem.

c43b5e3e:36f3465fc55fc3c07800086c4c80862.content: No Prime Agent may make an investment in Ethena Exposures that would cause its Ethena Exposures to exceed its Ethena Exposure Limit.

bd1f39ac:aed42a9093a49a26051313b1569f10f.title: Sale Of Investments When Ethena Exposure Limit Is Exceeded
bd1f39ac:aed42a9093a49a26051313b1569f10f.content: If a Prime Agent's Ethena Exposures exceed its Ethena Exposure Limit, then the Core Council may direct the Agent to sell Ethena Exposures to reduce its Ethena Exposures below its Ethena Exposure Limit.

bd1f39ac:f2ba78b01ae50264bda16b82c7df2e1.title: Superstate Aggregate Exposure
bd1f39ac:f2ba78b01ae50264bda16b82c7df2e1.content: Superstate Aggregate Exposure is the sum of Superstate Exposures (see A.3.3 - Superstate Required Risk Capital) across all Prime Agents in the Sky Ecosystem.

bd1f39ac:36f3465fc55fc3c07800086c4c80862.title: Prohibition On Investments That Would Cause Ethena Exposure Limit To Be Exceeded
bd1f39ac:36f3465fc55fc3c07800086c4c80862.content: No Prime Agent may make an investment in Ethena Exposures that would cause its Ethena Exposures to exceed its Ethena Exposure Limit.

bd1f39ac:054186adc3e096e807eb5718c185545.title: Superstate Aggregate Exposure Limit
bd1f39ac:054186adc3e096e807eb5718c185545.content: The Superstate Aggregate Exposure Limit is 500,000,000 USDS.

c43b5e3e:86b45022cf214cfa5c1dca9da2d0cc4.title: Pendle Ethena Exposures
c43b5e3e:86b45022cf214cfa5c1dca9da2d0cc4.content: Pendle Ethena Exposures are exposures from directly holding PT-USDe or PT-sUSDe. The Instance Financial RRC for Pendle Ethena Exposures is specified in the documents herein.

c43b5e3e:bfdf70b81ec2ff71f2ac5a901185792.title: Lending Non-Ethena Related Assets Against Ethena Related Collateral
c43b5e3e:bfdf70b81ec2ff71f2ac5a901185792.content: For non-Ethena related assets lent against Ethena related collateral (e.g. lending USDC against PT-USDe or PT-sUSDe), the Instance Financial RRC Ratio is 4%.

c43b5e3e:d16e8ba7770e858b296c6d52430a664.title: Maturity Greater Than Six Months
c43b5e3e:d16e8ba7770e858b296c6d52430a664.content: Pendle Ethena Exposures with more than six (6) months to maturity require 100% Instance Total RRC.

c43b5e3e:b8db77ff62f418e976c831de25c7c81.title: Maturity Less Than Or Equal To Six Months
c43b5e3e:b8db77ff62f418e976c831de25c7c81.content:
Pendle Ethena Exposures with less than or equal to six (6) months to maturity have Instance Financial RRC calculated as follows:

`Instance Financial RRC = initialValue - ((currentTime - startTime) * decayRatePerSecond)`

The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein.

c43b5e3e:08b667e527f3ff14267c523a4e25ca1.title: Initial Value
c43b5e3e:08b667e527f3ff14267c523a4e25ca1.content: The Initial Value `initialValue` is the Instance Financial RRC when the PT has exactly six (6) months to maturity. The `initialValue` is 10%.

bd1f39ac:8726ac270041caee622875b4387ac1e.title: Ethena Capital Requirement Ratio
bd1f39ac:8726ac270041caee622875b4387ac1e.content: Ethena Exposures consist of Direct Ethena Exposures (see A.3.3 - Direct Ethena Exposures), Indirect Ethena Exposures (see A.3.3 - Indirect Ethena Exposures), and Pendle Ethena Exposures (see A.3.3 - Pendle Ethena Exposures). The Instance Financial CRR for Ethena Exposures is specified in the documents herein.

bd1f39ac:8382455a0a87f4db44acf4e40351897.title: Ethena
bd1f39ac:8382455a0a87f4db44acf4e40351897.content: The near-term treatment for Ethena is specified in the documents herein.

bd1f39ac:de6f10d137946d15c8251f86b6cf5ee.title: Direct Ethena Exposures
bd1f39ac:de6f10d137946d15c8251f86b6cf5ee.content: Direct Ethena Exposures are exposures from directly holding USDe and sUSDe. Direct Ethena Exposures have a 3% Instance Financial CRR.

bd1f39ac:38abf275cb07c5cda6a9b202be0ccbb.title: Near-Term Treatment
bd1f39ac:38abf275cb07c5cda6a9b202be0ccbb.content: In the near term pending development of the implementation of the model for perpetual positions, the Instance Financial RRC Ratios specified in the documents herein will apply.

bd1f39ac:5220d361932c08523c5733d4335e6c5.title: Indirect Ethena Exposures
bd1f39ac:5220d361932c08523c5733d4335e6c5.content:
Indirect Ethena Exposures are exposures from lending against Ethena related assets through lending markets. Indirect Ethena Exposures have Instance Financial CRR as specified in the documents herein.

For Indirect Ethena Exposure through lending markets, only the portion of the exposure to the lending market that is backed by Ethena related assets is subject to the Instance Financial CRR specified in the documents herein. The Instance Financial CRR for the remaining portion of the exposure is calculated based on the nature of the assets backing the exposure.

bd1f39ac:c39bac4e985cdba1bd5c95f60009cb9.title: Perpetual Positions
bd1f39ac:c39bac4e985cdba1bd5c95f60009cb9.content: The implementation of the model for perpetual positions will be specified in a future iteration of the Atlas. The near-term treatment of these assets are specified in the subdocuments herein.

bd1f39ac:a7140f4a83edc46f05e205e82785f81.title: Lending Ethena Related Assets Against Ethena Related Collateral
bd1f39ac:a7140f4a83edc46f05e205e82785f81.content: For Ethena related assets lent against Ethena related collateral (e.g. lending USDe or sUSDe against PT-USDe or PT-sUSDe), the Instance Financial CRR is 3%.

c43b5e3e:7b428a61aecc392ef12c62a026d1214.title: Calculate Required Capital Percentage Using F1 Piecewise Function
c43b5e3e:7b428a61aecc392ef12c62a026d1214.content: The Required Capital Percentage using the F1 Piecewise Function should then be calculated by inputting the F1 parameter calculated in A.3.3 - Calculate F1 Parameter into the Piecewise Function specified in A.3.3 - Piecewise Function using the F1 thresholds specified in A.3.3 - Kink Threshold.

c43b5e3e:a1c4c7fecc8a67295aff3c9c2d2fbc8.title: Calculate F2 Parameter
c43b5e3e:a1c4c7fecc8a67295aff3c9c2d2fbc8.content: The F2 parameter $f\_{2}$ should then be calculated using the methodology specified in A.3.3 - F2 Function.

c43b5e3e:a0af72355ba822199f5ea8a622bbd13.title: Calculate Required Capital Percentage Using F2 Piecewise Function
c43b5e3e:a0af72355ba822199f5ea8a622bbd13.content: The Required Capital Percentage using the F2 Piecewise Function should then be calculated by inputting the F2 parameter calculated in A.3.3 - Calculate F2 Parameter into the Piecewise Function specified in A.3.3 - Piecewise Function using the F2 thresholds specified in A.3.3 - Maximum Threshold.

c43b5e3e:d6b784503ef44704845f933051124ea.title: Calculate F1 Parameter
c43b5e3e:d6b784503ef44704845f933051124ea.content: For medium risk protocols, the F1 parameter $f\_{1}$ should first be calculated using the methodology specified in A.3.3 - F1 Function.

c43b5e3e:2cff41bb820fb7afabd646bdc4c8962.title: Calculate Blended Average Required Capital Percentage
c43b5e3e:2cff41bb820fb7afabd646bdc4c8962.content:
The final Required Capital Percentage $x$ should be calculated as a weighted average of the F1 Required Capital Percentage and the F2 Required Capital Percentage as follows:

$$x = b \\times \\alpha \\times f\_2 + (1 - \\alpha) \\times f\_1$$

The parameters of this formula are defined in the subdocuments herein.

c43b5e3e:443df51487d69502db91ee9dd8a4ba7.title: Medium Risk Protocols
c43b5e3e:443df51487d69502db91ee9dd8a4ba7.content: Medium risk protocols are ones with a Risk Rating greater than `25` but less than or equal to `50`. The methodology for medium risk protocols is specified in the documents herein.

c43b5e3e:8b97912192cdde3af51d4b54258fb1f.title: Constant Factor
c43b5e3e:8b97912192cdde3af51d4b54258fb1f.content: The constant factor $b$ is set to `0.15`.

c43b5e3e:888d7bcfefad95eb2d918eebf277eb2.title: Calculate Required Capital Percentage Using Piecewise Function With F1 Thresholds
c43b5e3e:888d7bcfefad95eb2d918eebf277eb2.content: The Required Capital Percentage should then be calculated by inputting the F1 parameter calculated in A.3.3 - Calculate F1 Parameter into the Piecewise Function specified in A.3.3 - Piecewise Function using the F1 thresholds specified in A.3.3 - Kink Threshold.

c43b5e3e:79d107e0a35094bdf398ae2e4e58da5.title: Calculate F1 Parameter
c43b5e3e:79d107e0a35094bdf398ae2e4e58da5.content: For low risk protocols, the F1 parameter $f\_{1}$ should first be calculated using the methodology specified in A.3.3 - F1 Function.

c43b5e3e:78d4fe3e0ae63cf8aeba3b2f3172a8c.title: Low Risk Protocols
c43b5e3e:78d4fe3e0ae63cf8aeba3b2f3172a8c.content: Low risk protocols are ones with a Risk Rating between less than or equal to `25`. The methodology for low risk protocols is specified in the documents herein.

c43b5e3e:878f695954884db543a09d2925cc146.title: Calculation Of Instance Smart Contract RRC Percentage Based on Risk Category
c43b5e3e:878f695954884db543a09d2925cc146.content: The methodology used to calculate the Instance Smart Contract RRC as a percentage of the exposure depends on the Risk Rating $r$ of the protocol as specified in the documents herein.

c43b5e3e:4290419cb3cd3eaa26d84e10403ab5b.title: Alpha
c43b5e3e:4290419cb3cd3eaa26d84e10403ab5b.content:
Alpha $\\alpha$ is a weighting factor indicating how close the Risk Rating is to the threshold for a High Risk Protocol versus the threshold for a Low Risk Protocol. It is calculated as:

$$\\alpha = \\dfrac{r - 25}{50 - 25}$$

Here $r$ is the Risk Rating of the protocol.

c43b5e3e:f22ad8e07a4c3a621cfe2027fbb829b.title: Calculate Required Capital Percentage Using Piecewise Function With F2 Thresholds
c43b5e3e:f22ad8e07a4c3a621cfe2027fbb829b.content: The Required Capital Percentage should then be calculated by inputting the F2 parameter calculated in A.3.3 - Calculate F2 Parameter into the Piecewise Function specified in A.3.3 - Piecewise Function using the F2 thresholds specified in A.3.3 - Maximum Threshold.

c43b5e3e:4eaea1063a0d06b45e2407ae5b63ed4.title: Calculate F2 Parameter
c43b5e3e:4eaea1063a0d06b45e2407ae5b63ed4.content: For high risk protocols, the F2 parameter $f\_{2}$ should first be calculated using the methodology specified in A.3.3 - F2 Function.

c43b5e3e:d30f88ba1e8430006a71747e0c8eaed.title: Extreme Risk Protocols
c43b5e3e:d30f88ba1e8430006a71747e0c8eaed.content: Extreme risk protocols are ones with a Risk Rating greater than `75`. The methodology for extreme risk protocols is specified in the documents herein.

c43b5e3e:5c545a9270377356e1c6430cb743084.title: High Risk Protocols
c43b5e3e:5c545a9270377356e1c6430cb743084.content: High risk protocols are ones with a Risk Rating greater than `50` but less than or equal to `75`. The methodology for high risk protocols is specified in the documents herein.

c43b5e3e:bdaef30a4b6d7f5845f2bae2aad91e8.title: Maximum Required Risk Capital Percentage
c43b5e3e:bdaef30a4b6d7f5845f2bae2aad91e8.content: For extreme risk protocols, the required capital percentage is automatically set to 100%.

c43b5e3e:6acdede36be2ce5573545df74cdd850.title: F2 Required Capital Percentage
c43b5e3e:6acdede36be2ce5573545df74cdd850.content: The F2 Required Capital Percentage $f\_2$ is the figure calculated as the output of A.3.3 - Calculate Required Capital Percentage Using F2 Piecewise Function.

c43b5e3e:368b2f05a364df34cd447e398907de0.title: Calculation Of Instance Smart Contract RRC Value
c43b5e3e:368b2f05a364df34cd447e398907de0.content: The Instance Smart Contract RRC is equal to the product of (1) the Instance Smart Contract RRC Percentage calculated from A.3.3 - Calculation Of Instance Smart Contract RRC Percentage Based on Risk Category and (2) the exposure to the Allocation System opportunity.

bd1f39ac:fabe70a6c379c75a8355d5fd98694f8.content: The Capital Requirement Ratio using the F1 Piecewise Function should then be calculated by inputting the F1 parameter calculated in A.3.3 - Calculate F1 Parameter into the Piecewise Function specified in A.3.3 - Piecewise Function using the F1 thresholds specified in A.3.3 - Kink Threshold.

bd1f39ac:a1c4c7fecc8a67295aff3c9c2d2fbc8.content: The F2 parameter $f\_{2}$ should then be calculated using the methodology specified in A.3.3 - F2 Function.

bd1f39ac:7dedb76f4834e36448863e9f54a37df.title: Calculate Capital Requirement Ratio Using F2 Piecewise Function
bd1f39ac:7dedb76f4834e36448863e9f54a37df.content: The Capital Requirement Ratio using the F2 Piecewise Function should then be calculated by inputting the F2 parameter calculated in A.3.3 - Calculate F2 Parameter into the Piecewise Function specified in A.3.3 - Piecewise Function using the F2 thresholds specified in A.3.3 - Maximum Threshold.

bd1f39ac:d6b784503ef44704845f933051124ea.content: For medium risk protocols, the F1 parameter $f\_{1}$ should first be calculated using the methodology specified in A.3.3 - F1 Function.

bd1f39ac:2cff41bb820fb7afabd646bdc4c8962.content:
The final Required Capital Percentage $x$ should be calculated as a weighted average of the F1 Required Capital Percentage and the F2 Required Capital Percentage as follows:

The parameters of this formula are defined in the subdocuments herein.

bd1f39ac:210c413445bb73cb5a403c136c695b9.content: The Capital Requirement Ratio should then be calculated by inputting the F1 parameter calculated in A.3.3 - Calculate F1 Parameter into the Piecewise Function specified in A.3.3 - Piecewise Function using the F1 thresholds specified in A.3.3 - Kink Threshold.

bd1f39ac:79d107e0a35094bdf398ae2e4e58da5.content: For low risk protocols, the F1 parameter $f\_{1}$ should first be calculated using the methodology specified in A.3.3 - F1 Function.

bd1f39ac:78d4fe3e0ae63cf8aeba3b2f3172a8c.content: Low risk protocols are ones with a Risk Rating between less than or equal to `25`. The methodology for low risk protocols is specified in the documents herein.

bd1f39ac:0cd49a1a53eb651214cb406383396a3.title: Calculation Of Instance Smart Contract CRR Based on Risk Category
bd1f39ac:0cd49a1a53eb651214cb406383396a3.content: The methodology used to calculate the Instance Smart Contract CRR as a percentage of the exposure depends on the Risk Rating $r$ of the protocol as specified in the documents herein.

bd1f39ac:d34260bda27e667d8e6fe462e6580ac.content: The Capital Requirement Ratio should then be calculated by inputting the F2 parameter calculated in A.3.3 - Calculate F2 Parameter into the Piecewise Function specified in A.3.3 - Piecewise Function using the F2 thresholds specified in A.3.3 - Maximum Threshold.

bd1f39ac:29808f306059a2f2ee94939b56a55b6.content: For extreme risk protocols, the Capital Requirement Ratio is automatically set to 100%.

bd1f39ac:47f3b07043cd59351d4ae7e6d4ae031.title: F2 Capital Requirement Ratio
bd1f39ac:47f3b07043cd59351d4ae7e6d4ae031.content: The F2 Capital Requirement Ratio $f\_2$ is the figure calculated as the output of A.3.3 - Calculate Capital Requirement Ratio Using F2 Piecewise Function.

bd1f39ac:b485be12f396dec16d7eeab8415ec24.title: Calculation Of Instance Smart Contract CRR Value
bd1f39ac:b485be12f396dec16d7eeab8415ec24.content: The Instance Smart Contract CRR is equal to the product of (1) the Instance Smart Contract CRR calculated from A.3.3 - Calculation Of Instance Smart Contract CRR Based on Risk Category and (2) the exposure to the Allocation System opportunity.

c43b5e3e:3e76b48c6906e3271b1b8d3c7de2efc.title: Request By Stability Scope Advisors
c43b5e3e:3e76b48c6906e3271b1b8d3c7de2efc.content: Any requests to change stUSDS parameters set by the stUSDS BEAM must be posted to the Sky Forum by the Stability Scope Advisor recommending the change. Once Utilization is below 100% the Stability Scope Advisors should begin recommending changes based on the methodology specified in A.4.4 - Update Methodology but may deviate from the values resulting from this methodology if they determine that other values are advisable to support the growth of stUSDS and the interests of the Sky Protocol.
ancestors: Manual Parameter Updates By Operator Multisig

c43b5e3e:d55e887e1db2af7cf23afb57b2cf008.title: Manual Parameter Updates By Operator Multisig
c43b5e3e:d55e887e1db2af7cf23afb57b2cf008.content: Initially, the stUSDS parameters set by the stUSDS BEAM are managed by the Operator Multisig based on instructions provided by the Stability Scope Advisors.

c43b5e3e:20ac4d107a22619fdf69fee0c7e9f07.title: Operator Execution
c43b5e3e:20ac4d107a22619fdf69fee0c7e9f07.content: Once a request to change stUSDS parameters has been posted to the Sky Forum by the Stability Scope Advisors, the stUSDS BEAM Operators must prepare and execute the proposed changes in a timely manner. Preparation can include the creation of transaction simulations to verify inputs.
ancestors: Manual Parameter Updates By Operator Multisig

c43b5e3e:84d450b4bbf4b34b80221b2bfe66ca0.title: Initial Parameter Values Set In Executive Vote
c43b5e3e:84d450b4bbf4b34b80221b2bfe66ca0.content:
The initial parameters set by the stUSDS BEAM in the Executive Vote deploying stUSDS and the stUSDS BEAM are:

-   `str` - 0 basis points
-   `duty` - 2,000 basis points
-   `cap` - 200,000,000 USDS
-   `line` - 200,000,000 USDS

c43b5e3e:76b74f7e98b422f765c89ec310cf956.title: Public Communication
c43b5e3e:76b74f7e98b422f765c89ec310cf956.content: Once a change in stUSDS parameters set by the stUSDS BEAM has been executed, the execution must be publicly communicated to the Sky Ecosystem. This communication may take the form of either (1) a Forum post or (2) inclusion of the execution in an informational dashboard that allows community members to see each stUSDS parameter change executed by the stUSDS BEAM.
ancestors: Manual Parameter Updates By Operator Multisig

c43b5e3e:9f4424bf0d9a683e971abfdee57e559.title: Update Process
c43b5e3e:9f4424bf0d9a683e971abfdee57e559.content: The stUSDS parameters set by the stUSDS BEAM are managed by the stUSDS BEAM Operators as specified in the documents herein.

c43b5e3e:eb45d8fb48e4e7d52b12f918ebb087a.title: Automatic Updates By Operator Hot Wallet
c43b5e3e:eb45d8fb48e4e7d52b12f918ebb087a.content: Once the Operator Hot Wallet has been added as an Operator of the stUSDS BEAM (see A.4.4 - Operator Hot Wallet), the stUSDS parameters set by the stUSDS BEAM must be set by the Operator Hot Wallet. These changes must be based on the update methodology specified in A.4.4 - Update Methodology and the results must be publicly visible on an information dashboard.

c43b5e3e:c6babc38f5d78787bf8fab056c458e2.title: Request By Stability Scope Advisors
c43b5e3e:c6babc38f5d78787bf8fab056c458e2.content: Any requests to change rates set by the SP-BEAM must be posted to the Sky Forum by the Stability Scope Advisor that is recommending the change.
ancestors: Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module

c43b5e3e:f53231e5aaa38886deea7c2259ce940.title: Update Process
c43b5e3e:f53231e5aaa38886deea7c2259ce940.content: The rates set by the Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module (SP-BEAM) are managed by the SP-BEAM Operators. The SP-BEAM Operators' use of this authority must wholly adhere to instructions provided by the Stability Scope Advisors.
ancestors: Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module

c43b5e3e:00330b9c4952cf17d407d0c4c04f982.title: Operator Execution
c43b5e3e:00330b9c4952cf17d407d0c4c04f982.content: Once a rate change request has been posted to the Sky Forum by the Stability Scope Advisors, the SP-BEAM Operators must prepare and execute the proposed changes in a timely manner. Preparation can include the creation of transaction simulations to verify inputs.
ancestors: Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module

c43b5e3e:96e666dc2c6e49195db16c56872e34a.title: Operator Update Process
c43b5e3e:96e666dc2c6e49195db16c56872e34a.content: Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module Operators can be modified by the Stability Facilitators, in consultation with the Stability Scope Advisors. This process will be conducted through the Operational Weekly Governance Cycle or, if necessary, through out-of-schedule Executive Votes.
ancestors: Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module

c43b5e3e:43fd69adeecca22f4f5b888ec7c2b63.title: Public Communication
c43b5e3e:43fd69adeecca22f4f5b888ec7c2b63.content: Once a change in rates set by the SP-BEAM has been executed, the execution must be publicly communicated to the Sky Ecosystem. This communication may take the form of either (1) a Forum post or (2) inclusion of the execution in an informational dashboard that allows community members to see each rate change executed by the SP-BEAM.
ancestors: Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module

c43b5e3e:faeabad389975a9e24f81eaa4dcfb12.title: Operator Multisig Modification
c43b5e3e:faeabad389975a9e24f81eaa4dcfb12.content: Core Executor Agent Atlas Axis can change the signers of the Operator Multisig at any time, so long as there are at least three (3) signers and at least a majority of signers are required to execute transactions.
ancestors: Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module

c43b5e3e:a683989486cce81f7ef27039e83e59f.title: Keepers
c43b5e3e:a683989486cce81f7ef27039e83e59f.content: Keeper networks provide critical services for the back-end systems of Sky, enhancing protocol security and efficiency. There are multiple providers of keeper networks in the Sky Ecosystem, decentralizing the keepers and ensuring redundancy. The subdocuments herein specify ongoing payment streams to compensate the different providers of keeper networks.

c43b5e3e:5a58f61e5f3c267a3245bfa3a1cd133.title: Update Methodology
c43b5e3e:5a58f61e5f3c267a3245bfa3a1cd133.content: The documents herein define the methodology that should be used for determining when and how to update stUSDS parameters with the stUSDS BEAM.

c43b5e3e:ee7a6be24ce0c1529c4ab19fa1ba799.title: Short Term Process
c43b5e3e:ee7a6be24ce0c1529c4ab19fa1ba799.content: Initially when stUSDS parameters are set manually by the Operator Multisig (see A.4.4 - Manual Parameter Updates By Operator Multisig), the Stability Scope Advisors may deviate from the long term process specified in A.4.4 - Long Term Process in their best judgment based on the guidelines specified herein.

c43b5e3e:63a90e129712ca4e871ad7f2f1c831e.title: Initial Supply Rate
c43b5e3e:63a90e129712ca4e871ad7f2f1c831e.content: The initial value of the `str` parameter must be set extraordinarily high to a value of approximately 40% initially to incentivize deposits. This rate is not sustainable and must be lowered as specified in A.4.4 - Gradual Reduction In Supply Rate.

bd1f39ac:f917f53a371b94502a0b17d9c2502a7.title: Request By Core Council Risk Advisor
bd1f39ac:f917f53a371b94502a0b17d9c2502a7.content: Any requests to change stUSDS parameters set by the stUSDS BEAM must be posted to the Sky Forum by the Core Council Risk Advisor recommending the change. Once Utilization is below 100% the Core Council Risk Advisor should begin recommending changes based on the methodology specified in A.4.4 - Update Methodology but may deviate from the values resulting from this methodology if they determine that other values are advisable to support the growth of stUSDS and the interests of the Sky Protocol.
ancestors: Manual Parameter Updates By Operator Multisig

bd1f39ac:2dd82418db57f9365509d4dd34390a0.title: Manual Parameter Updates By Operator Multisig
bd1f39ac:2dd82418db57f9365509d4dd34390a0.content: Initially, the stUSDS parameters set by the stUSDS BEAM are managed by the Operator Multisig based on instructions provided by the Core Council Risk Advisor.

bd1f39ac:570be4b7b3ee516f09ac08d3575d018.title: Operator Execution
bd1f39ac:570be4b7b3ee516f09ac08d3575d018.content: Once a request to change stUSDS parameters has been posted to the Sky Forum by the Core Council Risk Advisor, the stUSDS BEAM Operators must prepare and execute the proposed changes in a timely manner. Preparation can include the creation of transaction simulations to verify inputs.

bd1f39ac:84d450b4bbf4b34b80221b2bfe66ca0.content:

-   `str` - 0 basis points
-   `duty` - 2,000 basis points
-   `cap` - 200,000,000 USDS
-   `line` - 200,000,000 USDS

bd1f39ac:eb45d8fb48e4e7d52b12f918ebb087a.title: Automatic Updates By Operator Hot Wallet
bd1f39ac:eb45d8fb48e4e7d52b12f918ebb087a.content: Once the Operator Hot Wallet has been added as an Operator of the stUSDS BEAM (see A.4.4 - Operator Hot Wallet), the stUSDS parameters set by the stUSDS BEAM must be set by the Operator Hot Wallet. c43b5e3e:ffd7a918b8595846415199c8ccaa8b1.title: Smart Contract Risk Required Risk Capital Calculation
c43b5e3e:ffd7a918b8595846415199c8ccaa8b1.content: The third step in calculating the Instance Smart Contract RRC with respect to an Allocation System opportunity is to calculate the Instance Smart Contract RRC as a function of the Smart Contract Risk Rating.

c43b5e3e:68a2209cfe80e4e32a64dcfb3337699.title: Audit Age
c43b5e3e:68a2209cfe80e4e32a64dcfb3337699.content: The Audit Age $auditAge$ is the age, in years, of the audit. The age of the audit should be measured based on the time elapsed between the date the audit report was issued and the date of calculation.

c43b5e3e:a9925b9dcebcf77e6f77eb8b68f07fa.title: Decay Factor
c43b5e3e:a9925b9dcebcf77e6f77eb8b68f07fa.content:
The Decay Factor $decayFactor$ is a parameter indicating how rapidly the effectiveness of audits in reducing risk decreases over time. The $decayFactor$ is calculated as follows:

$$decayFactor =\\begin{cases}1 & \\text{if } auditAge \\leq 2 \\\\\\frac{10 - auditAge}{8} & \\text{if } 2 < auditAge < 10 \\\\0 & \\text{if } auditAge \\geq 10\\end{cases}$$

The parameter of this formula is specified in the subdocument herein.

c43b5e3e:9b251c52c7c32c1e2cf50bd4624a221.title: Starting Rating
c43b5e3e:9b251c52c7c32c1e2cf50bd4624a221.content: The Starting Rate $\\text{SR}$ is an initial risk rating for Administrative Risk before taking into account the Delay Factor and Lindy Adjustment Factor. It is a function of the type of backdoor access that exists to the protocol, as specified in the documents herein.

c43b5e3e:d31704dc40530c96d88ff2cea626d67.title: Administrative Risk Rating Cap
c43b5e3e:d31704dc40530c96d88ff2cea626d67.content: The Administrative Risk Rating Cap $\\text{CAP}$ is a temporary cap on the Administrative Risk Rating. The value of the $\\text{CAP}$ is `30`.

c43b5e3e:2bb27fbbf3feb24ea4bd77b1ff4266b.title: No Backdoor
c43b5e3e:2bb27fbbf3feb24ea4bd77b1ff4266b.content: A protocol with no backdoor access allows no privileged access to the relevant smart contracts by a whitelisted set of users. The Starting Rate for a protocol with no backdoor access is `0`.

c43b5e3e:96c6095fe7a4d1a17c0fd012c607af4.title: Limited Backdoor
c43b5e3e:96c6095fe7a4d1a17c0fd012c607af4.content: A protocol with limited backdoor access allows a set of privileged users to materially modify the terms of the smart contracts (e.g. freezing the transfer of funds) but does not allow root backdoor access as specified in A.3.3 - Root Backdoor. The Starting Rate for a protocol with limited backdoor access is `50`.

c43b5e3e:a9a65fb9675307f96d3817d55129619.title: Root Backdoor
c43b5e3e:a9a65fb9675307f96d3817d55129619.content: A protocol with root backdoor access allows a set of privileged users to make arbitrary changes to the terms of the smart contracts, including transferring user funds. The Starting Rate for a protocol with root backdoor access is `100`.

bd1f39ac:ffd7a918b8595846415199c8ccaa8b1.title: Smart Contract Risk Required Risk Capital Calculation
bd1f39ac:ffd7a918b8595846415199c8ccaa8b1.content: The third step in calculating the Instance Smart Contract RRC with respect to an Allocation System opportunity is to calculate the Instance Smart Contract RRC as a function of the Smart Contract Risk Rating.

bd1f39ac:a9925b9dcebcf77e6f77eb8b68f07fa.title: Decay Factor
bd1f39ac:a9925b9dcebcf77e6f77eb8b68f07fa.content:
The Decay Factor $decayFactor$ is a parameter indicating how rapidly the effectiveness of audits in reducing risk decreases over time. The $decayFactor$ is calculated as follows:

$$decayFactor =\\begin{cases}1 & \\text{if } auditAge \\leq 2 \\\\\\frac{10 - auditAge}{8} & \\text{if } 2 < auditAge < 10 \\\\0 & \\text{if } auditAge \\geq 10\\end{cases}$$

The parameter of this formula is specified in the subdocument herein.

c43b5e3e:6b8d25beb89a2396947946277dd588e.title: Inputs To Instance Smart Contract RRC Calculations
c43b5e3e:6b8d25beb89a2396947946277dd588e.content: The documents herein define functions and parameters that are used in multiple parts of the methodology for calculating the Instance Smart Contract RRC based on the Smart Contract Risk Rating specified in A.3.3 - Calculation Of Instance Smart Contract RRC Percentage Based on Risk Category.

c43b5e3e:4b242b5d73628915868ad5fc86326e2.title: Piecewise Function
c43b5e3e:4b242b5d73628915868ad5fc86326e2.content:
The Piecewise Function $RCC(x)$ calculates a percentage risk capital requirement based on an input $x$ and is defined as follows:

$$\\text{RCC}(x) =\\begin{cases}a & \\text{if } x \\le x\_{\\text{start}}, \\\\\[8pt\]b \\times \\dfrac{x - x\_{\\text{start}}}{x\_{\\text{kink}} - x\_{\\text{start}}} & \\text{if } x\_{\\text{start}} < x \\le x\_{\\text{kink}}, \\\\\[8pt\]b \\;+\\; c \\;\\dfrac{x - x\_{\\text{kink}}}{x\_{\\text{max}} - x\_{\\text{kink}}}& \\text{if } x\_{\\text{kink}} < x < x\_{\\text{max}}, \\\\\[8pt\]d& \\text{if } x \\ge x\_{\\text{max}}.\\end{cases}$$

c43b5e3e:963bebbcfa4ec179faa3d983c78b630.title: Low Risk Parameter
c43b5e3e:963bebbcfa4ec179faa3d983c78b630.content: The low risk parameter $a$ is the output of the piecewise function when the input is at or below the starting threshold. The $a$ parameter is set to `0`.

c43b5e3e:e836271891d41b92509449c28064fd4.title: Medium Risk Parameter
c43b5e3e:e836271891d41b92509449c28064fd4.content: The medium risk parameter $b$ is the output of the piecewise function when the input is equal to the kink threshold. The $b$ parameter is set to `0.25`.

bd1f39ac:2a3ad74e48913ba72248379e4d6316b.title: Inputs To Instance Smart Contract CRR Calculations
bd1f39ac:2a3ad74e48913ba72248379e4d6316b.content: The documents herein define functions and parameters that are used in multiple parts of the methodology for calculating the Instance Smart Contract CRR based on the Smart Contract Risk Rating specified in A.3.3 - Calculation Of Instance Smart Contract CRR Based on Risk Category.

The Piecewise Function $CRR(x)$ calculates a percentage risk capital requirement based on an input $x$ and is defined as follows:

$$\\text{CRR}(x) =\\begin{cases}a & \\text{if } x \\le x\_{\\text{start}}, \\\\\[8pt\]b \\times \\dfrac{x - x\_{\\text{start}}}{x\_{\\text{kink}} - x\_{\\text{start}}} & \\text{if } x\_{\\text{start}} < x \\le x\_{\\text{kink}}, \\\\\[8pt\]b \\;+\\; c \\;\\dfrac{x - x\_{\\text{kink}}}{x\_{\\text{max}} - x\_{\\text{kink}}}& \\text{if } x\_{\\text{kink}} < x < x\_{\\text{max}}, \\\\\[8pt\]d& \\text{if } x \\ge x\_{\\text{max}}.\\end{cases}$$

bd1f39ac:963bebbcfa4ec179faa3d983c78b630.content: The low risk parameter $a$ is the output of the piecewise function when the input is at or below the starting threshold. The $a$ parameter is set to `0`.

940c4fad:ff1c718a61ceb547e1a6f8f56000517.title: Relayer Role
940c4fad:ff1c718a61ceb547e1a6f8f56000517.content:

```

              function setDelegatedSigner(address delegatedSigner)
                external
                onlyRole(RELAYER)
                isActive

```

5cd70e53:6ea0a649304cfe6839001e4c0d306f8.title: Governance Facilitators Must Exercise Due Caution In Reviewing Use Of Multisig
5cd70e53:6ea0a649304cfe6839001e4c0d306f8.content: The list of instances justifying use of the multisig in the Target Document is not intended to be exhaustive. However, the Governance Facilitators must exercise due caution in reviewing and validating use of the multisig in edge cases, i.e., use of the multisig that falls outside of the examples provided in the Target Document. In such “edge cases,” the Governance Facilitators must ensure that a postmortem is publicly published on the Sky Forum which justifies the use of the multisig. The Governance Facilitators should also consider proposing an edit to the Target Document so that the edge case is explicitly included in the examples provided in the Target Document.
5cd70e53:6ea0a649304cfe6839001e4c0d306f8.parentTitle: Immutable Documents Can Be Amended In The Transition To Endgame

5cd70e53:6b2add8af9473df7c7ed5fbdada8c8a.title: Formalizing actions via Governance Poll is encouraged, but not mandatory
5cd70e53:6b2add8af9473df7c7ed5fbdada8c8a.content:
If a Scope Facilitator decides to supersede a particular Atlas document due to its inadequacy in addressing a specific challenge, the Facilitator is encouraged, though not required, to initiate a Governance Poll to allow SKY holders to vote on a revised version of the document that corrects the identified shortcomings. The Target Document does not require Facilitators to run a Governance Poll to formalize their actions.

Similarly, if a Facilitator identifies a gap in the Atlas where a particular need is not explicitly addressed, they may extrapolate a course of action based on their interpretation of the Spirit of the Atlas. In this case, as well, the Target Document does not require Facilitators to run a Governance Poll to formalize their interpretation or extrapolated actions.

This Action Tenet acknowledges the necessity for Facilitators to possess flexible and broad discretionary authority during the early stages of the Atlas' development. Such flexibility ensures that the ecosystem can swiftly adapt to emerging challenges. Consequently, it is important at this stage to avoid over-formalizing actions and decisions taken by Facilitators pursuant to A.0.1 - Atlas Preamble - General Provisions - Facilitators' Broad Discretionary Capacity.
5cd70e53:6b2add8af9473df7c7ed5fbdada8c8a.parentTitle: Immutable Documents Can Be Amended In The Transition To Endgame

5cd70e53:a3d65b87f76e533be36c1dc2e5d5ec0.title: Facilitators must apply strictest possible requirements of Universal Alignment on ACs
5cd70e53:a3d65b87f76e533be36c1dc2e5d5ec0.content:
In any adjudication involving potential misalignment of Alignment Conservers (ACs), Facilitators are unequivocally directed to apply the strictest and highest standards of Universal Alignment.

As ACs are held to the most rigorous standards of Universal Alignment, Facilitators should acknowledge evidence of misalignment if such evidence is deemed at least 51% more likely than not to be valid or to substantiate the presented claim. Additionally, should the overall weight of the evidence demonstrate a 51% or greater chance that the AC committed a misaligned act, the Facilitator is required to derecognize the AC.

Given the exceptionally high stakes in cases of potential AC misalignment, Facilitators must prioritize an approach grounded in an abundance of caution, steering away from notions of 'fairness' or 'lenience.' Any lapse or misjudgment on the part of an AC cannot be excused based on ignorance of the rules, good intentions, honest mistake or similar factors. Maximal accountability for ACs is non-negotiable, a principle underpinned by the indispensable role of ACs as stewards of Universal Alignment.

5cd70e53:1839a6d63846b62b382d7339e733867.title: Facilitators' Authority To Raise Formal Allegation
5cd70e53:1839a6d63846b62b382d7339e733867.content:
Any community member or Aligned Delegate with information pertinent to suspected Alignment Conserver misalignment may take their concerns directly to the Core Facilitator. Upon receiving such information, the Core Facilitator must promptly conduct an initial review to quickly assess the credibility of the concern. Based on this preliminary review, the Core Facilitator must decide whether to initiate a formal adjudication process in accordance with A.1.4 - Alignment Conservers - Accountability And Misalignment Handling - Adjudication Process.

Where the allegation of misalignment concerns a Governance Facilitator, a community member can take their concerns to any other Scope Facilitator, who is then empowered to initiate the formal adjudication process.
5cd70e53:1839a6d63846b62b382d7339e733867.parentTitle: Immutable Documents Can Be Amended In The Transition To Endgame

5cd70e53:f10e537d1a784eb970edca36b07e4e8.title: Change To Minimum Positive Participation Value Cannot Affect Polls That Have Already Begun
5cd70e53:f10e537d1a784eb970edca36b07e4e8.content: "In progress" refers to the state of a Ratification Poll that has already started, where voting is currently taking place. The Target Document thus states that any changes to Minimum Positive Participation values cannot affect polls that have already begun.

5cd70e53:ac0d432861c9579d71341b5ca1d8857.title: Evaluating AC breach of role-specific requirement vs. general requirement
5cd70e53:ac0d432861c9579d71341b5ca1d8857.content: When an Alignment Conserver breaches a role-specific requirement, this is misalignment on par with a breach of a general AC requirement, and vice versa. Facilitators must not default to assigning greater or lesser culpability on the sole basis of whether the breached rule is role-specific or general. Apart from this caveat, misaligned acts can have varying degrees of severity or harm, and should be individually evaluated by the Facilitator in any action.
5cd70e53:ac0d432861c9579d71341b5ca1d8857.parentTitle: Immutable Documents Can Be Amended In The Transition To Endgame

5cd70e53:e3e24c0fd8e4069428fec6e2679a466.title: Immutable Documents Can Be Amended
5cd70e53:e3e24c0fd8e4069428fec6e2679a466.content: Currently, in the transition to Endgame, the Immutable Documents (Articles and Sections) can be amended pursuant to A.1.11 and A.1.12. Once the Sky Ecosystem enters the Endgame State, the Immutable Documents of the Atlas will be forever locked down and cannot be changed.

5cd70e53:2773618cffadb2bc10b844baaf3cfbf.title: Corrections By Governance Facilitators
5cd70e53:2773618cffadb2bc10b844baaf3cfbf.content:
To correct a clear error, the Governance Facilitators may directly update an Active Data document at any time. Prior to taking such action, the Governance Facilitators should notify the respective Responsible Party charged with maintaining the Active Data document.

However, if the error or issue is not clearly evident, the Active Data document must be updated in accordance with the established procedure defined in A.1.13 - Updating Active Data - Update Process - Direct Edit.

5cd70e53:87bb75cf2a8280d722b97349b2d4329.title: Direct Edit
5cd70e53:87bb75cf2a8280d722b97349b2d4329.content:
Active Data with the "Direct Edit" Update Process may be edited pursuant to the following process.

The Responsible Party must post on the Sky Forum their proposed changes to the Active Data, using the category specified by the relevant Facilitator. After confirming that the Responsible Party has the authority to request a Direct Edit, the Core Facilitator shall then modify the Atlas to reflect the Responsible Party's proposed change.

It is permissible for an Active Data Controller to specify unique requirements in addition to the general "Direct Edit" Update Process described above. These additional requirements, if any, must be specified directly in the Active Data Controller Document; this can be done through a reference or citation to the pertinent Atlas document containing the additional requirements. The additional requirements may supplement, but cannot conflict with, any aspect of the "Direct Edit" Update Process defined herein.

5cd70e53:f90ef7cb9d522359d09e93896db6324.title: Alignment Conserver Changes
5cd70e53:f90ef7cb9d522359d09e93896db6324.content:
Active Data with the "Alignment Conserver Changes" Update Process pertains to the Governance Facilitators' maintenance of the Atlas' official listing of some subset of Alignment Conservers.

The triggers of such updates can include, but are not limited to, recognizing a new Alignment Conserver; offboarding an Alignment Conserver at the request of that Alignment Conserver; adding an Alignment Conserver to the list of ACs who have received a formal warning; or derecognizing an Alignment Conserver for misalignment.

The Governance Facilitators can modify the pertinent Active Data documents to reflect such changes immediately; they are not required to create a post on Sky Forum.

5cd70e53:b4e1c063e089f2387c1c0d4cfb51919.title: Update Process
5cd70e53:b4e1c063e089f2387c1c0d4cfb51919.content:
The Active Data Update Process specified in any Active Data Controller document must conform to one of the processes defined in the subdocuments herein.

Since the Update Process element is defined in an Active Data Controller Document, modification of that Update Process element is subject to a SKY vote pursuant to standard governance processes.

5cd70e53:210baf75963d57468cc1f480028305a.title: Agents And The Sky Atlas
5cd70e53:210baf75963d57468cc1f480028305a.content: The documents contained herein define the relationship between the Sky Atlas and Agents, including the pre-eminence of the Sky Core Atlas and how conflicts between the Sky Core Atlas and Agent Artifacts are identified, escalated, and resolved.

5cd70e53:b6e5044a5d2b3a1e6a80b30d0aff561.title: Responsible Party
5cd70e53:b6e5044a5d2b3a1e6a80b30d0aff561.content:
The Responsible Party is the entity responsible for updating the Active Data. The Responsible Party has the permissions and obligation to update the Active Data through the Update Process specified in the respective Active Data Controller Document.

Since the Responsible Party element is defined in an Active Data Controller Document, modification of that Responsible Party element is subject to a SKY vote pursuant to standard governance processes.

5cd70e53:d55402533e64de28a68185e658a4308.title: Sky Atlas Jurisdiction
5cd70e53:d55402533e64de28a68185e658a4308.content: The Sky Atlas is the overarching governance framework for the entire Sky ecosystem and comprises six (6) Scopes in total. The first five Scopes define ecosystem-wide rules and governance processes, while the final Scope contains all Agent Artifacts.

5cd70e53:422cd1094cb3ce895f9832a13fd218a.title: Governance Facilitators' Review
5cd70e53:422cd1094cb3ce895f9832a13fd218a.content: The Governance Facilitators are required to review all Atlas Edit Proposals (AEPs) submitted for Formal Submission to determine whether they are misaligned.

5cd70e53:43cdde846fccf35a09ba8bcd4635af7.title: Submitting To Formal Submission
5cd70e53:43cdde846fccf35a09ba8bcd4635af7.content: When the Atlas Edit Proposal is ready for Formal Submission, the AEP Author submits their AEP to the Monthly Governance Cycle by posting a Forum comment that states "Formal Submission". This can only be done within the Formal Submission Window of a Monthly Governance Cycle. The Formal Submission Window is a two-day window that starts at 00:00 UTC on the first Monday of the Monthly Governance Cycle and lasts until 23:59 UTC on Tuesday the next day.

5cd70e53:fd89a3f90cc5fcf9b94d7431bb293fc.title: Procedure For Blocking AEP For Misalignment
5cd70e53:fd89a3f90cc5fcf9b94d7431bb293fc.content:
An Atlas Edit Proposal can be blocked by the Governance Facilitators for misalignment. Unanimity among the Governance Facilitators is not required to block an AEP for misalignment.

Where an AEP has been blocked for misalignment, the Governance Facilitators must update the AEP status as "Rejected-Misaligned".

Each Governance Facilitator should issue a written advisory opinion containing their findings/reasoning either supporting or rejecting the blocking of the AEP.

5cd70e53:9174d9e020a004cb40182f801b635bd.title: Fulfilled Feedback Period Requirements
5cd70e53:9174d9e020a004cb40182f801b635bd.content: After the Atlas Edit Proposal has fulfilled the requirements for a community feedback period, it is ready for Formal Submission.

5cd70e53:a32df013d5cd79829c208d6b2f48937.title: Resubmitting A Blocked AEP To A Future Monthly Cycle
5cd70e53:a32df013d5cd79829c208d6b2f48937.content: An Atlas Edit Proposal that has been blocked for misalignment can be amended and re-submitted in a future Atlas Edit Monthly Governance Cycle.

5cd70e53:31b6b330ecd29c373a61dae09d78018.title: Request for Comments
5cd70e53:31b6b330ecd29c373a61dae09d78018.content:
After the Atlas Edit Proposal is verified, a period of reviewing by the community and attendant redrafting begins. The minimum duration of this period is determined by the Feedback Period and the Frozen Period.

The Feedback Period is the minimum amount of time within which the community can give feedback in response to an Atlas Edit Proposal before it can advance to Formal Submission.

The Frozen Period is the minimum amount of time during which an Atlas Edit Proposal must remain unchanged before it can advance to Formal Submission.

These periods can overlap.

5cd70e53:c448453bc731cc3afc942f72b0731de.title: Update Status
5cd70e53:c448453bc731cc3afc942f72b0731de.content: If an AEP has passed the Governance Facilitators' review, the Governance Facilitators must update the status of the AEP to "Formal Submission."

02a3eb13:9174d9e020a004cb40182f801b635bd.title: Fulfilled Feedback Period Requirements
02a3eb13:9174d9e020a004cb40182f801b635bd.content: After the Atlas Edit Proposal has fulfilled the requirements for a community feedback period, it is ready for Formal Submission.

02a3eb13:a32df013d5cd79829c208d6b2f48937.title: Resubmitting A Blocked AEP To A Future Monthly Cycle
02a3eb13:a32df013d5cd79829c208d6b2f48937.content: An Atlas Edit Proposal that has been blocked for misalignment can be amended and re-submitted in a future Atlas Edit Monthly Governance Cycle.

02a3eb13:31b6b330ecd29c373a61dae09d78018.title: Request for Comments
02a3eb13:31b6b330ecd29c373a61dae09d78018.content:
After the Atlas Edit Proposal is verified, a period of reviewing by the community and attendant redrafting begins. The minimum duration of this period is determined by the Feedback Period and the Frozen Period.

The Feedback Period is the minimum amount of time within which the community can give feedback in response to an Atlas Edit Proposal before it can advance to Formal Submission.

The Frozen Period is the minimum amount of time during which an Atlas Edit Proposal must remain unchanged before it can advance to Formal Submission.

These periods can overlap.

02a3eb13:184257ac2fcd68e4b2fcbc981506007.content: If an AEP has passed the Core Facilitators' review, the Core Facilitator must update the status of the AEP to "Formal Submission."

d531de16:36c29c3ef6cde44df8641f2473fee71.title: Root Edit Token Holder Vote
d531de16:36c29c3ef6cde44df8641f2473fee71.content:
Where their review of the proposal results in a finding of alignment with the Sky Core Atlas and Spark Artifact, and where the proposal passes review by the SRC (defined as "Passed SRC Review" in SRC Risk Review.), the Operational Facilitator next triggers a Snapshot poll to allow token holders to vote on the proposal. Token holders may vote directly or through Delegates. See Delegation Framework. The poll is open for three (3) days. A poll must have more than 50% of votes cast, excluding abstentions, in favor to be approved.

Spark's governance runs in a weekly cycle that begins every Monday. Upon receiving all approvals, the proposal is automatically included in the next cycle. The cut-off time is Friday 8:00 am UTC to ensure the Operational Facilitator has sufficient time to prepare the needed polls for the following Monday. After the cut-off time, it is at the discretion of the Operational Facilitator whether the proposal can be included in the immediate next cycle, or the following cycle.

d531de16:14fde909c13ecd4054b38acdfea49be.title: Spark
d531de16:14fde909c13ecd4054b38acdfea49be.content: The documents herein specify all of the logic for Spark, including Spark's strategy and how it uses the Sky Primitives to operationalize this strategy.

d531de16:7201d95694779280efc87ed07d3684e.title: Introduction
d531de16:7201d95694779280efc87ed07d3684e.content: Spark is an Agent focused on building on USDS in the Ethereum and adjacent DeFi ecosystem. This includes driving adoption of USDS and deploying collateral backing USDS at attractive risk-adjusted returns. Spark does this through the Spark Liquidity Layer, SparkLend, and Spark Savings.- The Spark Liquidity Layer directly provides USDS, sUSDS, and USDC liquidity across networks and DeFi markets.- SparkLend is a lending market focused on USDS borrowing, sourcing liquidity directly from Sky to provide the best borrow rates for USDS.- Spark Savings enables stablecoin holders to earn the best risk-adjusted rate in DeFi, at large scale, with minimal liquidity constraints.

d531de16:fb8af1b3b99e753dfa932ddd2ad42e1.title: Instance Operational Conformance
d531de16:fb8af1b3b99e753dfa932ddd2ad42e1.content: Operational deviation from Artifact specifications can render an Instance's RRC, and thus the Prime's Aggregate RRC, invalid. Prime Agents must therefore ensure that each Allocation System Instance adheres to its respective Instance Configuration Document. Whether a Prime self-operationalizes its Allocation System or contracts with an Operational Executor Agent, its Agent Artifact must define processes for monitoring for, and addressing deviations of, Instance operational conformance. This document will be developed further in a future iteration of the Atlas.

d531de16:17d10e40ff1f989d3d1be81e05be65a.title: Allocation Instance Adjustments, Scaling, And Settlement
d531de16:17d10e40ff1f989d3d1be81e05be65a.content: On an ongoing basis, the Prime Agent team or Operational GovOps operates the Allocation Instance, scaling exposure up and down. Any change to the Allocation Instance outside of the limits specified in the Prime Agent Artifact or requiring judgment on the part of Operational GovOps (where the Allocation System Instance is operationalized by the Operational Executor Agent) requires a new vote of Prime Agent token holders. See A.2.4 - Modification Of Existing Instances. As part of monthly and quarterly settlement cycles, Core GovOps reviews yields and obligations, applying penalties retroactively for any previously undisclosed violations. In the event of any such violations, Operational GovOps may be required to take escalatory steps based on the fallback strategy in the Prime Agent Artifact.

d531de16:872bd6514f7f6da6043d893a6420704.title: Risk-Capital Incident Response
d531de16:872bd6514f7f6da6043d893a6420704.content:
Where a Prime Agent's Allocation System Instances are operationalized by its Operational Executor Agent, the management of and response to Required Risk Capital (RRC)-related incidents requires a defined framework within each Prime Agent's Artifact (the Multi-Instance Coordinator Document for the Allocation System Primitive) and its associated Executor Accord.

While the Prime Agent's strategic team ("Prime Team") determines the specific rectification strategy for an RRC incident-considering its holistic portfolio, prevailing market conditions, and the potential for strategic acceptance of penalties-this discretion is exercised subject to the authority of Sky Core to impose penalties and take corrective measures, up to and including the conservatorship of a Prime Agent, to protect the ecosystem and make whole losses.

This document will be developed further in a future iteration of the Atlas.

d531de16:441492a76cc2bf7b7718567f69796e3.title: Modification Of Existing Instances
d531de16:441492a76cc2bf7b7718567f69796e3.content: When a Prime Agent wishes to modify an existing Allocation System Primitive Instance in a manner that cannot be accommodated by the existing operational parameters defined in its Agent Artifact, the Prime Agent must initiate an Artifact Edit Proposal process as detailed herein.

d531de16:2a5f558fe64986317935f3a39ec62f1.title: Finalized Determination Of TRC Position And Penalties
d531de16:2a5f558fe64986317935f3a39ec62f1.content:
After reaching a definitive accounting of Prime Agents' capital position and TRC adequacy, penalties are finalized by Core GovOps. This involves reconciling the interim penalty ledger (derived from the OVRC system) with the definitive TRC history, which incorporates all validated information from the TRC Report including any intra-period shortfalls.

1.  If the validated TRC Report indicates that the Prime Agent's TRC was below its Aggregate RRC during the reporting period, and this actual shortfall was more severe than, or not detected by, the OVRC monitoring system, then penalties will be finalized as follows: if the OVRC system had already accrued penalties, these will be adjusted upwards to match the actual shortfall; if the OVRC system had not detected a shortfall, penalties will be assessed and applied retroactively based on the full duration and magnitude of the actual shortfall.
2.  If the validated TRC Report confirms that TRC shortfalls were identical in duration and magnitude to those logged by the OVRC monitoring system throughout the reporting period: the penalties accrued in the interim penalty ledger will be confirmed and finalized.
3.  If the validated TRC Report confirms that TRC was higher than a misleading OVRC reading during a specific portion of the reporting period which led to an erroneously logged penalty: Core GovOps will adjust or void the penalty accordingly.

d531de16:4d44a9bb3603f190afab4771b445663.title: Conditions Requiring Artifact Edit Proposal
d531de16:4d44a9bb3603f190afab4771b445663.content:
An Artifact Edit Proposal is mandatory for an Instance modification under the following conditions:

1.  a desired modification to the Instance's operational parameters falls outside the pre-defined operational ranges codified in the respective Instance Configuration Document or other applicable Artifact Documents; or
2.  a desired modification, even if notionally within defined ranges in the Artifact, is determined by Operational GovOps to materially alter the Instance's risk profile in a way that could invalidate the underlying Capital and Operational Plan and, consequently, the premises driving the current Required Risk Capital (RRC) for that Instance. Operational GovOps retains the discretion to require an Artifact Edit Proposal if a proposed change, regardless of its fit within existing operational ranges, is determined to pose a material change to the assessed risk.

d531de16:d9ede57a42bc57779ce38760c6a90b7.title: Available Total Senior Risk Capital Pool Determination
d531de16:d9ede57a42bc57779ce38760c6a90b7.content: Total Senior Risk Capital (TSRC) is the amount of Senior Risk Capital that is available each Monthly Settlement Cycle for Primes to originate and thus turn into Originated Senior Risk Capital (OSRC) through the monthly origination process. TSRC is the sum of designated Internal Senior Risk Capital (ISRC) from Sky surplus buffers and available External Senior Risk Capital (ESRC) from the srUSDS contract. Prior to each monthly bidding window, the TSRC is calculated and publicly announced. Additional operational details will be defined in a future iteration of the Atlas.

d531de16:67220091402c22e606b940a3ccdcf0e.title: Process Timing and Schedule
d531de16:67220091402c22e606b940a3ccdcf0e.content: The SRC origination process operates monthly, synchronized with the Monthly Settlement Cycle. The bidding window occurs during the current month for SRC that is usable in the next month; the bidding window closes before settlement processing begins. Additional operational details, including timelines, will be specified in a future iteration of the Atlas.

d531de16:e6c33391cdc3132e1b68cd194288cd6.title: Bidding Process
d531de16:e6c33391cdc3132e1b68cd194288cd6.content: Participating Prime Agents submit bids via the Powerhouse interface during the defined bidding window. Each bid must specify: (1) The quantity of SRC the Prime seeks to originate, and (2) The maximum price the Prime is willing to pay (expressed in basis points above the Base Rate) for using the OSRC during the upcoming monthly period. Additional operational details will be specified in a future iteration of the Atlas.

d531de16:d5703e65aef96012e40af3f6e2c5d3d.title: Senior Risk Capital (SRC) Origination Process
d531de16:d5703e65aef96012e40af3f6e2c5d3d.content: This document defines the operational details of the recurring monthly process allowing Prime Agents to originate Senior Risk Capital (Originated Senior Risk Capital or OSRC) from the Total Senior Risk Capital (TSRC) pool. The process involves determining the available TSRC supply, a bidding phase, an allocation auction, and settlement aligned with the Monthly Settlement Cycle.

d531de16:006fda4c663396e006a4c60c3b502cc.title: Allocation & Clearing Price Determination
d531de16:006fda4c663396e006a4c60c3b502cc.content: Bids are ranked descending by price. TSRC is allocated sequentially to the highest bids until the pool is exhausted or all bids are filled. The price of the lowest successful bid that receives an allocation (even partial) sets the uniform clearing price for the month. All winning bidders pay this clearing price per unit of OSRC allocated, regardless of their original bid price. Additional operational details will be specified in a future iteration of the Atlas.

d531de16:ec31cec070e0b6d5acff55ecc327e40.title: srUSDS Accessibility Reward
d531de16:ec31cec070e0b6d5acff55ecc327e40.content: Prime Agents and third-party partners that drive srUSDS usage are entitled to a srUSDS Accessibility Reward similar to the Accessibility Reward paid on USDS balances. The srUSDS Accessibility Reward Fee is the same as the Accessibility Reward Fee on USDS. See A.2.4 - Accessibility Reward Primitive.

d531de16:ef1295bd6a5316e7849c2e2b55d4259.title: Settlement Of Origination
d531de16:ef1295bd6a5316e7849c2e2b55d4259.content: During the Monthly Settlement Cycle following allocation, the cost (Allocated OSRC Quantity \* Clearing Price) is deducted from each winning Prime Agent's operational account. Concurrently, the allocated OSRC amount is credited to the Prime Agent's Risk Capital account as OSRC for the upcoming monthly period.

d531de16:44114f4b6dcafa4457ecc9479c0aa96.title: Root Edit Token Holder Vote
d531de16:44114f4b6dcafa4457ecc9479c0aa96.content: Where their review of the proposal results in a finding of alignment with the Sky Core Atlas and Grove Artifact, the Operational Facilitator next triggers a Snapshot poll to allow token holders to vote on the proposal. The poll is open for three (3) days. A poll must have at least 10% of the circulating token supply participating and must have more than 50% of votes cast, excluding abstentions, in favor to be approved.

d531de16:f6daa4810d9c2faae012e1fda29a162.title: Root Edit Proposal Review By Operational Facilitator
d531de16:f6daa4810d9c2faae012e1fda29a162.content:
Within seven (7) days of the proposal being submitted, the Operational Facilitator must review the Root Edit Proposal for alignment.

If the proposal is aligned, the Operational Facilitator must respond to the Forum post to announce their finding. In this Forum post, the Operational Facilitator must also confirm that the proposal is feasible for Operational GovOps to operationalize.

If the proposal is misaligned, the Operational Facilitator must respond to the Forum post to announce their finding and provide the reasoning for it.

d531de16:761a355440ecd62e6afe22259412ca3.title: Root Edit Expert Advisor Review
d531de16:761a355440ecd62e6afe22259412ca3.content: A future iteration of the Launch Agent 3 Artifact will specify guidelines for obtaining specialized review of proposals requiring advanced technical or financial analysis.

d531de16:e28a458607610392a18220b03f64a99.title: Short-Term Transitionary Measures
d531de16:e28a458607610392a18220b03f64a99.content: Until the Powerhouse system supports submitting Artifact Edit Proposals, AGENT3 token holders may submit Artifact Edit Proposals by posting them to the Sky Forum under the "Launch Agent 3 Prime" category. The title of the post must include the text "Launch Agent 3 Artifact Edit Proposal". The post must include cryptographic proof that the author controls an account holding the required percentage of the total AGENT3 token supply specified in Root Edit Proposal Submission.

d531de16:fcf62265bf3bae36f514edd4f0f3881.title: Root Edit Proposal Review By Operational Facilitator
d531de16:fcf62265bf3bae36f514edd4f0f3881.content:
Within seven (7) days of the proposal being submitted, the Operational Facilitator must review the Root Edit Proposal for alignment. The Operational Facilitator also checks if the author of the proposal complies with the requirements in Root Edit Proposal Submission.

If the proposal is aligned, and the author is entitled to submit it, the Operational Facilitator must respond to the Forum post to announce their finding. In their Forum post, the Operational Facilitator must also confirm that the proposal is feasible for Operational GovOps to operationalize.

If the proposal is misaligned, or the author is not entitled to submit it, the Operational Facilitator must respond to the Forum post to announce their finding and provide the reasoning for it.

d531de16:66334ee5764187c6c1c261f9c73d847.content: All Spark Root Edit proposals must be reviewed by the Spark Risk Council. The mandate, scope, and review process of the SRC are specified in Spark Risk Council.

d531de16:710e5298484a01ad0531e2d6467b8af.title: Root Edit Voting Process in Urgent and Emergency Situations
d531de16:710e5298484a01ad0531e2d6467b8af.content: In an Urgent or Emergency Situation, as defined by the Sky Core Atlas in A.1.8 - Emergency Response System - Emergency Response - Definition Of Emergency Situations, the Operational Facilitator may allow a Root Edit to occur more quickly than the timeline specified above. Where feasible, the Operational Facilitator should announce the decision to deploy the emergency Root Edit protocol and provide their reasoning via a public Sky Forum post (under the "Spark Prime" category), unless doing so would endanger Spark or its users.

d531de16:3db5449be8b48edbee11d91bf150b30.title: Short-Term Transitionary Measures
d531de16:3db5449be8b48edbee11d91bf150b30.content: The parameters specified in Allocation System Primitive and SparkLend will be controlled by Sky Core Governance until Sky determines that the SPK token is decentralized enough to allow for meaningful governance by tokenholders. At such time, which is currently estimated for September 17, 2025, control will transition to Spark Governance. This transitionary measure ensures better decentralization of the SPK token before Spark Governance takes full control of the named parameters under the Root Edit Primitive.

d531de16:97bfe50ac7aada470ae1595c8b14ef9.title: Requirements
d531de16:97bfe50ac7aada470ae1595c8b14ef9.content:
When a collateral type threatens the security or solvency of the Sky Protocol, an expedited offboarding is in order. Expedited offboardings override the timeline specified in A.3.9 - Measures For Endgame Transition - Offboarding Process - Technical Process and allow the immediate modification of all relevant parameters.

Expedited offboardings must proceed pursuant to the following requirements:

-   The Offboarding Proposal must state that the offboarding should be expedited due to an emergency or urgent concern, as defined in A.1.8 - Emergency Response System - Emergency Response - Definition Of Emergency Situations.
-   The Offboarding Proposal must explicitly reference this Atlas document.

d531de16:d85163dcb390f9621e9ac35446799f8.title: Expedited Offboarding
d531de16:d85163dcb390f9621e9ac35446799f8.content: The subdocuments herein define an expedited offboarding process in the event a collateral type needs to be removed quickly due to security or solvency concerns.

d531de16:c02d300c432c78e764f92c5d7f59710.title: Announcements
d531de16:c02d300c432c78e764f92c5d7f59710.content: The public announcements defined in A.3.9 - Measures For Endgame Transition - Offboarding Process - Technical Process must still be carried out. However, the timing of these announcements no longer constrains the modification of parameters. These announcements must also state that the offboarding is being expedited and explain the reasons for this accelerated process.

d531de16:25c21e6f4baf1cd274801652d5a5e09.title: Communication Channels And Media Assets
d531de16:25c21e6f4baf1cd274801652d5a5e09.content:
