79abe87f:756f29675288711d3a6cd064850e762.content: Core GovOps reviews the calculation of Risk Capital by each Star Agent as part of the Settlement Cycle. In the event that it detects that Risk Capital requirements were violated, it applies the penalty mechanisms specified in A.3.3 - Penalty Mechanisms.

79abe87f:c53c4e081b8d27d7bdda3ad7f6d164e.title: Monitoring And Penalty Mechanisms
79abe87f:c53c4e081b8d27d7bdda3ad7f6d164e.content: The documents herein define monitoring and penalty mechanisms.

79abe87f:59903c6c305a33e5509ae68b16281e9.title: Penalty Mechanisms
79abe87f:59903c6c305a33e5509ae68b16281e9.content: The documents herein specify the penalty mechanisms that exist to incentivize Star Agents and Operational Agents to ensure that sufficient capital is always held against investments by Star Agents and to protect Sky from risks due to insufficient capital.

79abe87f:7befd1a2a741aa5a0d3cf137a8ee8fb.title: No Penalties For Changes In Methodology Or Governance Parameters In Near Term
79abe87f:7befd1a2a741aa5a0d3cf137a8ee8fb.content: In the near term as the Risk Capital implementation continues to be developed, Star Agents will not be subject to penalties for failing to supply the incremental capital required by changes to the Risk Capital implementation. However, Operational GovOps must reduce the exposure to Allocation Conduits managed by the Star Agent to bring it back into compliance with capital requirements if the Star Agent does not work in good faith to provide the additional capital on the timeline specified above.

79abe87f:08e9eb26bf9d3db2014e61115801c20.title: Penalty Mechanisms For Star Agents
79abe87f:08e9eb26bf9d3db2014e61115801c20.content: The documents herein specify the penalty mechanisms for Star Agents for breaches of the Risk Capital requirements.

79abe87f:52322ad6876d77620628df61aec1efd.title: Phased Update To Risk Capital For Changes In Methodology Or Governance Parameters
79abe87f:52322ad6876d77620628df61aec1efd.content: To the extent that a change to the implementation of the Risk Capital framework or a parameter set by Sky Governance changes the Required Risk Capital or Total Risk Capital, the change will phase in over time. The Star Agent must provide 50% of the additional Total Risk Capital necessary to comply with the change within seven (7) calendar days of the change, and the remaining 50% on a pro rata basis over the following twenty one (21) calendar days.

79abe87f:9bb5fc3128bdf31b20894b489e3b789.title: Financial Penalties For Breach Of Capital Requirements
79abe87f:9bb5fc3128bdf31b20894b489e3b789.content: The documents herein define the financial penalties for breaches of Risk Capital requirements.

baf25904:c511ca58ed687924a24c85cddf7e34b.title: Incorporation Of Additional Risk Factors
baf25904:c511ca58ed687924a24c85cddf7e34b.content: Additional risk factors, including legal risk and oracle risk, will be incorporated in future iterations of the risk framework.

baf25904:1faa768149de81df2eb508cd80cb09d.title: Application To Lending Markets
baf25904:1faa768149de81df2eb508cd80cb09d.content: The near term focus of the framework is on lending markets such as SparkLend. For lending markets, the relevant risk factors are financial risk, smart contract risk, and admin risk.

baf25904:5a9beaf13a25dc12369aefbeb5ef98d.title: Financial Risk
baf25904:5a9beaf13a25dc12369aefbeb5ef98d.content: The documents herein define the conceptual framework for determining the Risk Capital required to protect Sky from financial risk arising from investments by Star Agents of funds from Sky’s Collateral Portfolio. The financial risk framework is currently focused on credit risk. In future iterations of the risk framework, financial risk will be disaggregated into credit risk, liquidity risk, and market risk.

baf25904:9395f49323c5f83a80b529ce3f4099c.title: Calculating Aggregate Risk Capital
baf25904:9395f49323c5f83a80b529ce3f4099c.content: Once the Risk Capital requirements associated with each risk factor are calculated, they should be added to arrive at a total Risk Capital requirement.

baf25904:5814714458dbb530a7add82359245ce.title: Credit Risk
baf25904:5814714458dbb530a7add82359245ce.content: Credit risk is the risk that a loan or other debt instrument will not be repaid according to agreed terms.

baf25904:3184dff60cffad9ccd84228a5095150.title: Estimating Risk Factors
baf25904:3184dff60cffad9ccd84228a5095150.content: For each risk factor that is relevant to an investment, the required Risk Capital to protect Sky from potential losses on that investment should be estimated.

baf25904:b31e9a355784a101b54b74e7a9dbf56.title: Exposure And Rehypothecation
baf25904:b31e9a355784a101b54b74e7a9dbf56.content: In lending markets, an asset originally posted as collateral may be subsequently lent as collateral for additional loans, increasing overall exposure. Methodologies for estimating risk should take into account this overall exposure. To the extent that other investments have similar mechanisms that can increase overall risk, these should be incorporated into the calculation of required Risk Capital.

79abe87f:b3d87a17567a1f465faadafc66a2470.title: Incorporation Of Additional Types Of RRC
79abe87f:b3d87a17567a1f465faadafc66a2470.content: Additional types of RRC reflecting other risk factors, including legal risk and oracle risk, will be incorporated in future iterations of the risk framework.

79abe87f:288be5ec6722c8c103e2e3a13e47238.title: Application To Real World Assets
79abe87f:288be5ec6722c8c103e2e3a13e47238.content: Investments in Real World Assets, as defined in A.3.3 - Real World Assets, automatically have Instance Smart Contract RRC and Instance Admin RRC of zero. An additional type of Legal RRC, reflecting the unique risks of these assets, will be incorporated in future iterations of the risk framework.

79abe87f:7b9fd04a028425a4ab2ed5991c692ce.title: Instance Financial RRC
79abe87f:7b9fd04a028425a4ab2ed5991c692ce.content: The documents herein define the conceptual framework for determining the Instance Financial RRC required to protect Sky from financial risk arising from an Instance of the Allocation System Primitive.

79abe87f:c2ec9480f42263fbbdab44a09b8f83a.title: Instance Total RRC
79abe87f:c2ec9480f42263fbbdab44a09b8f83a.content: The Instance Total RRC for an Instance is equal to the sum of the Instance Financial RRC, Instance Smart Contract Risk RRC, and Instance Admin Risk RRC for that Instance. See A.3.3 - Instance Financial RRC, A.3.3 - Instance Smart Contract RRC, and A.3.3 - Instance Admin RRC.

79abe87f:b955d1a2585c8bdc5ef22bae96dfe8c.title: Introduction
79abe87f:b955d1a2585c8bdc5ef22bae96dfe8c.content: The conceptual framework for financial risk is designed to ensure that Star Agents hold sufficient capital to cover potential losses on their investments in case of an extreme market event. The financial risk framework is based on the Basel Accords developed by the Committee on Bank Supervision, including Basel II, Basel III, and Basel IV. These frameworks are then adapted to reflect the differences between traditional finance and decentralized finance.

79abe87f:7b6b9d11f963722ab228eb6634dceaa.title: Aggregate RRC
79abe87f:7b6b9d11f963722ab228eb6634dceaa.content: The Aggregate RRC that a Star Agent must maintain is equal to the sum of the Instance Total RRC for each Active Instance of the Allocation System Primitive that the Star Agent has deployed.

79abe87f:0ff2b8b0ca7cc0304e3cb54e481cdeb.title: Financial Risk Categories
79abe87f:0ff2b8b0ca7cc0304e3cb54e481cdeb.content: Financial risk can be divided into three categories, as specified in the documents herein. These categories of risk are interrelated, so Instance Financial RRC is not directly associated with these risk categories. Instead, risk models are developed for different asset classes, as specified in A.3.3 - Financial Risk Models. The development of each of these risk models is informed by considerations regarding how each of the financial risk categories impacts the specific asset.

baf25904:1c02677c20f2d66bd167e7db33cbc52.title: External Senior Risk Capital
baf25904:1c02677c20f2d66bd167e7db33cbc52.content: External Senior Risk Capital (ESRC) is capital provided from the srUSDS smart contract, which allow users to provide USDS to Sky Core to serve as senior risk capital in exchange for higher returns. The mechanics of this are specified in A.3.3 - Risk Capital - Implementation - Senior Risk Capital System Implementation - External Senior Risk Capital And srUSDS System.

baf25904:6a9e57c0f7620188b9345b8cb5fa6d0.title: Internal Senior Risk Capital
baf25904:6a9e57c0f7620188b9345b8cb5fa6d0.content: Internal Senior Risk Capital (ISRC) is capital provided from Sky Core’s Surplus Buffer. The composition of Internal Senior Risk Capital will be specified in more detail in a future iteration of the Atlas.

baf25904:e155fd330ab5e20ac62b0dd11b3bb31.title: Risk Capital Sourcing Ratios
baf25904:e155fd330ab5e20ac62b0dd11b3bb31.content: The documents herein define the required relationship and constraints between the different types of Risk Capital. These ensure that the Star Agent maintains the appropriate level of Internal First Loss Capital relative to its External and Senior capital exposures, ensuring sufficient “skin in the game” with respect to its investments.

baf25904:147f617885d692c1563cb9d6fb52557.title: Senior Risk Capital Types
baf25904:147f617885d692c1563cb9d6fb52557.content: The documents herein define the types of Senior Risk Capital.

baf25904:d315c00d729cb49fdd15f3ba7668957.title: Definition Of Ratios
baf25904:d315c00d729cb49fdd15f3ba7668957.content: The documents herein define the Risk Capital sourcing ratios.

baf25904:b46666ea84a724a1fe36b4f0d5e7646.title: Senior Risk Capital
baf25904:b46666ea84a724a1fe36b4f0d5e7646.content:
Senior Risk Capital (SRC) is protected from losses relative to First Loss Capital. Senior Risk Capital only begins to absorb losses after First Loss Capital has experienced 100% losses and absorbs 100% of losses thereafter.
Senior Risk Capital can be originated from Sky Core on a monthly basis as part of the Monthly Settlement Cycle; Star Agents can also rent Senior Risk Capital from each other.

baf25904:6d4063b691000d640158e1b0e7a23c0.title: External Per Internal Ratio
baf25904:6d4063b691000d640158e1b0e7a23c0.content: The External Per Internal (EPI) ratio determines the maximum amount of External First Loss Capital (SEFLC and TEFLC combined) that a Star Agent can source directly based on its held Internal First Loss Capital (IFLC). This acts as the primary constraint ensuring a baseline level of the Star’s own capital backs its external FLC sourcing. The required External Per Internal ratio is specified in A.3.3 - Risk Capital - Implementation - Core Risk Capital Parameters - Risk Capital Composition Structural Ratios - External Per Internal (EPI) Ratio Value.

79abe87f:b11ff49f78ec4c3a2ac16c1bb88dac2.title: External Senior Risk Capital
79abe87f:b11ff49f78ec4c3a2ac16c1bb88dac2.content: External Senior Risk Capital (ESRC) is capital provided from the srUSDS smart contract, which allow users to provide USDS to Sky Core to serve as senior risk capital in exchange for higher returns. The mechanics of this are specified in A.3.3 - External Senior Risk Capital And srUSDS System.

79abe87f:ac5603fc0d141aaffc803f9c3c8caab.title: Internal Senior Risk Capital
79abe87f:ac5603fc0d141aaffc803f9c3c8caab.content: Internal Senior Risk Capital (ISRC) is capital provided from Sky Core's Surplus Buffer. The composition of Internal Senior Risk Capital will be specified in more detail in a future iteration of the Atlas.

79abe87f:da670697eef72ea3459b7db3887d0c4.title: Total Risk Capital Sourcing Ratios
79abe87f:da670697eef72ea3459b7db3887d0c4.content: The documents herein define the required relationship and constraints between the different types of Total Risk Capital. These ensure that the Star Agent maintains the appropriate level of Internal Junior Risk Capital relative to its External and Senior capital exposures, ensuring sufficient "skin in the game" with respect to its investments.

79abe87f:147f617885d692c1563cb9d6fb52557.title: Senior Risk Capital Types
79abe87f:147f617885d692c1563cb9d6fb52557.content: The documents herein define the types of Senior Risk Capital.

79abe87f:075c4f6f0dc4aaac9394308209d93c8.title: Definition Of Ratios
79abe87f:075c4f6f0dc4aaac9394308209d93c8.content: The documents herein define the Total Risk Capital sourcing ratios.

79abe87f:fec1a14ab2d68baeda53e88788735ed.title: Senior Risk Capital
79abe87f:fec1a14ab2d68baeda53e88788735ed.content:
Senior Risk Capital (SRC) is protected from losses relative to Junior Risk Capital. Senior Risk Capital only begins to absorb losses after Junior Risk Capital has experienced 100% losses and absorbs 100% of losses thereafter.

Senior Risk Capital can be originated from Sky Core on a monthly basis as part of the Monthly Settlement Cycle; Star Agents can also rent Senior Risk Capital from each other.

79abe87f:8d5d3e07e84ac30d94005cc7198456e.title: External Per Internal Ratio
79abe87f:8d5d3e07e84ac30d94005cc7198456e.content: The External Per Internal (EPI) ratio determines the maximum amount of External Junior Risk Capital (SEJRC and TEJRC combined) that a Star Agent can source directly based on its held Internal Junior Risk Capital (IJRC). This acts as the primary constraint ensuring a baseline level of the Star's own capital backs its external JRC sourcing. The required External Per Internal ratio is specified in A.3.3 - External Per Internal (EPI) Ratio Value.

baf25904:7a2d278da344d30d155ae9fe047c49a.title: Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module
baf25904:7a2d278da344d30d155ae9fe047c49a.content: The Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module (SP-BEAM) enables designated, Governance-whitelisted operators to adjust the Stability Fees of supported vault types, the Dai Savings Rate (DSR), and the Sky Savings Rate (SSR). Adjustments are governed by the SP-BEAM smart contract logic and specific parameters set by Sky Governance. SP-BEAM holds four parameters that can be set for each vault type or savings rate: (i) min, (ii) max, (iii) step, and (iv) tau.

baf25904:9ebdc72911ba1c20024b5c0bea21357.title: Min Definition
baf25904:9ebdc72911ba1c20024b5c0bea21357.content: The min parameter defines the minimum value for rates in basis points that can be set using the Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module. Each rate parameter added to the SP-BEAM has a specific min.
ancestors: Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module

baf25904:1d4506cc01daa6f39abb509c8dc1b96.title: Updates
baf25904:1d4506cc01daa6f39abb509c8dc1b96.content: If not otherwise specified, the Stability Facilitators have the ability to modify any of the parameters defined in A.3.9 - Measures For Endgame Transition - Native Vault Engine - Risk Parameter Definitions for any of the Vault Types in A.3.9 - Measures For Endgame Transition - Native Vault Engine - Vault Types. As a general rule, the modification of said parameters is pursuant to the Operational Weekly Cycle and can be effected directly via an Executive Vote, without requiring a Governance Poll. Exceptions to this general rule must be clearly stated in the relevant Atlas document.

baf25904:14fbf20ee63c77bca09b181476106ce.title: Max Definition
baf25904:14fbf20ee63c77bca09b181476106ce.content: The max parameter defines the maximum value for rates in basis points that can be set using the Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module. Each rate parameter added to the SP-BEAM has a specific max.
ancestors: Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module

baf25904:2b83c565af078d109bb9b7c2dfa8dea.title: Oracles
baf25904:2b83c565af078d109bb9b7c2dfa8dea.content: The Native Vault Engine collateral types of ETH, STETH, WBTC will specifically use the Chronicle v3 oracle solution, until at least January 1st 2026. The Native Vault Engine collateral types must be migrated to the new version of the Chronicle v3 oracle when it is feasible to do so.Other oracle solutions, including diversified oracles, will only be considered until January 1st, 2026, and only if there are unresolvable security concerns with the Chronicle v3 oracles.

baf25904:d01b4f8c4c3db80387395e525571d79.title: Max Technical Upper Limit
baf25904:d01b4f8c4c3db80387395e525571d79.content: Although the max parameter can be set higher, the SP-BEAM cannot be used to set a rate higher than 50% (5,000 basis points) due to technical limitations. Attempts to use the SP-BEAM in this manner will revert. To avoid confusion, max should not be set to a value higher than 50% (5,000 basis points).
ancestors: Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module

baf25904:726f27c270e342e8e390ccfcb51f613.title: Interaction Between Ratios And SPFL Capacity
baf25904:726f27c270e342e8e390ccfcb51f613.content:
The sourcing of External First Loss Capital and enablement of Senior Risk Capital involves a sequential application of the Risk Capital sourcing ratios in conjunction with the Star Agent’s deployment of its SPFL capacity.
First, the EPI ratio sets the initial limit for sourcing standard, SPFL-bearing EFLC based solely on the Star Agent’s IFLC.
Second, the total SPFL capacity is calculated from the Star Agent’s resulting FLC pool (IFLC + any EPI-sourced EFLC).
Finally, this total calculated SPFL capacity can be allocated by the Star Agent to enable SRC (standard use), and/or to source additional, non-SPFL-bearing EFLC using the mechanism described under A.3.3 - Risk Capital - Conceptual Framework - Eligible Assets - Risk Capital Sourcing Ratios - Definition Of Ratios - Senior Per First Loss Ratio - Alternative Use Of SPFL Capacity To Source External First Loss Capital. Any specific portion of the total SPFL capacity allocated towards sourcing EFLC cannot simultaneously be allocated towards enabling SRC.

baf25904:6b085e34f7c668a5946c3ecccb03450.title: Asset Class Specific Implementation
baf25904:6b085e34f7c668a5946c3ecccb03450.content: The documents herein define implementations of the financial risk framework for specific asset classes. In the near term, the only implementation that is defined is for lending markets. In the future additional implementations will be added herein.

baf25904:7bcc62f7ebba720e3c168a3f340fc4e.title: Alternative Use Of SPFL Capacity To Source External First Loss Capital
baf25904:7bcc62f7ebba720e3c168a3f340fc4e.content:
A Star Agent may optionally choose to deploy all or some portion of its calculated SPFL capacity not to enable Senior Risk Capital, but instead to source additional External First Loss Capital. This provides a secondary mechanism to increase the total FLC potentially beyond the amount initially constrained by the EPI ratio applied solely to IFLC.
Crucially, the EFLC tranche acquired through utilizing SPFL capacity is permanently accounted for as having an SPFL ratio of zero (0). It contributes to the FLC buffer but provides no capacity itself for enabling SRC in any subsequent calculations. This contrasts with EFLC sourced normally via the EPI ratio, which retains its standard SPFL capacity.

baf25904:b1f17ae48b88b0faa4d9b5a4989b475.title: Risk Capital Required
baf25904:b1f17ae48b88b0faa4d9b5a4989b475.content:
Finally, the Risk Capital (FLC(u)) required for each market u is the Risk Weighted Assets (RWA(u)) multiplied by three times 2.75%, reflecting that 100% weight is being placed on Credit Risk and 0% weight on Market Risk and Liquidity Risk.

```python

          FLC(u) = RWA(u) * (0.0275 * 3)

```

The total Risk Capital required across all markets is simply the sum of the Risk Capital required for each market.

baf25904:9cdeec78a913f0d436f814d9a3a35b2.title: External Per Internal (EPI) Ratio Value
baf25904:9cdeec78a913f0d436f814d9a3a35b2.content:
The External Per Internal (EPI) ratio is **1.00**. For example, if a Star Agent has $20 million of Internal First Loss Capital, the EPI ratio enables it to source $20 million of External First Loss Capital.
This EPI ratio governs the initial mechanism for sourcing EFLC (SEFLC + TEFLC) and is based purely on the Star’s IFLC; Stars can source EFLC via this initial mechanism up to a maximum amount equal to their IFLC holdings. However, additional EFLC may potentially be acquired via the alternative use of SPFL capacity, as described in A.3.3 - Risk Capital - Conceptual Framework - Eligible Assets - Risk Capital Sourcing Ratios - Definition Of Ratios - Senior Per First Loss Ratio - Alternative Use Of SPFL Capacity To Source External First Loss Capital.

baf25904:f4b1f026f0a0580ed8b0b1618f2d227.title: Calculation Of Risk Weighted Assets
baf25904:f4b1f026f0a0580ed8b0b1618f2d227.content:
The Risk Weighted Assets (RWA(u)) for each market (u) is calculated as the product of the Total Debt Backed (total\_debt\_backed(u)) and the Weighted Credit Risk (weighted\_credit\_risk(u)).

```

          RWA(u) = total_debt_backed(u) * weighted_credit_risk(u)

```

baf25904:b86ec0c7b3de8b8b8895b31bb5c65ef.title: Per-Event Basis
baf25904:b86ec0c7b3de8b8b8895b31bb5c65ef.content:
The FLC loss allocation rules are applied independently based on the total losses attributed to each distinct risk event. The concept of “per-event basis” is crucial; the classification of a distinct risk event (classifying losses as one large event versus multiple smaller ones) can dictate whether the Tip FLC threshold is breached.
Breaching the threshold activates the pro-rata sharing mechanism for any losses exceeding the Tip FLC amount, distributing such excess losses between both the remaining Internal FLC (IFLC) and all External FLC (EFLC). Conversely, if the threshold is not breached for an event, the loss is contained entirely within the Tip layer and absorbed solely by IFLC.
The operational process for the determination of distinct risk events will be defined in a future iteration of the Atlas.

baf25904:c9fb5b16e2a9f001fe61f7108a7cb7c.title: Post-Tip FLC Loss Allocation
baf25904:c9fb5b16e2a9f001fe61f7108a7cb7c.content: If a loss event exceeds the Tip FLC amount, the remaining loss is allocated pro-rata across the rest of the FLC capital. This includes the remaining Internal First Loss Capital (Total IFLC minus the Tip amount) and all External First Loss Capital (Star External First Loss Capital plus Tokenized External First Loss Capital).

baf25904:bddc0c9d3d830774a4357d945e4be9e.title: Initial Loss Absorption by "Tip FLC"
baf25904:bddc0c9d3d830774a4357d945e4be9e.content:
The Tip FLC mechanism dictates that losses from a distinct risk event are first absorbed entirely by the Star Agent’s Internal First Loss Capital (IFLC), up to a specific threshold amount. This threshold amount is calculated as a percentage of Total FLC and is specified in A.3.3 - Risk Capital - Implementation - Core Risk Capital Parameters - FLC Loss Allocation Parameters.
Only losses exceeding this threshold amount trigger absorption by other First Loss Capital components - specifically, the remaining IFLC and External First Loss Capital. This initial absorption solely by IFLC ensures that Star Agents are highly incentivized to prevent losses and avoids the need to resolve disputes regarding the allocation of small losses to EFLC providers.

79abe87f:473749c809e7dd182bac0916ff43941.title: Per-Event Basis
79abe87f:473749c809e7dd182bac0916ff43941.content:
The JRC loss allocation rules are applied independently based on the total losses attributed to each distinct risk event. The concept of "per-event basis" is crucial; the classification of a distinct risk event (classifying losses as one large event versus multiple smaller ones) can dictate whether the Tip JRC threshold is breached.

Breaching the threshold activates the pro-rata sharing mechanism for any losses exceeding the Tip JRC amount, distributing such excess losses between both the remaining Internal JRC (IJRC) and all External JRC (EJRC). Conversely, if the threshold is not breached for an event, the loss is contained entirely within the Tip layer and absorbed solely by IJRC.

The operational process for the determination of distinct risk events will be defined in a future iteration of the Atlas.

79abe87f:61268b50df48f13057c869aa8bc11ae.title: Post-Tip JRC Loss Allocation
79abe87f:61268b50df48f13057c869aa8bc11ae.content: If a loss event exceeds the Tip JRC amount, the remaining loss is allocated pro-rata across the rest of the JRC capital. This includes the remaining Internal Junior Risk Capital (Total IJRC minus the Tip amount) and all External Junior Risk Capital (Star External Junior Risk Capital plus Tokenized External Junior Risk Capital).

79abe87f:4e48be8a038bb5eb43c1e3ace4d046a.title: Initial Loss Absorption By "Tip JRC"
79abe87f:4e48be8a038bb5eb43c1e3ace4d046a.content:
The Tip JRC mechanism dictates that losses from a distinct risk event are first absorbed entirely by the Star Agent's Internal Junior Risk Capital (IJRC), up to a specific threshold amount. This threshold amount is calculated as a percentage of Total JRC and is specified in A.3.3 - JRC Loss Allocation Parameters.

Only losses exceeding this threshold amount trigger absorption by other Junior Risk Capital components - specifically, the remaining IJRC and External Junior Risk Capital. This initial absorption solely by IJRC ensures that Star Agents are highly incentivized to prevent losses and avoids the need to resolve disputes regarding the allocation of small losses to EJRC providers.

baf25904:5e6daba29eb6a4d5715e829b2af928c.title: FLC Loss Allocation Rules
baf25904:5e6daba29eb6a4d5715e829b2af928c.content: This document defines the conceptual framework for distributing losses within the FLC layer.

baf25904:0144b09a6008f184c56a0456b07b65d.title: Users Can Withdraw Unencumbered Funds From Smart Contract
baf25904:0144b09a6008f184c56a0456b07b65d.content: Users can withdraw funds from the smart contract so long as there are unencumbered funds available. Withdrawals increase the percentage of funds that are encumbered, increasing the interest rate and naturally incentivizing other users to deposit funds.

baf25904:21143ed1dbd545a654b4e4116e8f9c7.title: Interest Rate On Smart Contract Determined By Percentage Of Encumbered Funds
baf25904:21143ed1dbd545a654b4e4116e8f9c7.content: The interest rate paid to users depositing funds into the smart contract is a function of the percentage of funds in the smart contract that are encumbered. This is similar to how the interest rate in decentralized lending markets is a function of the utilization rate. In this way, a Star Agent encumbering a high percentage of the available funds will pay a higher interest rate, naturally incentivizing additional funds to be deposited.

baf25904:f0d34f41437df69a7469109ec189dda.title: Star Agent Can Encumber Funds From Smart Contract To Count Towards Capital Requirements
baf25904:f0d34f41437df69a7469109ec189dda.content: Star Agents, through their Operational Executor Agents, have the ability to encumber a portion of the funds in the smart contract, essentially “borrowing” the funds to serve as First Loss Capital. The encumbered portion of funds in the smart contract qualifies as Tokenized External First Loss Capital towards the Star Agent’s required Risk Capital.

79abe87f:594015e681b4ea7903dec1e3c7b13a3.title: JRC Loss Allocation Rules
79abe87f:594015e681b4ea7903dec1e3c7b13a3.content: This document defines the conceptual framework for distributing losses within the JRC layer.

79abe87f:70f3fea01de637349d3c02aa7be7799.title: Tokenized External Junior Risk Capital (TEJRC)
79abe87f:70f3fea01de637349d3c02aa7be7799.content: Tokenized External Junior Risk Capital is capital provided by external capital providers depositing sUSDS into the Tokenized External Junior Risk Capital smart contract, from which Stars can encumber funds. The details of this contract will be specified in a future iteration of the Atlas.

79abe87f:c8937b2ae64d7b684a8aa4ced0027c3.title: Star-External Junior Risk Capital (SEJRC)
79abe87f:c8937b2ae64d7b684a8aa4ced0027c3.content: SEJRC is JRC rented from another Star Agent via the A.2.4 - Junior Risk Capital Rental Primitive. The capital remains in the lender's treasury but counts towards the borrower's JRC amount. SEJRC is represented by a registered Ecosystem Accord signifying that a specified amount of the lending Agent's JRC (held within the lender's treasury) is designated to count towards the borrowing Agent's JRC requirement for the duration and terms specified in the Accord.

79abe87f:34a285036916a2e9308b870d5161179.title: Types Of Eligible Assets For IJRC
79abe87f:34a285036916a2e9308b870d5161179.content:

79abe87f:820879575440410bf1218fa61ee0fa1.title: Process For Calculating Instance Financial RRC
79abe87f:820879575440410bf1218fa61ee0fa1.content: The documents herein define the process for calculating Instance Financial RRC for lending markets.

79abe87f:1c7444717307fcd74ed3406870eea5f.title: Calculate Probability Of Default
79abe87f:1c7444717307fcd74ed3406870eea5f.content:
The first step is calculating the Probability Of Default $PD$. $PD$ is calculated using the following formula:

$$\\text{PD} = N(-d\_1) + N(-d\_2) \\left( \\frac{\\sum\_{i=1}^n \\text{LT}i V\_0^i}{\\sum{j=1}^m D\_0^j} \\right)^{-2a}$$

Here $N$ is the normal cumulative probability distribution function.

The parameters of this formula are specified in the subdocuments herein.

baf25904:e600db618ab52c193b352fe1ff66cae.title: Tokenized External First Loss Capital (TEFLC)
baf25904:e600db618ab52c193b352fe1ff66cae.content: Tokenized External First Loss Capital is capital provided by external capital providers depositing sUSDS into the Tokenized External First Loss Capital smart contract, from which Stars can encumber funds. The details of this contract will be specified in a future iteration of the Atlas.

baf25904:fdf60e08481d6a0a1e14b1828a81734.title: Star-External First Loss Capital (SEFLC)
baf25904:fdf60e08481d6a0a1e14b1828a81734.content: SEFLC is FLC rented from another Star Agent via the A.2.4 - First Loss Capital Rental Primitive. The capital remains in the lender’s treasury but counts towards the borrower’s FLC amount. SEFLC is represented by a registered Ecosystem Accord signifying that a specified amount of the lending Agent’s FLC (held within the lender’s treasury) is designated to count towards the borrowing Agent’s FLC requirement for the duration and terms specified in the Accord.

baf25904:db43386b673179f5b415d3a6fa4192c.title: Definition of TEFLC System
baf25904:db43386b673179f5b415d3a6fa4192c.content: The documents herein describe at a high-level the working of the TEFLC system.

baf25904:764b8c4ba32319d55bd2f4de39a4089.title: Types Of Eligible Assets For IFLC
baf25904:764b8c4ba32319d55bd2f4de39a4089.content: The documents herein define the types of assets that qualify as Internal First Loss Capital. These types will be specified in a future iteration of the Risk Framework.

baf25904:181ad4014259318ba495ef01660fc66.title: Deployment Of Smart Contract
baf25904:181ad4014259318ba495ef01660fc66.content: To access Tokenized External First Loss Capital, the Star Agent first deploys a Tokenized External First Loss Capital smart contract. This will be available as a Sky Primitive in a future iteration of the Atlas.

baf25904:0a57ebe7424aeb7be5bf459f8ddb699.title: Internal First Loss Capital (IFLC)
baf25904:0a57ebe7424aeb7be5bf459f8ddb699.content: Internal First Loss Capital is capital owned by the Star Agent itself. It serves as the foundation for the Star’s risk capacity: the amount of IFLC directly dictates the maximum External FLC the Star can source (governed by the External Per Internal ratio) and provides the primary capacity for enabling Senior Risk Capital (via the Senior Per First Loss ratio), while also bearing the initial impact of any losses (the Tip FLC mechanism). IFLC must be eligible assets held in the Star Agent’s designated treasury account (e.g., SubProxy), controlled via its Operational Executor Agent. See A.3.3 - Risk Capital - Conceptual Framework - Eligible Assets - Risk Capital Sourcing Ratios - Definition Of Ratios - External Per Internal Ratio, A.3.3 - Risk Capital - Conceptual Framework - Eligible Assets - Risk Capital Sourcing Ratios - Definition Of Ratios - Senior Per First Loss Ratio, and A.3.3 - Risk Capital - Conceptual Framework - Eligible Assets - Types Of Risk Capital - First Loss Capital - FLC Loss Allocation Rules.

baf25904:5a9f9793ef09d21fefdf7156eabb69c.title: Users Deposit sUSDS Into Smart Contract
baf25904:5a9f9793ef09d21fefdf7156eabb69c.content: The smart contract allows users to deposit sUSDS, taking on the risk of losses on the Star Agent’s investments in return for the potential of higher yield than the Sky Savings Rate.

baf25904:08e2acf592492c255690301a533523f.title: Sky Core-Designated Address
baf25904:08e2acf592492c255690301a533523f.content: The address to which tokens must be transferred will be specified in a future iteration of the Atlas.

baf25904:b9a87152f7bdca4801638e36dcb8cc3.title: Distribution Requirement Primitive
baf25904:b9a87152f7bdca4801638e36dcb8cc3.content: The Distribution Requirement Primitive requires Agents to periodically buy and distribute 0.25% of their token supply per year. The annual requirement of 0.25% of the token supply is divided into twelve (12) equal monthly distributions. Distributions must occur on the first day of each month, with tokens purchased by the Star Agent on the open market and transferred to an address designated by Sky Core in A.2.4 - Sky Core-Designated Address. Star Agents choose between fulfilling either the Distribution Requirement Primitive or the Market Cap Fee Primitive.

baf25904:7bc7fcdecbd2b1baea630e66128565b.title: Calculation of Distributed Tokens
baf25904:7bc7fcdecbd2b1baea630e66128565b.content: The value of the distributed tokens is calculated as the number of tokens distributed, multiplied by the Time-Weighted Average Price (TWAP) of the token over the 24-hour period ending at 23:59 UTC on the last day of each month, immediately preceding the distribution event. This value is applied in the rebate calculation under the Upkeep Rebate Primitive. See A.2.4 - Upkeep Rebate Primitive.

baf25904:ed66bf9ce5280f6aa2f5eae9d1a064a.title: Ecosystem Upkeep Primitives
baf25904:ed66bf9ce5280f6aa2f5eae9d1a064a.content: Ecosystem Upkeep Primitives ensure that all Agents contribute to long-term ecosystem sustainability. Star Agents must choose between either the Distribution Requirement Primitive or the Market Cap Fee Primitive; whereas the Upkeep Rebate Primitive applies universally to all Star Agents. The term "Ecosystem Upkeep Fees" refers to the upkeep obligation of a Star Agent pursuant to either the Distribution Requirement Primitive or the Market Cap Fee Primitive.

baf25904:c3f0b5696140e19647241f2c1987ee0.title: Market Cap Fee Primitive
baf25904:c3f0b5696140e19647241f2c1987ee0.content: The Market Cap Fee Primitive requires Star Agents to pay an annual fee equivalent to 0.30% of their market capitalization to Sky, accounted for monthly. The annual fee of 0.30% of the market capitalization is divided into twelve (12) equal monthly payments, equating to 0.025% of the market capitalization per month. Payments must occur on the first day of each month, with the fee transferred to an address designated by Sky Core in A.2.4 - Sky Core-Designated Address. Star Agents choose between fulfilling either the Distribution Requirement Primitive or the Market Cap Fee Primitive.

baf25904:6cd403525dc9b175ba29c8279d1962d.title: Light Agent Primitive
baf25904:6cd403525dc9b175ba29c8279d1962d.content: The Light Agent Primitive enables users to create Light Agents, which are sub-agents operating on top of the Agent's Executor Accord, conferring the advantages of Sky GovOps at a lower cost, but without direct access to other Sky Primitives.

baf25904:436b56c9d42de16881ee31a4772e757.title: Valuation
baf25904:436b56c9d42de16881ee31a4772e757.content: The market capitalization is determined as the total token supply multiplied by the TWAP of the token over the 24-hour period ending at 23:59 UTC on the last day of each month, immediately preceding the payment event. This value is applied in the rebate calculation under the Upkeep Rebate Primitive. See A.2.4 - Upkeep Rebate Primitive.

baf25904:2942cb97c50aaabfa48a90f11082618.title: Upkeep Rebate Primitive
baf25904:2942cb97c50aaabfa48a90f11082618.content: The Upkeep Rebate Primitive allows a Star Agent (”Holding Agent”) to claim a rebate on its Ecosystem Upkeep Fees when it holds any portion of the token supply of another Star Agent (”Issuing Agent”). Ecosystem Upkeep Fees are accounted on a monthly basis. The Upkeep Rebate is calculated on the same cadence per Holding Agent as follows: (1) The Holding Agent’s share of the Issuing Agent’s token supply at the time the Issuing Agent pays its Ecosystem Upkeep Fees, multiplied by (2) The total monthly Ecosystem Upkeep Fees paid by the Issuing Agent. For a Star Agent deploying the Distribution Requirement Primitive, the value of its total monthly Ecosystem Upkeep Fee is calculated pursuant to A.2.4 - Calculation of Distributed Tokens. For a Star Agent deploying the Market Cap Fee Primitive, the value of its total monthly Ecosystem Upkeep Fee is calculated pursuant to A.2.4 - Valuation. This resulting rebate amount is applied against the Holding Agent’s Ecosystem Upkeep Fees due in the calendar month immediately following the Issuing Agent’s payment.

baf25904:aefc48a4d039495bfc7fbccbb84f57d.title: SkyLink Primitives
baf25904:aefc48a4d039495bfc7fbccbb84f57d.content: SkyLink Primitives are Sky Primitives that are technical infrastructure that extends the Sky Protocol. SkyLink Primitives are built autonomously by Star Agents, but owned by Sky Core and shared among all Star Agents. Star Agents are reimbursed for the cost of setting up SkyLink Primitives and given additional first-mover incentives.

baf25904:e50bb2108bda53f8e82d806c3cf89c2.title: yUSDS Risk Parameters
baf25904:e50bb2108bda53f8e82d806c3cf89c2.content: This document defines the liquidation parameters for SKY-backed loans funded via yUSDS. These parameters will be specified in a future iteration of the Atlas.

baf25904:f69ad13f322092589b01a2851a46570.title: yUSDS Accessibility Reward Definition
baf25904:f69ad13f322092589b01a2851a46570.content: yUSDS Accessibility Reward is defined in A.4.4 - SKY Staking Mechanism - SKY Staking - SKY-Backed Borrowing - yUSDS Accessibility Reward.

baf25904:96d4e7d7a8ee7523f88d3463dec6623.title: yUSDS Accessibility Reward
baf25904:96d4e7d7a8ee7523f88d3463dec6623.content: The yUSDS Accessibility Reward is an incentive mechanism, similar to the USDS Accessibility Reward, designed to encourage Star Agents and Integrators to promote yUSDS adoption. See A.2.4 - Accessibility Reward Primitive. It is calculated as a percentage of the yUSDS balance associated with a Reward Code. The reward is initially set at 0.05% for the Integrator portion and 0.05% for the Star Agent Management Fee, totaling 0.1%.

baf25904:928eac95e041c9c7bb2d16497232d57.content: Sky Savings Rate is defined in A.3.2 - Core Stability Parameters - Parameters - Sky Savings Rate.

baf25904:5b7bfa344c372a0cc0a09c2544a1970.content: The documents herein define short-term logic for SKY staking rewards and SKY-backed borrowing pending the implementation of the Sky Treasury Management Function and the yUSDS system. Short-term logic regarding MKR staking rewards and MKR-backed borrowing is also included herein.

baf25904:1d62327c1e63b18efdbf78fbe7d1957.title: Parameters Definition
baf25904:1d62327c1e63b18efdbf78fbe7d1957.content: The parameters of the SKY Borrow Minimum Rate formula are further defined in the documents herein.

baf25904:e7d76925f05aa7e2b4b234aa9290f95.title: Short Term Staking SKY Rewards

Until the Treasury Management Function (TMF) is live, USDS rewards for SKY stakers will be temporarily funded by the Smart Burn Engine; this interim mechanism will be discontinued once the TMF becomes operational.

baf25904:5e8f9ccab34822a8b33d98a73b6a696.title: Scaffold Artifact Setup
baf25904:5e8f9ccab34822a8b33d98a73b6a696.content: Core GovOps prepares a Scaffold Agent Artifact ("Scaffold Artifact") containing all Sky Primitives. In the Scaffold Artifact, the Upkeep Rebate Primitive is globally activated by default. See A.2.4 - Initial Primitive Global Activation Status. All other Primitives are initially set to Inactive. The Scaffold Artifact also includes an initial set of Omni Documents that provide general information about the Agent and organize the various Sky Primitive Instance Configuration Documents. Core GovOps must add the Scaffold Artifact to the Atlas' Agent Artifact Scope.
baf25904:5e8f9ccab34822a8b33d98a73b6a696.parentTitle: Prerequisites For Activating Agent Creation Primitive

79abe87f:dbc76f72aae8795022f48f1136d7d24.title: Internal Junior Risk Capital (IJRC)
79abe87f:dbc76f72aae8795022f48f1136d7d24.content:
Internal Junior Risk Capital is capital owned by the Star Agent itself. It serves as the foundation for the Star's risk capacity: the amount of IJRC directly dictates the maximum External JRC the Star can source (governed by the External Per Internal ratio) and provides the primary capacity for enabling Senior Risk Capital (via the Senior Per Junior ratio), while also bearing the initial impact of any losses (the Tip JRC mechanism). IJRC must be eligible assets held in the Star Agent's designated treasury account (e.g., SubProxy), controlled by the Star's root governance.

See A.3.3 - External Per Internal Ratio, A.3.3 - Senior Per Junior Ratio, and A.3.3 - JRC Loss Allocation Rules.

79abe87f:304351f7fdace4e07bc34c3d0a18f27.title: Alternative Enforcement Mechanisms
79abe87f:304351f7fdace4e07bc34c3d0a18f27.content:
In the event that the Star Agent's Total Risk Capital is less than its Required Risk Capital at the time of the Monthly Settlement Cycle, or the collection of the penalty would cause the Star Agent's Total Risk Capital to fall below its Required Risk Capital, then Sky may exercise the alternative enforcement mechanism described below.

In this instance Sky, at its discretion, may issue additional tokens of the Star Agent and sell them on the open market until it has collected proceeds equal to the calculated penalty. Any proceeds above the calculated penalty shall be refunded to the Star Agent SubProxy account.

Alternatively, Sky may convert the penalty into a debt owed by the Star Agent to Sky Core at terms mutually agreed between Sky Core and the Star Agent.

baf25904:0c544caf5e2a09d33e08caa2f2c19d0.title: Allocation Conduit Setup Conduit Development And Testing
baf25904:0c544caf5e2a09d33e08caa2f2c19d0.content: Once formally validated, the Star Agent implements the new Allocation Conduit based on the specifications in the Star Agent Artifact. Operational GovOps must test the Allocation Conduit with minimal funds from the Star Agent's Central Allocation Buffer, verifying deposit / withdrawal logic, slippage constraints, and oracle checks. If this testing is successful Operational GovOps confirms that the Allocation Conduit satisfies all risk constraints specified in the Star Agent Artifact. The output of this step is validated contracts for the Allocation Conduit and a green light to proceed with a scaled deployment.

baf25904:87351d8ec55ad7d98a14c80ef236386.title: Allocation Conduit Setup Deployment
baf25904:87351d8ec55ad7d98a14c80ef236386.content: The documents herein define how the deployment of an Allocation Conduit is executed on-chain.

baf25904:e85409e4dc21a8eb89c3da2b1103022.title: Allocation Conduit Setup Initial Deployment and First Loss Capital / Asset Liability Management Execution
baf25904:e85409e4dc21a8eb89c3da2b1103022.content: The Star Agent finalizes First Loss Capital and Asset Liability Management Arrangements. Operational GovOps records these arrangements in the Powerhouse interface. Operational GovOps deploys funds from the Star Agent's Operational Buffer into the Allocation Conduit, performing any necessary DEX exchanges. In doing so, Operational GovOps follows instructions in the Agent Artifact regarding the amount of capital to deploy and slippage tolerances. The output of this step is a fully deployed Allocation Conduit conforming to First Loss Capital and Asset Liability Management requirements.

baf25904:72fa2fa926478984cbfbaf2239de81a.title: Official Update of Artifact
baf25904:72fa2fa926478984cbfbaf2239de81a.content: If the Allocation Conduit is successfully approved, the Operational Executor Facilitator finalizes and publishes the update to the Star Agent Artifact, making it effective in the Atlas. The output of this step is an updated Star Agent Artifact with the new Allocation Conduit.

baf25904:d63145bcb849aca25f21e581a32bbb5.title: Allocation Conduit Ongoing Management
baf25904:d63145bcb849aca25f21e581a32bbb5.content: The documents herein define the process for managing an Allocation Conduit as part of the Allocation System Primitive

baf25904:ce73465ec59dc1d8e7392e94428a72d.title: Validation And Off-Chain Vote
baf25904:ce73465ec59dc1d8e7392e94428a72d.content: The Operational Executor Facilitator reviews the proposal to ensure that it is complete and aligned with the Atlas. The Operational Executor Facilitator then initiates an off-chain snapshot vote, following the quorum and majority rules in the Star Agent Artifact. When complete, the result of the vote is recorded in the Powerhouse system. The output of this step is the snapshot vote result recorded in the Powerhouse system.

baf25904:2cd05c0b304acd626a59fa5caf0d668.title: Allocation Conduit Management Periodic Data Submission And Validation
baf25904:2cd05c0b304acd626a59fa5caf0d668.content: At specified intervals, data providers submit yield, exchange rate, First Loss Capital, and Asset Liability Management data as specified in the data submission protocol for the Allocation Conduit in the Star Agent Artifact. Operational GovOps cross-checks the data submitted against on-chain and off-chain for consistency. If the Allocation Conduit is significantly underperforming or there are violations of First Loss Capital or Asset Liability Management requirements, Operational GovOps must initiate escalation steps as defined in the Star Agent Artifact.

79abe87f:ba16c51f8bd44a4af8451ff3058b6b2.title: Conduit Development And Testing
79abe87f:ba16c51f8bd44a4af8451ff3058b6b2.content: Once formally validated, the Star Agent implements the new Allocation Instance based on the specifications in the Star Agent Artifact. Operational GovOps must test the Allocation Instance with minimal funds from the Star Agent's Central Allocation Buffer, verifying deposit / withdrawal logic, slippage constraints, and oracle checks. If this testing is successful Operational GovOps confirms that the Allocation Instance satisfies all risk constraints specified in the Star Agent Artifact. The output of this step is validated contracts for the Allocation Instance and a green light to proceed with a scaled deployment.

79abe87f:2b626580c137ec4137abcc2c80f0324.title: Instance Setup Deployment
79abe87f:2b626580c137ec4137abcc2c80f0324.content: The documents herein define how the deployment of an Allocation Instance is executed on-chain.

79abe87f:54565709fb14c160f5fb754dd1dfb20.title: Initial Deployment and Required Risk Capital / Asset Liability Management Execution
79abe87f:54565709fb14c160f5fb754dd1dfb20.content: The Star Agent finalizes JRC/SRC and Asset Liability Management Arrangements. Operational GovOps records these arrangements in the Powerhouse interface. If Operational GovOps is charged with operationalizing an Instance, it deploys funds from the Star Agent's Operational Buffer into the Allocation Instance, performing any necessary DEX exchanges. See A.2.4 - Operationalization Of Allocation Instances. In doing so, Operational GovOps follows instructions in the Agent Artifact regarding the amount of capital to deploy and slippage tolerances. The output of this step is a fully deployed Allocation Instance conforming to Risk Capital and Asset Liability Management requirements.

79abe87f:b40cc4fd8b11424650795f8ebaaff15.title: Official Update of Artifact
79abe87f:b40cc4fd8b11424650795f8ebaaff15.content:
If the Allocation Instance is successfully approved, the Operational Executor Facilitator finalizes and publishes the update to the Star Agent Artifact, making it effective in the Atlas. The output of this step is an updated Star Agent Artifact with the new Allocation Instance.

Once a new Instance is deployed, its data is integrated into risk-capital monitoring systems and its RRC will be officially determined and tracked via the Sky Core RRC Dashboard/API. See A.2.4 - Sky Core Required Risk Capital (RRC) Dashboard And API. This official RRC figure supersedes the Star-prepared pro-forma RRC.

79abe87f:6da17f888020778876949c636753c28.title: Allocation Instance Ongoing Management
79abe87f:6da17f888020778876949c636753c28.content: The documents herein define the process for managing an Allocation Instance as part of the Allocation System Primitive.

79abe87f:ce73465ec59dc1d8e7392e94428a72d.title: Validation And Off-Chain Vote
79abe87f:ce73465ec59dc1d8e7392e94428a72d.content: The Operational Executor Facilitator reviews the proposal to ensure that it is complete and aligned with the Atlas. The Operational Executor Facilitator then initiates an off-chain snapshot vote, following the quorum and majority rules in the Star Agent Artifact. When complete, the result of the vote is recorded in the Powerhouse system. The output of this step is the snapshot vote result recorded in the Powerhouse system.

79abe87f:300da361c502d37b32bb56df6edeae6.title: Operationalization Of Allocation Instances
79abe87f:300da361c502d37b32bb56df6edeae6.content:
Star Agent teams may choose to directly operationalize their Allocation System Primitive Instances ("Instances") using internal, proprietary strategies that are not defined in their Artifacts. Alternatively, Star Agents may elect to have the Instances operationalized by their Operational Executor Agent. This constitutes an exception to the general rule that Operational Executor Agents operationalize all Sky Primitives on behalf of Star Agents. See A.1.14 - Agent Role Delineation.

For Star Agent teams that operationalize their Instances, they will be required to formulate KPIs for their proprietary strategies; should an Instance under-perform these KPIs, Operational GovOps is authorized to step in and operationalize the Instance(s) via a back-up strategy that is defined in the Agent Artifact. baf25904:067d02cba547300861b1aad9224e976.title: Available Total Senior Risk Capital Pool Determination
baf25904:067d02cba547300861b1aad9224e976.content: Total Senior Risk Capital (TSRC) is the amount of Senior Risk Capital that is available each Monthly Settlement Cycle for Stars to originate and thus turn into Originated Senior Risk Capital (OSRC) through the monthly origination process. TSRC is the sum of designated Internal Senior Risk Capital (ISRC) from Sky surplus buffers and available External Senior Risk Capital (ESRC) from the srUSDS contract. Prior to each monthly bidding window, the TSRC is calculated and publicly announced. Additional operational details will be defined in a future iteration of the Atlas.

baf25904:67220091402c22e606b940a3ccdcf0e.title: Process Timing And Schedule
baf25904:67220091402c22e606b940a3ccdcf0e.content: The SRC origination process operates monthly, synchronized with the Monthly Settlement Cycle. The bidding window occurs during the current month for SRC that is usable in the next month; the bidding window closes before settlement processing begins. Additional operational details, including timelines, will be specified in a future iteration of the Atlas.

baf25904:6c7b7a940e6c2dc3a6d2fd380dc92df.title: Bidding Process
baf25904:6c7b7a940e6c2dc3a6d2fd380dc92df.content: Participating Star Agents submit bids via the Powerhouse interface during the defined bidding window. Each bid must specify: (1) The quantity of SRC the Star seeks to originate, and (2) The maximum price the Star is willing to pay (expressed in basis points above the Base Rate) for using the OSRC during the upcoming monthly period. Additional operational details will be specified in a future iteration of the Atlas.

baf25904:9d35943cbfb9703fe4805115dff70f9.title: Senior Risk Capital (RSC) Origination Process
baf25904:9d35943cbfb9703fe4805115dff70f9.content: This document defines the operational details of the recurring monthly process allowing Star Agents to originate Senior Risk Capital (Originated Senior Risk Capital or OSRC) from the Total Senior Risk Capital (TSRC) pool. The process involves determining the available TSRC supply, a bidding phase, an allocation auction, and settlement aligned with the Monthly Settlement Cycle.

baf25904:006fda4c663396e006a4c60c3b502cc.title: Allocation And Clearing Price Determination
baf25904:006fda4c663396e006a4c60c3b502cc.content: Bids are ranked descending by price. TSRC is allocated sequentially to the highest bids until the pool is exhausted or all bids are filled. The price of the lowest successful bid that receives an allocation (even partial) sets the uniform clearing price for the month. All winning bidders pay this clearing price per unit of OSRC allocated, regardless of their original bid price. Additional operational details will be specified in a future iteration of the Atlas.

baf25904:492c4d1ceda482f4b375acd1b51ae04.title: srUSDS Accessibility Reward
baf25904:492c4d1ceda482f4b375acd1b51ae04.content: Star Agents and third-party partners that drive srUSDS usage are entitled to a srUSDS Accessibility Reward similar to the Accessibility Reward paid on USDS balances. The srUSDS Accessibility Reward Fee is the same as the Accessibility Reward Fee on USDS. See A.2.4 - Accessibility Reward Primitive.

baf25904:7201d95694779280efc87ed07d3684e.title: Introduction
baf25904:7201d95694779280efc87ed07d3684e.content: Spark is an Agent focused on building on USDS in the Ethereum and adjacent DeFi ecosystem. This includes driving adoption of USDS and deploying collateral backing USDS at attractive risk-adjusted returns. Spark does this through the Spark Liquidity Layer, SparkLend, and Spark Savings.- The Spark Liquidity Layer directly provides USDS, sUSDS, and USDC liquidity across networks and DeFi markets.- SparkLend is a lending market focused on USDS borrowing, sourcing liquidity directly from Sky to provide the best borrow rates for USDS.- Spark Savings enables stablecoin holders to earn the best risk-adjusted rate in DeFi, at large scale, with minimal liquidity constraints.
